Radiographic suspicion was recorded in 1,573 teeth (0.43%) across 1,509 patients, with detection rising with age. Suspected sites showed more localized periodontal bone loss than within-patient reference sites, but cemental tear was rarely documented as the initial diagnosis (17 of 1,466 tooth-level records).
why: Dentists reviewing radiographs may encounter suspected cemental tears alongside periodontal breakdown, so combining clinical and radiographic evaluation is advised before settling on a diagnosis, though the authors call for prospective validation.

headline: Podcast Offers Trade Show Strategy for Orthodontists Launching Their Own Products
summary: An Orthodontic Products podcast episode features Personify Group co-founders Mark Ross and Michael Ventriello discussing how orthodontist-inventors can get a return from trade shows. They argue exhibitors should treat shows as a way to build consideration rather than close immediate sales, and that pre-show credibility and a clear brand story matter. The episode also covers sales and marketing alignment and Personify's new trade show ROI guide and calculator.
why: For dentists or orthodontists developing their own product, the episode suggests that pre-show groundwork, such as a defined brand story and unique selling proposition, may matter more to trade show results than the booth itself.

headline: Align Technology Q3 2026 Revenue Rises 1.9% on Clear Aligner Growth
summary: Align Technology reported third-quarter 2026 total revenues of $1.015 billion, up 1.9% year over year, led by its clear aligner segment. Clear aligner revenue reached $839.3 million (up 4.2%) on 690,600 cases (up 6.6%), while imaging systems and CAD/CAM revenue fell 7.6% to $175.5 million. The company also announced that Jennifer L. Davis will succeed longtime CEO Joseph M. Hogan, effective December 31, 2026.
why: Aligner volume growth and the leadership change at a major clear aligner supplier may influence how practices think about aligner offerings, while the decline in scanner and imaging revenue is a signal about digital workflow spending.

headline: New matrix ranks precision dentistry research priorities by feasibility and importance
summary: Researchers developed a scientometric-importance-feasibility matrix and applied it to 912 precision dentistry articles published from January 2016 through October 2025. Expert clinicians rated the research hot spots using best-worst scaling, which produced 13 research clusters and a three-stage shift from phenotype correlation toward combining artificial intelligence with noninterventional techniques. Machine learning and decision support systems were placed in the top priority tier for immediate action, while foundational biological research was judged highly important but limited by clinical translation barriers.
why: It suggests where near-term efforts in precision dentistry, such as machine learning and decision support tools, are most practical, while basic biological work will need sustained funding before it reaches the clinic.

headline: Multiloop edgewise archwire shows overbite gain for anterior open bite, but evidence remains weak
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of five retrospective observational studies assessed the multiloop edgewise archwire (MEAW) technique for anterior open bite. The pooled analysis found a significant overbite increase with no significant change in mandibular plane angle, though the certainty of evidence was rated low. The authors concluded that the technique's effectiveness remains inconclusive and called for larger, higher-quality randomized controlled trials.
why: Orthodontically treating anterior open bite with MEAW may improve overbite, but the low-certainty evidence means dentists should not treat it as a proven approach without better trial data.

headline: Jennifer L Davis Named Next CEO of Align Technology
summary: Align Technology's board has picked Jennifer L Davis, formerly CEO of Procter & Gamble's global healthcare business, to succeed Joseph M Hogan as president and CEO, effective December 31, 2026. Davis joins as CEO-elect and board member on November 2, 2026, and will work with Hogan during the transition. Hogan, who has led Align since 2015, will retire from the board after a strategy meeting on June 16, 2027.
why: Leadership changes at Invisalign's parent company may shape the direction of clear aligner products, digital oral-health tools, and the doctor relationships that many practices rely on.

headline: Surface-based registration gives accurate robotic maxillofacial osteotomy in lab model
summary: Researchers compared four registration methods for a task-autonomous robot performing maxillofacial osteotomies on a model built from imaging data: splint-based landmarks, dental landmarks, dental surfaces, and bone surfaces. All four methods kept mean target-registration error under 0.8 mm, and surface-based methods (bone and dental surface) generally matched or beat landmark-based ones. Splint-based landmark registration was the fastest, and no consistent accuracy difference appeared between dental-surface and bone-surface registration.

headline: SCTG and GBR for small peri-implant buccal dehiscences: 3-year pilot results
summary: A small pilot study randomly treated small buccal bone dehiscences (3 mm or less) around single implants with either subepithelial connective tissue grafts or guided bone regeneration, comparing them with a group of five patients without dehiscences. Of the patients, 16 were available at 3 years, and both approaches kept buccal soft-tissue contours stable. Peri-implant health measures, marginal bone levels, and oral health-related quality of life stayed stable and comparable between the two groups.
why: For clinicians treating thin buccal bone around implants, this small pilot suggests both graft methods may hold up over three years, but the authors say larger randomized trials are needed before changing practice.

headline: Zirconium oxynitrate etchant boosts dentin bond strength and cuts enzyme activity after 5 years
summary: An in-vitro study tested an experimental zirconium oxynitrate etchant against standard phosphoric acid on dentin bonded with two simplified adhesives, measuring bond strength and matrix metalloproteinase activity at baseline and after simulated 5-year aging. The etchant produced higher bond strength in several groups and significantly lower collagen-degrading enzyme activity than phosphoric acid at both time points. Bond strength dropped with aging in all groups, and the best results came when the etchant was paired with a universal adhesive.
why: If these lab findings hold clinically, a zirconium-based etchant paired with a universal adhesive could help dentin bonds last longer, though it remains in-vitro evidence and not yet a proven clinical change.

headline: Piezoelectric resin composites could use chewing forces to fight bacteria and aid remineralization
summary: A critical review examines dental resin composites containing piezoelectric fillers that convert mastication-induced mechanical loading into localized electrical charges. It covers barium titanate and zinc oxide, focusing on their energy conversion, antibacterial and antibiofilm mechanisms, and support for dentin remineralization. The authors call for future studies to validate antibacterial efficacy, remineralization, and biosafety under conditions that better reflect the oral environment.

headline: Veneer-specific resin cements outperform universal cements in lab color, conversion and water tests
summary: This in vitro study compared two veneer-specific resin cements (G-CEM Veneer and RelyX Veneer) with two universal resin cements (G-CEM ONE and RelyX Universal). Researchers measured color change after immersion in distilled water, Coca-Cola, red wine, or black coffee for 1 and 7 days, plus degree of monomer conversion and water sorption and solubility. Veneer-specific cements showed higher conversion, and G-CEM Veneer had the lowest color change and water sorption/solubility, while RelyX Universal had the highest water sorption/solubility and the widest color change range.
why: For veneer and other esthetic indirect restorations, choosing a veneer-specific cement may give more stable color and better-converted material than a universal cement, though these are lab results rather than clinical outcomes.

headline: In vivo study finds apical diameter, gel concentration and nanoparticle hydrophobicity shape endodontic hydrogel release
summary: Researchers tested fibrin hydrogels used in endodontic regeneration in an in vivo model implanted in hairless mice, tracking release with live fluorescence imaging. They found that narrowing the apical opening from 2000 to 1000 µm cut apical release over the first 48 hours by 87.5-94.2%. Higher hydrogel concentration reduced the initial burst effect, and a hydrophobic nanoparticle slowed release compared with a hydrophilic one over 6 days.
why: These findings suggest that canal apical size, hydrogel formulation and carrier particle chemistry all affect how long regenerative materials stay in place, which may matter when planning regenerative endodontic procedures, though this is preclinical animal work.

headline: Bone-driven fibula reconstruction leaves limited space for implants in the posterior mandible
summary: An observational study of 19 mandibular reconstruction patients, assessed with postoperative cone beam CT, measured the bone available for implant prostheses after bone-driven fibular reconstruction. Vertical bone height fell from about 27.6 mm at the central incisor to about 16.6 mm at the second molar, and the fibula's own height averaged about 14.5 mm. The authors also simulated a double-barrel fibula technique and found it limited in the posterior region.
why: Surgeons and prosthodontists planning implant rehabilitation after fibular mandibular reconstruction should expect vertical deficiency and poor ridge alignment posteriorly, so prosthetic planning may need to favor the first molar and accept edge-to-edge anterior relationships.

headline: Osstem shares digital implant workflows at Paris seminar for French dentists
summary: A seminar in Paris, held to mark 140 years of diplomatic ties between France and South Korea, presented South Korean expertise in digital implant dentistry to French practitioners. The South Korean embassy organised the event with support from Osstem Implant's local subsidiary, and 40 local dental professionals attended. The stated aim was to strengthen clinical knowledge and professional links between the two countries.

headline: Hall Technique beats silver fluoride for treating caries in primary molars
summary: An 18-month randomised split-mouth trial compared the Hall technique and silver fluoride with conventional restorations for dentine caries in primary molars. It assessed clinical and radiographic success, treatment time and patient experience. Silver fluoride's practical advantages come with doubts about how reliably it works as a longer-term treatment.
why: For dentists treating decayed primary molars, the Hall technique appears more dependable over time than silver fluoride, which may be quicker and simpler but carries uncertainty about durability.

headline: LANAP Training Reaches 49% of Active US AAP Periodontists
summary: Millennium Dental Technologies, developer of the LANAP laser protocol and maker of the PerioLase MVP-7 laser, announced at the AAP Annual Meeting in Seattle that 49% of active US AAP members are now LANAP-trained. The company ties the milestone to the 25th anniversary of the PerioLase MVP-7 and the 10th anniversary of the protocol's FDA clearance for periodontal regeneration. The announcement is promotional in tone and comes from the manufacturer.
why: Dentists considering laser-assisted periodontal therapy as an alternative to traditional osseous surgery may see more LANAP-trained colleagues, but the claims about outcomes and regeneration come from the manufacturer and should be weighed accordingly.

headline: Self-reported gum disease linked to weaker cognition and some Alzheimer's biomarkers
summary: Using data from the nationally representative High School and Beyond (HS&B:80) cohort, researchers analyzed nearly 14,000 participants with a mean age of 58 and found 15.2% reported a history of periodontal disease. Periodontal disease was associated with lower general cognitive functioning, some domain-specific cognitive scores, and higher levels of pTau-181 and C-reactive protein. Most associations did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons, with only working memory meeting the false discovery rate threshold.
why: This cross-sectional study suggests a possible link between gum disease and cognitive health, but its associations were largely not significant after statistical correction, so it does not establish that treating periodontitis affects dementia risk.

headline: Few extensively restored teeth need root canal treatment, mostly within the first year
summary: A Swedish register-based cohort followed 271,368 teeth restored with major direct or indirect restorations in the Public Dental Service between 2014 and 2019 for up to 10 years. About 5.7% of teeth went on to endodontic treatment, often within a year of restoration, and 6.6% were extracted. Direct restorations, younger age, and posterior teeth were linked to a higher hazard of endodontic treatment.

headline: Restoring Overlooked Anterior Enamel Fractures with Universal Shade Composites
summary: The article argues that anterior enamel fractures, common traumatic injuries in general practice, are often missed or left undocumented even though they can be restored. It describes universal shade composites such as OMNICHROMA, which use light scattering rather than pigments to blend with adjacent tooth structure, reducing the need for multiple shades and layering.
why: Many patients with Ellis Class I fractures may not know a minimally invasive, aesthetic restoration is available, so routine exams that document these defects could open a conservative treatment option.

headline: Aspen Dental Offers Free Savings Plan Enrollment to Veterans in November
summary: The Aspen Group announced new initiatives to make dental care more affordable for veterans, building on a five-year, $100 million commitment to underserved patients. Veterans can enroll in the Aspen Dental Savings Plan at no cost for the first year during November, with the $49 enrollment fee waived and renewals priced at $29 after that. Aspen Dental is also expanding benefits for Veterans of Foreign Wars members through its role as the VFW's official dental provider.
why: Practices in Aspen Dental's network may see more veteran patients using the savings plan, and the plan's stated features (no waiting periods, annual maximums, or age- or preexisting-condition exclusions) describe what those patients will expect.

headline: Josh Poupore Named NYSDA Executive Director, Starting January 2027
summary: The New York State Dental Association has appointed Josh Poupore as its next executive director, effective January 1, 2027, succeeding Michael Herrmann, who retires at the end of 2026. Poupore is a former NYSDA assistant executive director and marketing and communications director (2011 to 2015) and currently runs Corning Place Communications in Albany.

headline: Colorado pediatric practice placed on probation after infection control violations
summary: The Colorado Dental Board found multiple violations at a pediatric dental practice in Pueblo, and its dentist was placed on one year of probation. An unplanned August visit found expired surface disinfection wipes, improper use of personal protective equipment, biohazard waste collection scheduled only once a year, and an expired fire extinguisher. The dentist must fix all problems within 30 days, pay for a follow-up inspection, and the team must complete OSHA compliance training; no patient harm has been reported.
why: It shows regulators will act on basic infection control and safety lapses, such as expired disinfectants, PPE technique, and waste pickup schedules, and that a designated infection control coordinator can help keep a practice compliant.

headline: Sticky Halloween candies may raise caries risk in states that favor them
summary: Americans are still spending heavily on Halloween despite high candy prices, with the National Retail Federation projecting over $4 billion in spending. An Instacart study found the most popular candy varies by state, with many states favoring sugary, sticky sweets over chocolate. The article notes that sticky candies can lodge in pits and fissures, which may lead to tooth decay.
why: Dentists in states where sticky candies are most popular may see more caries, so patients could benefit from oral hygiene advice after Halloween.

headline: Quiz on Substance Use and Dental Care Covers Oral Effects and Drug Interactions
summary: A Decisions in Dentistry quiz tests readers on dental considerations linked to substance use. It covers cannabis and dry mouth, caution with epinephrine-containing anesthetics during stimulant intoxication, and the risks of combining benzodiazepines with opioids.
why: Dentists treating patients who use cannabis, stimulants, or sedating medications may need to watch for caries and periodontal risk, cardiovascular complications with epinephrine, and sedation or overdose risk, and review medications before treatment.

headline: Rural Dental Practice Offers Financial and Lifestyle Upsides
summary: Citing 2024 ADA Health Policy Institute data, the article notes rural areas have about half the dentists per resident of urban areas (32.7 vs. 64.7 per 100,000). It reports that rural practices saw nearly a 12% revenue increase across two periods, while urban practices saw a 0.1% decline. Dentists who work in designated shortage areas may also qualify for loan repayment through federal programs offering $40,000 to $200,000.
why: Dentists considering where to practice may find rural ownership financially competitive with urban markets, and shortage-area loan repayment programs could ease student debt.

headline: Shofu Dental Launches AccuMix Capsule Mixer
summary: Shofu Dental Corporation has launched AccuMix, a compact, heavy-duty capsule mixer built for quiet, consistent operation. The device offers preset 5-, 10-, and 15-second mixing modes and is compatible with most encapsulated dental materials.
why: For practices that use encapsulated materials, AccuMix offers a small, quiet mixer with simple timing presets and easy capsule loading, which may fit busy workflows.

headline: Hummingbird Associates Releases Orthodontic Communication Playbook for 2027
summary: Practice consulting firm Hummingbird Associates is releasing a 302-page communication playbook for orthodontic teams on January 1, 2027. It covers patient communication from the first phone call through retention, with scripts in a "Say It Like This" format and a toolkit of 93 letters, emails, handouts, and forms. The playbook is available for pre-order in 2026 at $400, rising to $500 at release, and comes in print, linked PDF, and editable Word formats.
why: Orthodontic practices looking to standardize how staff talk with patients and parents about scheduling, finances, and other sensitive topics may find this resource useful, though its value depends on whether it fits the practice's needs and budget.

headline: Research should weigh environmental impact alongside oral health gains
summary: A J Am Dent Assoc article synthesizes literature on implementation research, health systems research, and sustainable practices in oral health care. It identifies three areas: implementation research that improves population oral health with less environmental impact, research agendas viewed through an environmental lens, and research processes designed to cut waste. The authors also propose that funders require environmental impact statements in research proposals, similar to public health impact statements in journals.
why: It suggests prevention can serve both patient health and sustainability, since good oral health cuts travel, resource-heavy treatment, and material waste, which may shape how dental research and practice are planned.

headline: Guidance on building an eco-friendly, resilient dental practice
summary: A Journal of the American Dental Association article reviews how dental offices can become more sustainable and resilient through green design, retrofits, and operational changes. It covers emergency preparedness, prevention-focused care, digital workflows, teledentistry, waste management, and risk-based recall intervals. The authors report that meaningful sustainability gains appear achievable without large cost premiums, based on analysis of LEED certification categories.
why: Practices weighing new construction or renovation can use this framework to reduce resource use and waste, improve indoor air, lighting, and acoustics, and potentially support staff well-being and long-term viability.

headline: Narrative review finds biophotonics supported for only three oral disease uses
summary: This narrative review assessed light-based (biophotonic) methods for diagnosing and treating oral disease across caries, periodontal and peri-implant disease, oral potentially malignant disorders, oral cancer, and endodontics. The evidence was mixed: quantitative light-induced fluorescence showed good accuracy for occlusal caries, while a Cochrane review found high sensitivity but lower specificity for oral cancer and potentially malignant disorders. Only photobiomodulation for oral mucositis prevention, photodynamic therapy for oral leukoplakia, and fluorescence-based caries detection were judged supported for clinical use.
why: Dentists should treat most biophotonic devices as investigational outside caries detection, and should weigh regulatory clearance and marketing claims against actual clinical evidence before adopting them.

headline: AI adoption in dentistry is uneven; sustainability barriers identified
summary: A JADA article reviews dental and medical studies on artificial intelligence and how it can be sustained across the profession's fragmented ecosystem. It identifies barriers including siloed innovation, ethical uncertainty, and unequal infrastructure. The authors call for cohesive stakeholder engagement, curriculum and ethical frameworks, regulatory initiatives, and strategic steps that use the profession's diversity to support sustainability.
why: Dentists may see AI tools adopted unevenly across practices, so decisions about integration may depend on infrastructure, training, and clear ethical and regulatory guidance.

headline: Framework proposes adding planetary health to oral health guideline development
summary: The authors adapted the GRADE Guidance 46 approach for oral health so that environmental effects, such as those linked to climate change, pollution, and biodiversity loss, can be weighed in clinical and public health guidelines. The framework adds a planetary boundaries criterion and a planetary health subjudgment within the existing equity criterion. The excerpt suggests life cycle assessments could inform decisions on visit frequency, single-use versus reusable instruments, and reprocessing and procurement.
why: Future guidelines may ask dentists to consider environmental impact alongside infection control, effectiveness, safety, and equity when choosing care pathways and supplies.

headline: Dental manufacturers urged to adopt sustainability initiatives and ESG principles
summary: A J Am Dent Assoc article argues that sustainability is becoming a central concern in dentistry and that dental manufacturers and suppliers should embrace environmental, social, and governance principles. The authors propose seven initiatives, including reducing packaging and waste, refurbishment programs, going paperless, digital labeling, working with regulators to limit product registration requirements, developing products that prevent oral disease, and minimizing hazardous waste.
why: Suppliers that adopt these practices may offer more sustainable products and services to practices, and younger dentists in particular are pushing for this focus, so it may shape purchasing choices over time.

headline: WHO position article links oral health to environmental sustainability and climate resilience
summary: A position article in the Journal of the American Dental Association sets out how the World Health Organization wants oral health placed within global environmental and public health agendas. It reviews WHO frameworks, including the Global Strategy and Action Plan on Oral Health 2023-2030, and WHO efforts to phase out dental amalgam and promote less invasive caries prevention and management. The article urges the oral health community to adopt prevention-focused, sustainable, and climate-resilient approaches.
why: Dental practices may see growing emphasis on mercury-free materials, less invasive caries care, and sustainability measures as part of global health policy.

headline: Contralateral lymph node drainage found in 40% of early lateralised oral cancers
summary: A single-centre retrospective study of 64 patients with early lateralised oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma who had sentinel node biopsy and wide local excision between 2016 and 2022. Contralateral or bilateral drainage occurred in 40.6% of cases, but contralateral metastases were found in only three patients (4.7%). The authors suggest sentinel node biopsy may refine staging by identifying contralateral drainage that ipsilateral elective neck dissection would miss.
why: Contralateral drainage is common in early tongue and oral cancers, so sentinel node biopsy may help clinicians decide on neck management that a standard ipsilateral dissection would not cover, though the authors call for prospective multicentre studies first.

headline: Review weighs management options for separated endodontic instruments
summary: This narrative review compared nonsurgical retrieval, bypass, retention, and surgical management of separated endodontic instruments, focusing on residual dentin, fracture resistance, healing, and tooth retention. It found that aggressive retrieval can remove substantial dentin, and that clinical evidence is mostly observational. No strategy was shown to be superior for long-term tooth survival in controlled comparative studies.

headline: Arginine added to restorative dental materials shows antimicrobial promise in lab studies
summary: A scoping review of 17 in vitro studies mapped how arginine has been incorporated into restorative materials, mainly orthodontic cements, adhesive systems, and resin-modified glass ionomers. Direct mixing of L-arginine powder was the most common method, and studies that tested antimicrobial effects reported favorable results, including on bacterial growth, adhesion, biofilm behavior, and pH. Mechanical effects depended on concentration, with some improvements and some reductions, though several studies found a concentration that kept properties close to the unmodified control.
why: Arginine may eventually give restorative materials added antibiofilm function without clearly compromising mechanical performance, but the evidence is laboratory-only and heterogeneous, so it has no direct clinical application yet.

headline: Income gaps in childhood caries persist across levels of municipal oral care coverage
summary: This cross-sectional Brazilian study analyzed 7,185 five-year-olds from the 2023 National Oral Health Survey, linked to monthly municipal oral healthcare coverage from 2019 to 2021. Coverage was grouped into four trajectories, and income-related inequalities in dmft and pufa scores were measured. Income gaps in dmft did not vary by trajectory, while pufa gaps were larger in medium-high coverage municipalities than in always-low ones.
why: Expanding dental service coverage alone may not close socioeconomic gaps in young children's caries, so practices and policymakers may need to address broader social factors as well.

headline: Low-profile EMI attachments lose retention faster than Locator in implant overdentures
summary: A crossover clinical trial with 20 edentulous participants compared an EMI low-profile attachment system with a conventional Locator system in conventional and 3D-printed implant-retained mandibular overdentures over 9 months. Both systems lost retention over time, but the EMI attachments started with higher retention, declined sharply, and showed more component wear and more frequent replacement needs. Locator retention remained more stable, and its patient satisfaction scores did not change significantly over time.
why: When choosing attachments for implant overdentures, the EMI system may require more frequent component checks or replacements than Locator, which bears on maintenance planning and long-term patient satisfaction.

headline: Digitally guided workflow preserves occlusal plane in Jaw-in-a-Day maxillary reconstruction
summary: This clinical report describes a digitally guided, prosthesis-centered approach to immediate implant-supported rehabilitation after subtotal maxillectomy. A 69-year-old woman with adenoid cystic carcinoma and failing implant prostheses received a fibula free flap using a Jaw-in-a-Day approach, with virtual planning used to orient the reconstructed maxilla relative to stable craniofacial landmarks. An interim prosthesis was used to set the occlusal scheme, verify vertical dimension, and guide graft positioning, and occlusion was reported as stable at 24 months.
why: It shows how a prosthesis-first, landmark-based occlusal plan may help dentists and prosthodontists restore function when no natural dentoalveolar references remain, though this is a single case report.

source: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol
headline: Bone collagen aids bone regeneration after jaw cyst enucleation
summary: A prospective nonrandomized controlled study of 50 patients with jaw cysts compared bone collagen implantation with an absorbable gelatin sponge after cyst enucleation. Cone-beam CT at 3 and 6 months showed higher bone density and greater cyst volume reduction in the bone collagen group. That group also had fewer postoperative complications.

source: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol
headline: Qualitative study examines how clinicians decide on temporomandibular disorder management
summary: Researchers interviewed 12 oral medicine or oral and maxillofacial surgery providers about how they manage temporomandibular disorders (TMD). Thematic analysis of the transcripts produced five themes, covering perceptions, TMD-specific challenges, general management approach, factors shaping decisions, and barriers and facilitators of good outcomes. The authors describe TMD care as complex, with limited strong evidence on management strategies, and note that education and conservative care remain central.
why: It highlights that patient preferences, circumstances, and each clinician's own specialty and experience shape TMD treatment choices, and that the evidence base for those choices is thin.

headline: Graft voids after sinus lift linked to more implant failures in retrospective study
summary: In a retrospective review of 307 patients who had lateral sinus floor elevation between 2018 and 2023, voids in the graft were seen on 6-month CBCT scans in 31.3% of cases. Specific graft material, greater graft volume, and a smaller sinus mucosa tension angle were independently associated with voids. Over a mean follow-up of about 46.6 months, implants in sites with voids failed more often (7.3% vs. 1.9%) and had lower cumulative survival.
why: Radiographic voids in grafted sinuses may signal a higher risk of implant failure, so graft material choice, graft volume, and post-op CBCT review deserve attention when planning sinus augmentation.

headline: Systematic review finds no proven way to preserve resin bonds to eroded dentin
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis pooled preclinical studies on resin bonding to dentin damaged by erosion, searched through August 2026, and kept 58 primary reports from 1,163 records. Chlorhexidine applied at the interface showed numerically lower bond strength than controls at 12-18 months, though not significantly so. Favorable long-term results for DMSO, hydrophobic coatings, and some collagen biomodifiers came mainly from single studies or one shared cohort.

headline: Opioid exposure after adolescent third molar surgery viewed through a neurodevelopmental lens
summary: This perspective article reviews epidemiologic findings on persistent opioid use after third molar extraction in adolescents and considers how adolescent brain development may relate to it. Retrospective cohort studies cited report higher adjusted odds of persistent opioid use among some opioid-naive adolescents who received dental opioid prescriptions, though the absolute risk is low. The author notes that current evidence does not establish that short-course postoperative prescribing causes addiction.

headline: AI jaw-motion simulation shows smaller contact footprint in digital restoration planning
summary: An exploratory within-case study of 14 paired intraoral scan datasets compared three digital workflows for monolithic restorations, measuring the share of software-rendered contact and penetration area. The AI jaw-motion file-driven simulation produced the lowest median contact area fraction (2.19%), lower than both the axiography-programmed and the average-value chairside reference workflows. The authors describe this as geometric compatibility with recorded morphology, not validated patient-specific movement accuracy.
why: For dentists planning monolithic restorations digitally, AI-driven jaw-motion simulation may help complement virtual occlusal assessment, though the small, unvalidated study does not establish that it improves clinical outcomes.

headline: Genetic study links oral and gastrointestinal diseases through immune pathways
summary: A large-scale genetic study from Wuhan, China, examined whether common oral and gastrointestinal diseases share genetic susceptibility. The researchers identified immune-related pathways as potential connections between oral and gut health. The results also add evidence of a possible causal relationship between periodontitis and inflammatory bowel disease.
why: It supports the idea that periodontal disease and gut conditions may be linked biologically, which may matter when dentists consider patients' broader health, though the findings remain associative and do not establish treatment changes.

headline: Registration open for 2027 Chicago Dental Society Midwinter Meeting
summary: Registration has opened for the Chicago Dental Society Midwinter Meeting, which returns to the McCormick Place West Building in Chicago from 25 to 27 February 2027. The meeting will offer an expanded scientific program and a new Midwinter Meeting Digital Pass giving access to recorded educational sessions.
why: Dentists who want to attend in person or remotely can now sign up for the 2027 meeting, and the digital pass offers a way to access continuing education sessions without traveling to Chicago.

headline: AI score from intraoral scans may objectively assess peri-implant mucosal erythema
summary: Researchers developed an AI-driven Digital Erythema Score (DES) that uses intraoral scan data to grade redness of peri-implant mucosa without invasive probing. A U-Net model segmented the mucosal margins and a YOLO model localized erythema regions, with diagnostic accuracy reported as good on both an internal dataset of 200 patients and an external set of 23 patients. The score also correlated with bleeding on probing, and it improved the diagnostic performance and consistency of observers with different experience levels in the external validation.
why: This preliminary study suggests intraoral scan-based AI could make peri-implant inflammation assessment more objective and support future remote or home-based monitoring, though it still needs validation with patient-accessible imaging devices before clinical use.

headline: Scan body type and AI tools affect accuracy of full-arch implant intraoral scans
summary: This comparative clinical study tested how accurately an intraoral scanner captured a complete maxillary arch with four implants, using non-splinting and non-calibrated implant scan bodies made of PEEK or titanium. Scans were taken with two scanning patterns, with and without the scanner's integrated AI-based tool, and were compared against a reference cast digitized by a laboratory scanner. Non-calibrated techniques showed better linear trueness and better angular trueness and precision than non-splinting methods, and titanium scan bodies in the non-splinting group outperformed PEEK ones; the scanning pattern did not affect accuracy.

headline: Millennium Dental Technologies and IALD Mourn Periodontist Raymond A. Yukna
summary: Millennium Dental Technologies and the Institute for Advanced Laser Dentistry announced the death of Professor Raymond A. Yukna, DMD, MS, a periodontist and educator. The tribute describes him as a respected researcher and clinician whose work shaped modern periodontal therapy and his role in early research supporting the LANAP® laser protocol.
why: Yukna's research and teaching influenced periodontal care and laser-assisted periodontal treatment, so his passing marks a loss for the specialty and for clinicians who trained under or learned from his work.

headline: BioHorizons Launches Metal-Free CERALOG Ceramic Implants in the U.S.
summary: BioHorizons has brought its CERALOG PROGRESSIVE-LINE ceramic implant system to the U.S. market as a fully metal-free option. The system includes a ceramic implant, zirconia/PEEK restorative components, and a metal-free screw, with a two-piece restorative design and a bolt-in-tube implant-abutment connection. The implant was originally developed by partner company Camlog and features a tapered thread design and dedicated surgical instruments.
why: Dentists treating patients who need a non-titanium option now have another metal-free implant system available in the U.S., with more restorative choices than one-piece ceramic designs offer.

headline: Charles A. Crago Takes Office as 2026-27 AAOMS President
summary: Charles A. Crago, DMD, MD, FACS, was introduced as president of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons for 2026-27 at the association's annual meeting in Seattle in September. The AAOMS represents more than 9,000 oral and maxillofacial surgeons. Crago succeeds Robert S. Clark, DMD, who becomes immediate past president, and he joins Debra M. Sacco, DMD, MD, as president-elect.
why: Leadership changes at AAOMS shape policy and advocacy for oral and maxillofacial surgeons, and this one comes from a long-serving leader with prior service as vice president, trustee, and state society president.

headline: Dentira Launches Dental Spend Index Benchmarking DSO Supply Costs
summary: Dentira, a procurement platform for dental groups, released its first Dental Spend Index, a semiannual benchmark built on live procurement data from 267 U.S. DSOs covering about 15,000 locations. The index reports supply spend, formulary compliance, and supplier strategy at segment and category levels, without disclosing individual pricing. The Fall 2026 findings show larger groups spend a smaller share of collections on supplies, supply prices rose across top categories since 2021, and about half of ordered products fall outside formulary.
why: DSO leaders and their financial backers can compare their supply spending, formulary use, and cost trends against peers while setting FY27 budgets.

headline: Social media habits linked to ethical sensitivity and educational use in dental students
summary: An online survey of preclinical and clinical dental students and young graduates at one Turkish institution and its alumni network examined how social media use relates to ethical sensitivity, interaction, attitudes, and educational use. Graduates scored lower on clinical data sharing and ethical sensitivity than students, while female participants reported more positive attitudes and greater educational use. Higher social media use was generally tied to more positive perceptions and more educational use, though the relationship with ethical sensitivity did not follow a straight line.
why: Dental educators and practice leaders may want to consider how students and new graduates use social media, especially around sharing clinical information and professional ethics.

headline: Angelalign Launches SuperElastic Aligner Material for Complex Cases
summary: Angelalign Technology has introduced SuperElastic (MC-SE), a proprietary clear aligner material aimed at complex orthodontic cases. The company says it took seven years of research and is designed to deliver continuous, biologically safe force with a larger elastic working range and greater strength. Unlike the firm's earlier PETG-based multi-layer aligners, MC-SE adds a medical-grade polyamide layer.
why: If you use clear aligners for complicated movements, this new material may offer more predictable force delivery, though the excerpt provides only company-reported test results and no clinical outcome data.

headline: Angelalign Unveils SuperElastic (MC-SE*) Clear Aligner Material
summary: Angelalign Technology has introduced SuperElastic (MC-SE*), a new proprietary clear aligner material it says is a major performance step up from its current material. The company says the material offers steady force at biologically safe levels, a wider elastic working range, and added strength and toughness, aimed at complex orthodontic cases. It will be sold globally once the required regulatory registrations are received.

headline: Saliva biomarkers may help flag active periodontitis and track treatment response
summary: A systematic review of 11 studies examined salivary biomarkers in systemically healthy people with periodontitis, looking at links to disease severity and changes after nonsurgical periodontal therapy. Inflammatory markers such as interleukin 1β and tumor necrosis factor-α were tied to active disease and fell after treatment, oxidative stress markers were elevated, and matrix metalloproteinase-8 consistently reflected periodontal breakdown and responded to therapy. Sample sizes and outcome reporting varied across the included studies.
why: Noninvasive saliva tests could eventually help dentists judge current disease activity and monitor response to periodontal treatment, but the authors say standardized longitudinal validation is needed before routine use.

headline: Platelet concentrates may lower palatal fistula risk in cleft repair, but evidence is weak
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of five randomized trials, covering 168 non-syndromic patients, examined autologous platelet concentrates (APCs) during primary cleft palate repair. Patients given APCs had a significantly lower likelihood of developing a palatal fistula than controls. The authors judged the certainty of the evidence to be very low and said more trials are needed before clinical recommendations can be made.

headline: Sagittal split osteotomy yields more bone contact than anterior oblique osteotomy in mandibular advancement
summary: A double-blind randomized clinical trial at one center compared sagittal split osteotomy (SSO) with anterior oblique osteotomy (AOO) in 52 skeletal class II patients, covering 104 osteotomies. SSO produced significantly greater bone contact area between segments, while advancement magnitude and execution time were similar. Lingual split patterns also differed significantly between the two techniques, with SSO showing mostly LSS3 fractures and AOO mostly LSS1.
why: For dentists involved in orthognathic planning, the trial suggests SSO may offer better bone contact for large mandibular advancements, though the authors note neither technique was absolutely superior.

headline: Global TMJ replacement device market has grown to 40 systems across 20 countries
summary: An updated review of alloplastic temporomandibular joint replacement (TMJR) systems identified 40 devices available worldwide as of 2025, up from 27 in a 2019 review. Titanium alloys and ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene, often backed by titanium alloy, remain the most common materials, while custom and 3D-printed devices now dominate the market. The authors found peer-reviewed preclinical and clinical data to be inconsistent and regulatory approval to vary widely, often limited to the country of origin.
why: Dentists and oral surgeons referring for TMJ replacement have more device options, but the uneven evidence and approval status mean careful comparison is needed before choosing a system.

headline: AI soft tissue prediction for orthognathic virtual planning is promising but early-stage
summary: A scoping review of six studies examined artificial intelligence models that predict facial soft tissue changes within virtual surgical planning for orthognathic surgery. All six used deep learning on point cloud or surface mesh data from CT, CBCT, and/or 3D surface scans. Geometric accuracy was often within clinically accepted limits of 2-3 mm, though accuracy was consistently lower in dynamic regions.
why: AI soft tissue prediction may eventually help dentists and surgeons plan jaw surgery outcomes, but the review found no adequate evaluation of patient-reported outcomes, clinician usability, or full workflow integration, so it is not ready for routine clinical use.

headline: Root resection failure risk similar for endodontic and periodontal molar indications
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of root resection in permanent molars found no statistically significant difference in failure risk between teeth treated for endodontic reasons and those treated for periodontal reasons. Five comparative studies were pooled, with a crude pooled failure risk ratio of 0.82 that crossed 1, and the authors judged the estimate fragile because follow-up periods varied widely. Overall certainty of evidence was rated very low.
why: For molars where retreatment or apical surgery is not feasible or furcation disease is severe, root resection appears to have a comparable failure risk regardless of indication, but the very low certainty means clinicians should weigh this cautiously against individual case factors.

headline: Intraosseous anesthesia beats nerve block for pulpitis molars in pooled trials
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of five randomized trials with 265 participants compared primary intraosseous anesthesia with inferior alveolar nerve block in mandibular teeth with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis. Anesthetic failure occurred in 27 participants given intraosseous anesthesia versus 65 given the nerve block, a pooled risk ratio of 0.46. The authors caution that the evidence base is small, has methodological concerns, and varies in agents and delivery systems.
why: For patients with irreversible pulpitis in lower teeth, intraosseous anesthesia may give more reliable numbness than a standard nerve block, but the small, heterogeneous evidence means it should be viewed as promising rather than settled.

headline: Digital workflow used to restore failed incisor with cantilever resin-bonded bridge
summary: A case report in the Journal of Prosthetic Dentistry describes a digital workflow for replacing a failed maxillary incisor with a resin-bonded fixed prosthesis in two patients, both with incisor root fractures. A digitally designed cantilever interim restoration was placed first, with the pontic sites gingivally contoured, and the definitive prostheses then copied that gingival form. The authors report that the digital approach offered significant advantages in predictability and consistency of pink and white esthetics compared with conventional techniques.

headline: 3D-printed interim resin full-arch prostheses show frequent fractures despite high early implant survival
summary: A retrospective multicenter study of 63 patients (77 arches, 320 implants) at four centers examined immediately loaded full-arch implant prostheses made from 3D-printed interim resin. Fifteen of 77 prostheses (19.5%) had at least one framework fracture, with recurrence in 13 arches after reprinting from the original files, and 3 of 320 implants failed (99.06% early survival over 6 months). Male sex was associated with a higher fracture rate, which the authors describe as exploratory.
why: Digital, printed interim full-arch prostheses may offer a streamlined workflow with early implant survival, but the fracture rate and recurrence after reprinting suggest that the design should be structurally checked before remaking them for patients.

headline: HeyGears to present dental 3D-printing workflows at Formnext 2026
summary: HeyGears will exhibit its newest digital dental production technologies at Formnext 2026 in Frankfurt am Main, held 17 to 20 November. The company plans to show automated multi-application production, dual-material denture printing, and high-transparency printing workflows. Its focus is on how connected digital tools can help labs and clinics achieve more integrated, efficient and scalable manufacturing.
why: Dental labs and clinics considering digital denture or appliance printing may find these workflow demonstrations useful when evaluating future production options.

headline: Practical review outlines safety framework for pain and medication in office-based dental anesthesia
summary: A review in Current Pain and Headache Reports examines perioperative pain assessment, medication documentation, local anesthetic toxicity preparedness, emergency medications, and discharge readiness in office-based dental practices. It aims to give providers an overview of what to incorporate into dental and similar anesthesia practices. The authors frame age-appropriate pain assessment, local-anesthetic safety, emergency preparedness, and recovery criteria as key components, and suggest a practical framework to help clinicians apply these safeguards consistently.
why: It offers a checklist-style reference for dentists who provide sedation or general anesthesia in the office, covering pain assessment, drug documentation, emergency readiness, and discharge criteria.

headline: UK report proposes five-year plan to rebuild dental clinical research workforce
summary: A Dental Schools Council report says the UK's clinical dental research workforce has shrunk substantially over the past two decades. The report lays out a five-year strategy to rebuild research capacity, improve career pathways, and bring more primary care dentists and dental care professionals into research.
why: A shrinking research workforce could limit the evidence base for oral health care and the training of future dentists, while clearer research career routes may open opportunities for practising dentists and dental care professionals to get involved.

headline: Dr. Silverman: A simple patient conversation can open cosmetic treatment opportunities
summary: In his weekly reflection, cosmetic dentist Harvey Silverman argues that practice growth can start with a single conversation rather than new technology, procedures, or marketing. He describes patients who did not realize they were candidates for cosmetic work, or who assumed it would be too invasive or too expensive, and says that discussion can shift their outlook.
why: Taking time to talk with patients about cosmetic options may uncover interest from people who have assumed treatment is out of reach, which can matter for case acceptance and practice growth.

headline: Dentsply Sirona's Primescan 2 Cart Receives 2026 Red Dot Product Design Award
summary: Dentsply Sirona announced that its Primescan 2 Cart has won the 2026 Red Dot Award in Product Design, an international design competition judged by independent experts. The company says the honor recognizes the device's combination of functionality, usability, and design. The cart features a compact, mobile, ergonomic build, optimized dimensions for access during scanning, a surface that supports efficient disinfection, and an integrated display meant to help patients understand their scan results.

headline: Align Technology Opens Applications for 2027 Research Award Program
summary: Align Technology has opened applications for its 2027 Annual Research Award Program, which will give up to $300,000 to university faculty for orthodontic and dental research. Since launching in 2010, the program has funded about $4.16 million in research. Awards are offered in several regions, starting with the Americas.
why: Dental faculty researchers may find new funding for clinical and evidence-based studies, and the program signals continued industry support for academic orthodontic research.

headline: Parkview Dental Partners Names Jon Gregoire Chief Executive Officer
summary: Parkview Dental Partners, a dental service organization backed by Cathay Capital, has appointed Jon Gregoire as its CEO. Gregoire has more than 20 years of DSO leadership experience, including co-founding Cornerstone Dental Partners and later serving as COO of P1 Dental Partners. He has been involved in more than 30 dental acquisitions.
why: A leadership change at a large DSO with an acquisition-focused executive signals continued consolidation and growth in the DSO sector, which may affect partner practices and the job market for dentists.

headline: FDA Grants Breakthrough Designation to OraLiva's Investigational Oral Cancer Test
summary: OraLiva announced that the FDA has granted Breakthrough Device Designation to ORAL ONC-InCYT, an investigational brush-based cytology test for suspicious white or red oral lesions. The test analyzes lesion cell morphology and biomarker-related features to produce a quantitative Oral Cancer Numerical Index meant to be read alongside a clinician's overall evaluation. The designation covers adults with lesions suspected to be oral potentially malignant disorders or oral lichenoid conditions.
why: If cleared, a objective cytology index could help dentists decide when to refer, biopsy, or escalate care for lesions that are often monitored for months, though the test is still investigational.

headline: Align Technology Opens Applications for 2027 Research Award Program
summary: Align Technology has opened its 2027 Annual Research Award Program, offering up to $300,000 to university faculty for orthodontic and dental research. Awards of up to US$25,000 each, four per region for one year, are available in the Americas, EMEA and APAC, open to faculty at universities where Invisalign or the iTero scanner is available. Applications are due by 5:00 pm Pacific Time on March 5, 2027, and an independent academic committee reviews them before Align makes final selections.
why: Dental faculty at eligible universities can apply for funding to pursue clinical research, which may strengthen the evidence base for orthodontic and general dental care.

headline: Henry Schein posts Q3 2026 sales growth and raises full-year EPS guidance
summary: Henry Schein reported $3.5 billion in third-quarter 2026 sales, up 4.0% overall and 3.1% on an internal basis in local currencies. US dental merchandise sales rose 8.6%, which the company attributed mainly to volume from market share gains, and it raised its 2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance to $5.50 to $5.56. The company also repurchased about 1.4 million shares for $125 million during the quarter.
why: Strong US dental distribution demand and a higher earnings outlook from a major supplier suggest healthy purchasing conditions in the dental supply market, though part of the guidance lift reflects one-time tariff refund benefits.

headline: Robotics in orthognathic surgery: scoping review finds mostly preclinical evidence
summary: A scoping review of 35 publications mapped robotic applications in orthognathic surgery, searching Embase, Web of Science, MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Library through 28 May 2026. Most studies used phantom, cadaver, or animal models, and clinical work was limited to early feasibility evaluations. Robots have moved from passive measurement and positioning toward systems that support navigation, bone repositioning, and controlled osteotomies, with the most consistent gains in geometric accuracy for maxillary positioning and linear cuts under surgeon supervision.
why: Robotic systems may offer a task-specific aid for accuracy in orthognathic cases, but the authors found no evidence yet that they should replace established digital workflows, and small cohorts and missing long-term data limit clinical use.

headline: CT-guided pathway for high-risk lower third molars shows low nerve injury rates
summary: A prospective cohort study from Amstelland Hospital in the Netherlands (2019-2025) compared coronectomy with complete removal of high-risk mandibular third molars, using CT assessment to guide treatment. Among 2,450 molars in 1,727 patients, inferior alveolar nerve hypoesthesia occurred in 1.2%, and most cases resolved. Molars where coronectomy was converted to complete removal during surgery had a much higher rate of nerve injury than planned removals.
why: It supports CT-based risk stratification before third molar surgery and suggests that intraoperative conversion of a planned coronectomy may signal higher nerve injury risk that clinicians should anticipate.

headline: Pentoxifylline-tocopherol-clodronate for jaw osteoradionecrosis: pooled healing data, no controls
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of six observational studies (303 total subjects, 192 treated with PENTOCLO) pooled time-to-event data to estimate mucosal healing in head and neck cancer-related osteoradionecrosis. The pooled median time to complete mucosal healing was 9.0 months, and the unhealed proportion fell from 70.7% at 6 months to 6.3% at 36 months. The reviewers rated risk of bias as serious to critical and found no untreated control groups.

headline: Scoping review maps large language model use in endodontics and its limits
summary: A scoping review of 50 studies from January 2023 to November 2025 mapped how large language model-based generative AI is used in endodontics across education, diagnosis and clinical support, and patient communication. GPT-series models accessed through ChatGPT were the most often evaluated. Performance was strong on structured multiple-choice questions but weaker on open-ended and case-based tasks, and diagnostic results were inconsistent and still below expert level.
why: Dentists considering AI tools for endodontic decision support or patient education should know that accuracy varies by task, and the authors call for standardized, prospectively validated evaluation before clinical use.

headline: Single RMS values may miss complex distortion in intraoral scans of edentulous implant arches
summary: This in vitro study compared three intraoral scanners and their recommended scan patterns on a five-implant edentulous mandible model, using a reference laboratory scan. It used an enhanced metrology method measuring linear, angular, and distance distortions, alongside the conventional best-fit alignment and RMS error approach. The authors argue that reporting one RMS value alone cannot capture the complex three-dimensional distortions that occur.
why: Dentists relying on a single accuracy figure for scanners may overlook arch-level distortions that matter for implant-supported prostheses, so scanner choice and scan technique deserve closer evaluation.

headline: Zirconia-resin interpenetrating composites: ceramic content tunes strength and antibacterial effect
summary: Researchers built zirconia scaffolds with 50% to 80% ceramic volume fractions using nanoparticle jetting, then infiltrated them with a UDMA/TEGDMA resin containing silver-loaded sodium zirconium phosphate. Stiffness and flexural strength rose with more ceramic, fracture toughness peaked at 70%, and antibacterial activity fell as ceramic content increased. Wear behavior stayed relatively stable across all four compositions, with low material wear and limited enamel wear on the opposing tooth.
why: This suggests the ceramic-to-resin ratio could be adjusted to balance strength, enamel compatibility, and antibacterial function in future restorative materials, though the findings are from laboratory testing only.

headline: Review finds restorative materials affect gum soft-tissue attachment, with inconsistent in-vitro methods
summary: This narrative review pooled 20 in-vitro studies examining how restorative materials placed near gum tissue influence cells involved in soft-tissue attachment. Fibroblasts were studied most often, and the studies varied widely in specimen design, surface treatment, cell type, and assays, which makes direct comparison difficult. Surface polishing, preventing the oxygen-inhibited layer, and coating with bioactive resin were linked to better cell attachment, while changes to filler, degree of conversion, or alumina blasting were not consistently helpful; some materials were limited by cytotoxicity.
why: For subgingival restorations, surface finish and resin handling may influence how well gum tissue attaches, but the evidence is too inconsistent to pick a best material yet.

headline: Review maps salivary biosensors for oral disease peptide and protein markers
summary: This narrative review surveys salivary biosensors that detect peptide and protein biomarkers linked to oral diseases, sorting the work into four domains by what each approach physically measures. It proposes an analytical framework explaining why these strategies face different hurdles on the way to clinical use. The authors conclude that protein-targeted platforms are the most mature, with detection limits already below clinically relevant levels, but that reference standards and diagnostic metrics are often unreported.
why: For dentists, salivary chairside tests are moving closer to practice, but their readiness depends on fixed case definitions, testing in unprocessed patient saliva, and comparison with existing point-of-care tests rather than sensitivity alone.

headline: Thiourethane oligomers and silanized TiO2 nanostructures tested in experimental composites
summary: Researchers tested experimental resin composites combining thiourethane oligomers (TU-Oli) with silanized titanium dioxide nanotubes or nanoparticles at low concentrations. TU-Oli increased degree of conversion and slowed polymerization rate, while 0.3 wt% TiO2 gave better depth of cure and light transmission than 0.9 wt%. Nanotube-containing composites had lower glass transition temperature, while flexural strength and polymerization stress were similar across groups.

headline: Randomised trial compares BioFlx resin crowns with stainless steel and zirconia
summary: An Indian randomised controlled trial compared stainless steel, zirconia and BioFlx crowns on primary molars, assessing clinical performance and parental satisfaction. BioFlx is marketed as a tooth-coloured option that needs less tooth preparation than zirconia, but its clinical record is less established. The authors suggest that the choice of material involves different clinical trade-offs.
why: For pediatric crown decisions, parents may favour tooth-coloured options like BioFlx, but this study indicates clinicians need to weigh performance differences against aesthetics and preparation needs.

headline: AI in Dental Research: Weighing Productivity Gains Against Research Integrity
summary: A Journal of Dental Research article examines how AI, including large language models and agentic pipelines, is changing knowledge production in oral health research. It weighs faster literature synthesis, data analysis and manuscript drafting against risks such as fabricated findings and citations, overconfident inference and narrowing of research focus. The authors identify three structural asymmetries and call for enforceable governance, including mandatory AI disclosure, provenance tracking, adversarial testing of tools and institutional reform.
why: Dentists who read or rely on published research should expect more AI-assisted papers, so critical appraisal and attention to disclosure and verification of citations will matter more.

headline: Proanthocyanidin acidic primers improve dentin-resin bond strength and durability in lab study
summary: Researchers tested four proanthocyanidin (PAC) preparations formulated as glycolic acid-based primers in a simplified 2-step prime-and-rinse adhesive protocol. Across timepoints up to one year, PAC-treated groups showed significantly higher microtensile bond strength than the control, and reduced dye infiltration at the hybrid layer and underlying dentin. The trimeric C. verum-AA formulation produced the highest and most stable viscoelastic effects on the hybrid layer and underlying dentin.

headline: Maternal periodontitis in mice linked to offspring gut and brain changes
summary: In a mouse study, periodontitis was induced in parous females by ligatures around the maxillary second molars for four weeks before breeding. Maternal periodontitis reduced oral microbial diversity and altered the maternal gut microbiome, and offspring showed reduced gut microbial diversity, impaired social interaction, reduced spontaneous locomotion, astrocyte increases in the cerebellum and frontal cortex, and disrupted Purkinje cell synchrony.

headline: Periodontitis linked to more non-VGS bloodstream infections after stem cell transplant
summary: A retrospective and prospective cohort study from Princess Margaret Cancer Centre examined how periodontitis affects bloodstream infections in allogeneic stem cell transplant recipients. Patients with periodontitis had a higher share of non-viridans group streptococci infections in the retrospective cohort, a similar but nonsignificant trend in the prospective cohort, and a higher mortality risk, with elevated VGS-specific antibody levels also observed.

headline: New framework models oral pH dynamics and introduces GatorpH web tool for caries parameters
summary: Researchers describe a quantitative framework using nonlinear mixed effects and fixed effects modeling to estimate caries-related plaque pH parameters from sparse sampling data. They report that sparse datasets, common in clinical studies using the indirect or strip method, can underestimate parameters tied to caries risk. The team also released a publicly available web interface, GatorpH, that applies these models to plaque and saliva pH profiles.
why: Dentists and researchers evaluating the cariogenicity of foods, cariostatic agents, or biomaterials may need to consider that sparse pH sampling can understate caries risk, and GatorpH offers a free way to analyze such data.

headline: Metabolic memory may keep oral inflammation going after blood sugar and lipids are corrected
summary: A review in the Journal of Dental Research describes how metabolic memory can sustain oral inflammation even after hyperglycemia or hyperlipidemia has been controlled. It is most evident in periodontitis and impaired wound healing, and the authors link it to epigenetic changes such as DNA methylation, histone modifications, and noncoding RNAs. The review also outlines possible preventive and therapeutic approaches.
why: Patients whose metabolic disease is under control may still have persistent periodontal inflammation and slower healing, which could affect how clinicians plan periodontal treatment and follow-up for these patients.

headline: Dental radiotherapy spacers: material and thickness modestly reduce transmitted dose
summary: An in vitro study compared three 3D-printed resins and three elastomeric impression materials, each at 5 mm and 10 mm thickness, for how much they reduced radiation transmitted through them in a solid-water phantom. Putty-type polyvinyl siloxane produced the largest reduction at both thicknesses, and thicker specimens reduced dose more than thinner ones. Among the printed resins, the Saremco Print CROWNTEC resin gave a greater reduction than the other two at 10 mm, while no difference was seen at 5 mm.
why: The reductions were small and tied to this specific setup, and the authors state they do not show intrinsic material attenuation or clinical tissue protection, so these results should not be used to judge how well a spacer protects patient tissue.

headline: Intraoral scans can track alveolar ridge gap in infants with cleft lip and palate
summary: A retrospective pilot study tested a standardized digital workflow that measures the distance between alveolar segments in six infants with unilateral cleft lip and palate. Serial intraoral scans were taken at birth, during presurgical treatment, and after primary lip repair, and the workflow was applied successfully at every time point. The measurements showed changes in segment distance over the treatment timeline.
why: This suggests intraoral scanning could give clinicians an objective, repeatable way to monitor presurgical infant orthopedic treatment, though the study is small and only demonstrates feasibility.

headline: Rotational path concept applied to maxillofacial prosthetics in a clinical case
summary: A Journal of Prosthodontics article describes extending the rotational path placement concept, usually used for removable partial dentures, to maxillofacial prostheses. The authors say these prostheses can restore oral continuity, esthetics and phonetics, and may also improve chewing, speech and swallowing. The report presents a clinical case to illustrate the approach.
why: It offers a possible prosthetic option for patients with maxillofacial defects, though the excerpt is based on a single case presentation and does not establish broader outcomes.

headline: WCLI Asia-Pacific symposium in Taipei draws 224 dental professionals
summary: The World Clinical Laser Institute held its 2026 Asia-Pacific Symposium in Taipei in October, with 224 dental professionals attending. The event aimed to widen access to clinical laser training and included lectures and a panel on laser use across implantology, periodontics, prosthodontics, aesthetic dentistry and paediatric dentistry.
why: It shows continued interest among dentists in the region in learning laser applications across several specialties, which may matter for those considering laser training for their practice.

headline: Free 1-hour CE webinar on doing analog implant impressions correctly
summary: Dentistry Today is promoting a free one-credit CE webinar, airing tonight at 8 PM Eastern, on analog implant impressions. Presenter Jimmy Stegall, CDT, a dental lab veteran and 2024 NADL Educator of the Year, will cover the full open-tray protocol, including coping management, tray selection, material flow, and chairside quality checks. The session also looks at how the Mira Tray system from Hager Worldwide addresses common failure points.
why: Dentists who still take analog implant impressions, and the lab technicians who receive them, may find practical steps to improve accuracy and communication between office and lab.

headline: Aligner distalization moves maxillary molars mainly by crown tipping and rotation
summary: A retrospective study of 30 adults treated with Invisalign sequential distalization plus Class II elastics used fused CBCT and intraoral scan models to measure maxillary first molar movement in three planes. The mesiobuccal cusp tip moved distally by a mean of 1.75 mm, about 69.7% of the planned movement, while the root apex moved only 0.35 mm, about 27.6% of the planned movement. Distal crown tipping exceeded the planned value, and mesial-out rotation was only slightly greater than planned.
why: For clinicians using clear aligners for Class II correction, the molar movement is largely crown tipping and rotation rather than true bodily distalization, which may matter when planning anchorage and expectations.

headline: Structured explanations by dental interns boost patient knowledge but not roles
summary: This randomized controlled trial tested a structured communication protocol used by dental interns in endodontics and periodontics clinics. Patients who received the structured explanations scored significantly higher on knowledge measures than controls (84 experimental, 52 control after excluding incomplete surveys). Overall communication and paternalism scores did not differ significantly, though the experimental group perceived more communicative effort and greater trust in clinical authority.
why: A single structured explanation session can improve patient understanding, but it did not shift traditional practitioner-patient roles, suggesting communication skills should be explicitly taught and assessed in dental curricula rather than assumed from student empathy.

headline: Pediatric dentistry program directors reach consensus on EPA timing for unsupervised practice
summary: A survey of pediatric dentistry residency program directors in the United States and Canada aimed to set expected timelines for when residents can perform each pediatric entrustable professional activity (EPA) without supervision. Of 108 directors contacted, 41 responded, and consensus, defined as 80% agreement, was reached for every EPA presented, with independence increasing over the course of residency. More than 90% of respondents (37 of 41) said they were likely or very likely to use national EPA benchmarks to assess resident progress.
why: A shared national timeline gives residency programs clearer, more transparent standards for when residents can practice independently, which supports safe care from new graduates.

headline: Desiccation Technology Emerges as Nonsurgical Adjunct for Periodontal Therapy
summary: An article describes desiccation technology, a nonsurgical adjunct that uses a liquid or gel medicament to pull moisture from biofilm and necrotic tissue so it can be removed more easily alongside mechanical periodontal treatment. The product YOUNG PerioDT is named as an example, with a manufacturer-recommended application time of 10 to 30 seconds followed by rinsing. The piece also cites a 2018 split-mouth clinical trial comparing scaling and root planing alone with scaling and root planing plus a desiccant, though the excerpt cuts off before its findings.
why: Dentists treating periodontal disease may find this an additional nonsurgical option to pair with debridement, though the excerpt does not report the trial results, so its clinical benefit remains unconfirmed here.

headline: Phoenix Dental Agency Launches Social Studio Social Media Service for Practices
summary: Phoenix Dental Agency has launched Social Studio, a service that turns in-office photos of dental teams into personality-driven social media content. It starts with a full-day photoshoot and is followed by a 12-month content plan with two custom posts per week, creative editing, ongoing support, and monthly paid boosts for top-performing posts.
why: Practices struggling to stand out on social media could outsource photography, content creation, and posting, letting staff focus on patient care while building familiarity with patients between visits.

headline: Dr. Cesar Tapia Named Fellow of the American College of Dentists
summary: Dr. Cesar Tapia, founder of ConfiDENT in Alpharetta and Cumming, Georgia, was awarded Fellowship in the American College of Dentists on October 24, 2026, at the College's Annual Meeting and Convocation in Santa Barbara, California. Fellowship is by invitation and recognizes demonstrated leadership and contributions to the dental profession and society. Dr. Tapia, who is originally from Lima, Peru, also holds two master's credentials in implantology and was named an Associate Fellow of the American Academy of Implant Dentistry in 2025.

headline: Extraction socket-supported guide improves implant accuracy in anterior in vitro models
summary: An in vitro study tested a root-shaped, extraction socket-supported guide (ESSG) for immediate single-tooth implant placement in the anterior region. Using 3D-printed resin models of central incisors with labial, central, or palatal root-position deviations, 120 implants were placed with either the ESSG or a conventional tooth-supported guide. In labial and palatal deviation models, the ESSG produced smaller angular errors and, in most cases, smaller positional errors, though the authors state clinical studies are still needed.
why: For dentists placing immediate anterior implants, this suggests a socket-based guide may improve placement accuracy when root position differs from the planned model, but the evidence is laboratory-based and not yet confirmed in patients.

headline: Play-Doh-inspired biomaterial shows preclinical promise for dental bone repair
summary: Researchers have developed iHEÄLS, a Play-Doh-inspired biomaterial designed to control bleeding, adhere to tissue, support bone regeneration, conform to irregular defects, and stay mechanically stable. Preclinical findings suggest it could be useful in oral and maxillofacial surgery, especially for irregular bone defects and stabilising bone grafts. Dental Tribune spoke with two of the researchers about the material and the research still needed before clinical use.

headline: UTSA dental school adds full digital restorative workflow to all four years
summary: The University of Texas at San Antonio School of Dentistry has introduced a complete digital workflow for restorative dentistry across its four-year DDS program. Students use the same digital tools in preclinical training that they will later use with patients, including intraoral scanning, digital jaw motion tracking, CAD design and in-house manufacturing, starting in the first year.

headline: Hardware-free wrapping technique for corticoperiosteal flaps in mandibular reconstruction
summary: A technical note describes a mandibular reconstruction method that seats a medial femoral condyle corticoperiosteal flap in a prepared recess without rigid fixation. The periosteum is drawn around the superior mandibular margin to form a sealed, vascularized envelope over exposed bone. The authors aim to improve osseous integration and revascularization in irradiated, infected, or osteonecrotic bone, and suggest it may suit selected oncologic cases needing postoperative radiotherapy.
why: For surgeons treating limited mandibular defects in compromised bone, this offers a possible hardware-free option that may reduce fixation-related complications, though the excerpt describes a technique without reported outcome data.

headline: Longer closed lock duration linked to weaker jaw function gains after arthroscopic disc repositioning
summary: A retrospective cohort study at Massachusetts General Hospital examined 38 patients with closed lock who had arthroscopic disc repositioning, covering 42 temporomandibular joints. Each additional month between symptom onset and surgery was associated with a smaller improvement in Jaw Functional Limitation Scale scores at three months, and this held after adjusting for preoperative score and age. The study reports that longer locking duration was tied to poorer short-term functional improvement.
why: For dentists and oral surgeons counseling TMJ patients, the findings suggest that delaying surgery after failed conservative care may be associated with less functional benefit, which can inform the timing of referral and surgical discussions.
