headline: PRF added to DFDBA does not significantly boost new bone in sinus augmentation
summary: In a split-mouth randomized trial, each patient had one maxillary sinus grafted with DFDBA alone and the other with DFDBA plus leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin and injectable PRF. Of 24 enrolled subjects, 21 completed follow-up, and newly formed bone at 6 months did not differ significantly between sides (median 48.72% with PRF versus 45.76% without, p = 0.5). Connective tissue was lower on the PRF side (31.48% versus 36.92%, p = 0.016), and all definitively restored implants remained functional over 1 year of prosthetic follow-up.
why: Adding PRF to DFDBA did not improve bone formation in this trial, so it offers no clear advantage for sinus graft outcomes, though the 1-year implant survival data are encouraging for restored implants.

headline: CBCT and finite element study of post-restored maxillary lateral incisors under lateral load
summary: Researchers used cone beam CT to measure buccolingual root diameter in maxillary lateral incisors of 30 participants, finding the mean rose from 5.09 mm at 5 mm to 5.80 mm at 9 mm from the radiographic apex. Separately, a finite element model of one tooth geometry tested post diameters of 1.3 or 1.6 mm and ferrules of 1 or 2 mm under a 200 N lateral load at three contact sites. The authors caution that the modeling results describe component-specific responses in one geometry and do not predict fracture, fatigue, or clinical outcomes.
why: It offers imaging-based reference values for lateral incisor root width near the apex, but the stress findings are modeling results only and should not be taken as guidance for choosing post or ferrule dimensions in patients.

headline: Salivary cytokines elevated in asymptomatic removable denture wearers
summary: Researchers compared unstimulated saliva from 34 asymptomatic removable denture wearers with 21 people who had healthy natural teeth, all without clinical signs of oral inflammation. Several cytokines, including TNF-α, IL-2, IL-17, IL-4 and IL-10, were significantly higher in the denture group, and TNF-α correlated strongly with IL-17. The authors suggest salivary cytokine analysis could be a noninvasive way to detect subclinical inflammation and patients at risk for denture-related stomatitis, though the excerpt cuts off before further conclusions.
why: This suggests saliva testing might one day help identify denture wearers at risk of stomatitis before visible symptoms appear, but it is a small study and the diagnostic use is not yet established.

headline: Low-temperature aging tested on colored multilayer ultratranslucent zirconia
summary: An in vitro study aged disks of three colored multilayered ultratranslucent zirconia materials in a hydrothermal reactor to simulate low-temperature degradation, then measured microstructure, optical properties, and mechanical strength of each layer. Aging kept phase composition largely stable and reduced translucency with color shifts that the authors judged clinically acceptable. Hardness was mostly maintained, though flexural strength dropped in one layer, and one material showed stable fluorescence.
why: This suggests these colored zirconias hold up reasonably well to aging-related changes in appearance and strength, which may inform material selection for esthetic restorations, though the findings come from lab testing rather than clinical outcomes.

headline: Dynamic navigation improves novice socket-shield accuracy in vitro versus freehand
summary: In a crossover in vitro study, eight novice dentists performed socket-shield preparations on standardized models using freehand and dynamic navigation. Dynamic navigation produced higher geometric overlap with the planned preparation (78.0% vs. 63.5%), shorter length deviation (1.12 mm vs. 2.68 mm), and higher self-rated confidence, with no perforations versus 5 of 24 freehand preparations. A small exploratory phase with four operators was analyzed descriptively only.
why: Dynamic navigation may help less experienced clinicians prepare socket-shield teeth more accurately and with fewer perforations in the lab, but the authors state the findings do not show clinical safety or patient benefit.

headline: Smoking's effect on L-PRF properties remains unclear, systematic review finds
summary: A PRISMA 2020 systematic review pooled laboratory studies comparing leukocyte-platelet-rich fibrin from smokers and non-smokers. Nine studies were included, with several reporting looser fibrin architecture and altered cell entrapment in smoker-derived membranes, while growth-factor findings were inconsistent. The certainty of evidence was rated very low, so the authors concluded that it is not yet possible to say whether smoking compromises L-PRF.
why: Dentists using L-PRF should not assume smoking impairs the membrane based on current data, but the review supports continuing to encourage smoking cessation given its known oral and systemic harms.

source: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol
headline: Ghost cell-negative jaw carcinoma with CTNNB1 mutation arising in a calcifying cyst
summary: A case report describes an odontogenic carcinoma in a 14-year-old girl that arose within a calcifying odontogenic cyst and lacked ghost cells, which are the usual histologic clue for this tumor type. Sequencing found a CTNNB1 G34E mutation and no mutations in the MAPK or SHH pathway genes, and the authors assigned a diagnosis of WNT pathway-altered odontogenic carcinoma. They propose a molecularly defined category to address cases that the ghost cell-based classification cannot place.
why: It suggests that some jaw tumors may be missed or misclassified if clinicians and pathologists rely only on ghost cells, so molecular testing may matter for future diagnostic accuracy.

headline: Burnout in dental and dental hygiene students tied to clinical training and stress
summary: A repeated survey of DDS and dental hygiene students at Dalhousie University in Fall 2023 and Winter 2024 measured burnout, stress, grit, and well-being. Exhaustion was highest among students in clinical training, in the Fall term, and among those with higher stress or lower well-being. After adjustment, burnout did not differ independently by program, and the authors call for multilevel strategies addressing workload, clinical pacing, and coping resources.
why: Burnout in students appears driven more by clinical training load, stress, and personal resources than by whether they are in dental or hygiene school, suggesting that workload and pacing of clinical work matter for future team members' wellbeing.

headline: Review urges dental curricula to include planetary health, One Health and sustainability
summary: A narrative review in the Journal of Dental Education argues that oral health is shaped by environmental, social and systemic factors beyond clinical care, and that dental professionals could do more to promote sustainable practices if trained for it. It describes strategies and resources for teaching Planetary Health, One Health and environmental sustainability in dental education, aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals. The authors also highlight curriculum initiatives at one dental institution in the United States and one in the United Kingdom.
why: Dental schools and educators may need to consider how to add transdisciplinary sustainability content to training, and practices may see growing expectations around environmental responsibility.

headline: Admissions Criteria Weakly Predict Preclinical Restorative Performance in Dental Students
summary: A study of 367 predoctoral students from the 2023-2025 graduating classes tested whether admissions data predict success in preclinical manual dexterity work. DAT Perceptual Ability Test scores and a quantitatively or biomedically intensive undergraduate major were significantly tied to dexterity-based GPA, and adding interaction terms modestly improved prediction. Models predicted the longitudinal grade trajectory better than static outcomes, though overall predictive power stayed limited.
why: Admissions scores alone are a weak guide to which students will struggle with hands-on restorative and prosthetic work, so faculty may get more value from tracking student progress over time and targeting advising early.

headline: Clear mold-guided composites outperform freehand in dental student simulation study
summary: In a within-subject simulation, 21 dental students placed maxillary anterior composite restorations on typodonts using freehand and clear mold-guided techniques. Three blinded faculty raters scored esthetics, and restorations were compared with a reference model by RMS deviation. The mold-guided technique scored higher on esthetics, had lower deviation from the planned morphology, and took less time.

headline: Peer-led and faculty-led teaching of updated FDI criteria yield similar learning gains
summary: A study of 49 dental students compared peer-assisted learning with faculty-led instruction on the updated FDI restorative evaluation criteria. Peer sessions were offered both face-to-face and online. Both approaches improved knowledge, with no significant difference between the two groups after adjusting for baseline scores, and no difference between online and in-person formats; the peer-assisted group also showed a significant drop in stress.

headline: Admetec Launches PLUS Family of Lightweight Headlights for Dental Loupes
summary: Admetec has introduced the PLUS Family, a new line of high-output, lightweight headlights designed for high-magnification loupes. The lineup includes the wireless Butterfly EVO+, rated up to 140,000 LUX with a 95-mm beam, and the wired Orchid+, rated up to 200,000 LUX with a tighter beam. The company says these are the first headlights made specifically for high-magnification loupes.
why: For clinicians using magnification loupes, brighter and more focused headlights may help offset the darker working field that comes with higher magnification, though the excerpt offers no independent performance data.

headline: Delta Dental Community Care Foundation Commits $16.3M in Access to Care Grants
summary: The Delta Dental Community Care Foundation, the philanthropic arm of Delta Dental of California and its affiliates, announced $16.3 million in Access to Care Grant funding for nonprofits serving underserved populations. The grants cover initiatives across the company's 15-state service area and Washington, D.C. The foundation says it has provided more than $200 million to nonprofits since 2011, with funding focused on seniors and special populations, innovative and preventive care, and rural communities.
why: Dentists may see more funding flowing to community clinics and nonprofit providers in underserved areas, which could expand affordable care options and referral partnerships in their region.

headline: Henry Schein to present at two investor conferences in late 2026
summary: Henry Schein, Inc. (Nasdaq: HSIC) will present at the Jefferies Healthcare Conference in London on November 17, 2026, and at the Piper Sandler Healthcare Conference in New York on December 1, 2026. Both presentations will be available by live webcast, with replays posted on the company's website afterward.

headline: Review urges sex-specific host modulation therapy for periodontitis
summary: A J Dent Res review examines preclinical and clinical evidence on how biological sex affects host modulation therapies for periodontitis. It reports that males show higher prevalence and severity of the disease, and that sex-dependent differences appear in pathways such as IL-1β/inflammasome signaling, RANKL/OPG-driven osteoclast activity, IL-17, IL-6, complement, resolvins and cyclooxygenase inhibitors. The authors call for sex to be treated as a biological variable in periodontal research and for sex-disaggregated data reporting.
why: Differences in how male and female patients respond to immune-targeted treatments suggest future nonsurgical periodontal therapies may need to account for patient sex, though these findings remain preliminary and clinical application is not yet established.

headline: Lifetime Water Fluoridation Not Linked to Cognition in Older Irish Adults
summary: A study using data from the Irish Longitudinal Study on Ageing estimated lifetime and early-life fluoride exposure from community water fluoridation by linking residential histories to national monitoring data. After adjusting for sociodemographic, lifestyle, health, loneliness, and health care access factors, lifetime exposure showed no association with errors on the MMSE or MoCA cognitive tests. Early-life exposure did not modify these associations.

headline: Metal and plastic probes perform comparably for peri-implant pocket depth; electronic probe unreliable
summary: A cross-sectional study of 50 patients with 85 implants compared a metal probe, a plastic probe and an electronic probe for measuring peri-implant probing depth, with patient pain and preference recorded. The metal and plastic probes were relatively accurate and agreed closely, though a thick peri-implant mucosal phenotype reduced the metal probe's accuracy. The electronic probe deviated by 1.5 mm or more from the correct depth in 65% of measurements.

headline: Dental students' predictions about treating underserved patients compared with alumni practice
summary: A longitudinal University of Iowa study compared dental students' stated willingness to treat 13 underserved populations with what their alumni actually do. Students' surveys from their first and fourth years were matched to alumni surveys mailed in Fall 2023, with 227 alumni responding. Many alumni treated more underserved groups than they had predicted as students, although they overestimated future care for some groups, including Medicaid, homebound or nursing home, and incarcerated patients.
why: The findings suggest dentists often end up serving a wider range of patients than they expected as students, though students may overestimate how much they will treat certain groups such as Medicaid patients, which is useful context for dental education and practice planning.

headline: Endodontic residents' colorblind racial attitudes linked to phone follow-up after root canal pain
summary: An online study of US endodontic residents used four standardized video vignettes, two featuring Black actors and two featuring White actors, describing moderate pain after root canal treatment. Residents rated how likely they were to offer various treatments and completed a colorblind racial attitudes scale; 37% of invited residents responded. Treatment choices differed little by patient race overall, but the likelihood of planning a follow-up phone call depended on residents' attitude scores, with low scorers more likely to call Black patients and high scorers more likely to call White patients.
why: Even when treatment decisions look consistent across patients, subtle differences in how clinicians communicate and follow up may vary by race and implicit attitudes, which is worth considering in patient communication and post-treatment care.

headline: Dentsply Sirona Offers Five Free CE Webinars in November and December
summary: Dentsply Sirona is hosting five complimentary live webinars in November and December 2026, each worth one CE credit. Topics include clear aligner case selection, connected implant workflows, digital scanning, and orthodontic treatment planning. The sessions are led by five dental presenters and are aimed at professionals at different career stages.
why: Dentists can earn free CE credit on digital workflows, clear aligner case selection, and implant planning, which may help with case selection and patient communication.

headline: Angelalign Appoints Former Straumann CEO Marco Gadola as Senior Advisor
summary: Angelalign Technology has named Marco Gadola, former chief executive of Straumann Group, as a senior advisor. He will advise the board and senior management on culture, strategy, and governance. The company's CEO, Fox Hu, said the appointment supports its growth plans.
why: A senior appointment from a well-known dental industry figure at an orthodontic aligner company signals the company's focus on global growth and governance, which may matter to orthodontists who use its products.

headline: Dentsply Sirona Academy Schedules Free Fall Webinars on Digital and Aligner Topics
summary: Dentsply Sirona Academy is offering five complimentary one-hour live webinars in November and December 2026. Topics include clear aligner case selection, connected implant workflows, digital scanning, and orthodontic treatment planning, and each session provides one continuing education credit.
why: Dentists can earn free CE credit on aligner candidacy, referral decisions, digital scanning, and implant workflows, which may help them decide whether to refer aligner cases or adopt digital tools.

headline: CT angiography shows limited accuracy in predicting internal maxillary artery course in TMJ ankylosis surgery
summary: This exploratory prospective case series of 34 patients (48 joints) with temporomandibular joint ankylosis compared preoperative CT angiography findings on the internal maxillary artery with what surgeons saw during 1 cm gap arthroplasty. Preoperative classification matched intraoperative findings in only 56.3% of joints, and CTA-based categories did not meaningfully separate patients by intraoperative outcomes such as resection time, blood loss, vascular control, or transfusion needs. The authors conclude CTA is best used as a complementary planning tool rather than a definitive predictor of intraoperative vascular anatomy.
why: Surgeons planning TMJ ankylosis procedures should not rely on CT angiography alone to anticipate the internal maxillary artery's position, and should stay prepared for intraoperative bleeding risk.

headline: Free latissimus dorsi flap with serratus fascia dural repair for complex skull infection
summary: A retrospective single-center series of 13 adults from 2016 to 2026 treated cranial osteomyelitis, osteoradionecrosis, or exposed skull bone with a free latissimus dorsi flap. When the dura needed repair, vascularized serratus anterior fascia from the same pedicle was used. Final flap survival was 85%, and 62% of patients had stable reconstruction without recurrent infection at a median of 15.5 months.
why: For oral and maxillofacial surgeons managing irradiated or infected skull defects, this suggests a microsurgical soft-tissue option, though the cohort is small, high-risk, and had 38% mortality, so it is not a general treatment guide.

headline: Piezosurgery and rotary burs give similar gingival stability after aesthetic crown lengthening
summary: A 6-month split-mouth randomised trial in 15 patients with altered passive eruption compared ostectomy performed with piezosurgery or rotary burs during aesthetic crown lengthening. Gingival margin change between 6 weeks and 6 months, the primary outcome, did not differ significantly between the two methods. Most crown height reduction occurred in the first week, and the tissue was stable by 6 weeks.
why: For clinicians choosing a bone-removal instrument for aesthetic crown lengthening, this suggests piezosurgery and burs produce comparable long-term gingival margin stability, so the choice can rest on other factors such as handling and patient experience.

headline: Labial augmented corticotomy improves mandibular incisor periodontium in Class III patients
summary: A prospective cohort study followed 35 skeletal Class III patients, covering 140 mandibular incisors, after labial augmented corticotomy during orthodontic-orthognathic treatment. Keratinised gingiva width and gingival thickness increased and stayed above baseline through treatment completion, and labial alveolar bone area remained higher than baseline. Lingual alveolar bone area decreased progressively over time, while probing depth and gingival recession showed no significant overall change.
why: For dentists treating Class III patients with orthognathic surgery, labial corticotomy may help sustain gingival and labial bone health in the lower incisors, though the loss of lingual bone over time is a consideration.

headline: Additively vs. subtractively made zirconia: optical differences after aging
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of five in vitro studies compared the optical properties of additively manufactured (AM) and subtractively manufactured (SM) zirconia after staining and aging. AM zirconia showed less color change and lower initial translucency than SM zirconia, but greater translucency change after aging. The authors reported that these differences stayed within clinically acceptable thresholds.
why: For restorations, the choice between AM and SM zirconia may make little visible difference in color stability or translucency over time, though AM material's translucency shifts more with aging.

headline: Systematic review finds conservative care favored for intruded primary teeth
summary: A PRISMA 2020 systematic review searched five databases for studies of intrusive luxation in primary teeth, including 21 studies (nine retrospective studies and 12 case reports) out of 1,331 records. Spontaneous re-eruption was the most common approach and generally had favorable outcomes, though recovery was slower and less predictable in severe intrusion. Surgical repositioning and fixation were described in only a few studies with variable results, and most studies had a low risk of bias.
why: The review supports watchful, conservative management for intruded primary teeth to avoid unnecessary invasive procedures and protect the permanent successors, but it stresses long-term follow-up for delayed pulpal, periodontal, and developmental complications.

headline: Collagen matrix added to immediate implants improves soft tissue thickness and stability
summary: A randomized clinical trial compared immediate anterior implants placed with or without simultaneous augmentation using a volume-stable collagen matrix. Of 40 enrolled patients, 38 completed follow-up, and soft tissue thickness was significantly greater in the augmented group at all time points. At 12 months, the augmented group gained soft tissue thickness and kept stable mucosal levels and volume, while the control group showed recession and volume shrinkage; marginal bone levels did not change significantly in either group.
why: For immediate implants in the esthetic zone, adding a collagen matrix at placement may help maintain thicker, more stable gum tissue over a year, though this is a single trial and its findings are preliminary.

headline: Angelalign Names Former Straumann CEO Marco Gadola as Senior Advisor
summary: Clear aligner company Angelalign Technology has appointed Marco Gadola, former CEO of Straumann Group, as a Senior Advisor. He will advise the board and senior management on culture, strategy, and governance. CEO Fox Hu said the company wants to keep improving its service to orthodontists.
why: A well-known former dental industry leader joining a major clear aligner company signals continued investment in orthodontic growth, which may affect the aligner options and industry direction practices see in the coming years.

headline: Align Technology Enters $270 Million Accelerated Stock Repurchase with Goldman Sachs
summary: Align Technology has entered a new accelerated stock repurchase agreement with Goldman Sachs to buy back $270 million of its common stock under a $1.0 billion program approved by its board in April 2025. The company says the deal fulfills a repurchase commitment announced in July and brings its total 2026 buybacks to about $500 million. The ASR is expected to be completed on or about December 29, 2026, funded from cash on hand, leaving roughly $330 million available under the program.
why: For dentists, this is a corporate finance update about Invisalign and iTero maker Align, with no direct change to clinical practice or patient care.

headline: Stabili-Teeth Chief Clinical Officer Urges Expanding Fixed Full-Arch Options
summary: In an interview, Dr. Dale Spadafora, chief clinical officer of Stabili-Teeth, argues that full-arch dentistry has reached an inflection point and that the next step is adding fixed treatment options rather than replacing existing ones. He says many patients who want fixed teeth leave without treatment due to anatomical or financial barriers, often defaulting to removable dentures. He describes the Stabili-Teeth protocol as a patented, fully implant-supported system using six implants, mixing standard and narrow-diameter implants, with fixed provisional teeth placed on the day of surgery.
why: It points to a possible fixed full-arch option for patients who might otherwise choose removable prostheses, though the excerpt is promotional from a company executive and offers no outcome data.

headline: Sandblasting with orthodontic primer gives strongest adhesive bond to stainless steel and CoCr
summary: An in-vitro study compared surface treatments (none, bur roughening, sandblasting) and primer systems for bonding orthodontic adhesive to stainless steel and cobalt-chromium. Metal primer alone caused complete pretest failures on untreated and bur-roughened surfaces of both metals. Sandblasting combined with an orthodontic primer produced the highest bond strengths on both substrates, while adding metal primer gave no consistent benefit.
why: For bonding attachments to non-noble metals such as stainless steel or CoCr, sandblasting followed by an orthodontic primer appears to be the most reliable approach, and metal primer alone is unlikely to be sufficient.

headline: Review of local anesthesia complications in dentistry proposes new classification
summary: A systematic review of PubMed, Web of Science and Scopus through June 2025 screened 364 records and included 28 studies on accidents and complications from dental local anesthetics. Complications were most frequent with inferior alveolar nerve blocks, and local and systemic events were identified, with many resolving on their own while others needed surgical or drug treatment. The authors propose classifying these events by affected anatomical plane (superficial, deep, neurological, orbitoocular) and by systemic category.
why: Dentists giving inferior alveolar nerve blocks should be aware that this technique carries the highest complication frequency, and a structured classification may help with recognizing and managing adverse events.

headline: Quiz Reviews Erosion, Abrasion, and Pathological Tooth Wear
summary: This Decisions in Dentistry quiz tests knowledge of tooth wear. It covers how erosion appears clinically, which everyday habits commonly cause abrasion, and how patient age helps decide whether wear is pathological or physiological.
why: A quick refresher on distinguishing erosive from abrasive wear and judging whether wear is age-appropriate can support more accurate assessment and management decisions during routine exams.

headline: Abusive supervision linked to hygienist distress and intent to leave
summary: A study in the Journal of Dental Hygiene surveyed 137 clinical hygienists in the US and Canada about abusive supervision, defined as sustained hostile verbal or nonverbal behavior from a supervisor. Of participants, 81% reported at least some abusive supervision, and about a third said it occurred moderately to very often. The article also reports high rates of psychological distress and notes that abusive supervision was more strongly tied to clinicians' intent to leave than psychological distress was.
why: Workplace culture, not only pay or scheduling, may play a major role in hygienist turnover, so practice leaders should examine how supervisors treat their teams.

headline: Unlicensed Iowa Clinic Offering Dental and Medical Care Is Shut Down by Court Order
summary: Authorities arrested Eddie Gingerich in August for running Old Cabin Retreat in Centerville, Iowa, a facility that provided medical, dental, and dietetic care without licenses. After Iowa's medical, dental, and dietetic boards filed a civil case, a court order has since closed the clinic, which had reportedly operated for six years. Gingerich pleaded guilty to employing an unlicensed dentist under a plea deal, and he now faces a felony charge for running an unlicensed hospital, which he disputes on sovereign citizen grounds.
why: It shows that state dental boards are working with medical and dietetic regulators to act against unlicensed clinics, and it is a reminder that dental care must be provided under a licensed professional.

headline: Missouri Expands Medicaid Dental Access as Federal Cuts Loom
summary: After Missouri's 2020 Medicaid expansion, adult dental benefits were added and reimbursement rates rose, bringing more dentists into the program. A new Independence surgery center, founded by Aaron Bumann, DDS, and colleagues, will serve Medicaid patients who need sedation for dental care and accepts referrals from other dental providers. Meanwhile, a 2025 federal budget law is expected to sharply cut Missouri's Medicaid funding starting in 2027, which could force benefit reductions and adds work requirements and six-month coverage renewals for beneficiaries.
why: Dentists treating Medicaid patients may see expanded access and new referral options, but upcoming funding cuts and stricter enrollment rules could reduce covered services and patient volume.

headline: California law requires dental plans to honor assignment of benefits from 2027
summary: Starting January 1, 2027, California dental plans must honor patients' assignment of benefits, so practices can collect payment directly from insurers rather than from patients up front. The change comes from AB 1629, a bill backed by the California Dental Association and signed by Governor Gavin Newsom in September. The law also requires patients to be told whether a practice is in network, receive an out-of-pocket cost estimate, and lets state regulators review dental networks for adequate provider coverage.
why: Dentists in California will be able to bill insurers directly instead of waiting on patient reimbursements, which may ease cash flow and reduce upfront collection friction.

headline: Polyacrylic acid toothpastes show promise against enamel erosion in lab study
summary: In an in vitro study, experimental toothpastes with bioadhesive polymers were tested on bovine enamel under erosive-abrasive and erosion-only cycling. Polyacrylic acid (PAA) formulations gave the strongest protection under erosive-abrasive conditions, performing better than the commercial anti-erosive comparator, while chitosan and linear polyphosphate formulations showed no protection. Under erosion-only conditions, PAA and the PAA, fluoride and stannous combination, along with a linear polyphosphate, fluoride and stannous formulation, also reduced surface loss.
why: This early laboratory work suggests PAA-based toothpastes could be a future option for patients with erosive tooth wear, but it does not yet show clinical benefit in people.

headline: Systematic review finds high bias and weak validation in AI dental diagnostic studies
summary: This PRISMA-guided systematic review assessed 96 studies of AI used in dental diagnosis across several specialties. Most studies were retrospective, convolutional neural networks were the most common architecture, and reported accuracy ranged from 81% to 99%. The authors found high risk of bias in 55.2% of studies, limited external validation, and gaps in reporting such as sample-size justification, missing-data handling, and data or code availability.
why: AI diagnostic tools look promising, but the evidence behind them is often weak, so they should be used as decision support that supplements, not replaces, clinical judgement.

headline: Robotic guided implant surgery shows promising early accuracy in edentulous patients
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis pooled five studies with 35 fully edentulous patients to assess robot-assisted computer-guided implant placement. The pooled deviations were 0.73 mm at the platform, 0.74 mm at the apex, and 1.64° angularly, with very low certainty of evidence. Higher-autonomy systems showed smaller platform and apex deviations than operator-dependent systems in an exploratory analysis.
why: Early data suggest robotic guidance can place implants accurately in fully edentulous patients, but the small sample and very low certainty mean it is not yet proven to outperform static or dynamic guided surgery, and survival and complication data are still lacking.

headline: Review finds promising clinical evidence for 3D-printed titanium implants and custom meshes
summary: A critical review of human clinical studies examined additively manufactured titanium implants, root-analogue implants, subperiosteal and maxillofacial devices, and customised titanium meshes used in oral rehabilitation and guided bone regeneration. Conventional additively manufactured endosseous implants showed favourable short- and medium-term results, with survival between 94.5% and 100% in selected cohorts. The authors noted that subperiosteal and maxillofacial devices carried notable long-term risks such as mucosal exposure and infection, and that heterogeneity and limited follow-up restrict firm comparisons.
why: Supports the use of additively manufactured titanium endosseous implants in practice, while signalling that custom subperiosteal devices and meshes need indication-specific judgement and longer-term data.

headline: Virtual surgical planning with standardized temporomandibular joint prostheses
summary: A technical note describes how virtual surgical planning can be carried out using available standardized total temporomandibular joint replacements instead of custom patient-specific implants. It covers the workflow and imaging outputs such as resection models, drilling depths, and occlusal splints. In the reported sample, the largest movements were 37 mm of anterior chin repositioning combined with 22 mm of vertical mandibular angle repositioning.

headline: Burning mouth syndrome linked to higher odds of psychological disorders, meta-analysis finds
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 52 studies examined the connection between burning mouth syndrome and psychological factors, searching several major databases through February 2026. Patients with burning mouth syndrome had about 3.19 times the odds of psychological disorders compared with controls, and the analysis found a strong positive association between the condition and psychological factors overall.
why: The findings support screening burning mouth syndrome patients for psychological concerns and including psychological assessment and support in a multidisciplinary management plan.

headline: Stem cell therapy shows no proven edge over iliac crest grafting for alveolar cleft repair
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 20 studies (six RCTs, 11 non-randomized studies, three case series; 437 participants) compared stem cell-based therapies with autologous bone grafting for secondary alveolar cleft repair. The single eligible RCT found less bone fill at 6 months with stem cell therapy than with iliac crest bone graft, while success rates and bone volume did not differ significantly between the two approaches. Certainty of evidence was rated very low for all outcomes.
why: Current evidence does not show stem cell therapy outperforms iliac crest grafting for alveolar cleft repair, so conventional grafting remains the reference approach until larger 12-month trials report results.

headline: Patient-specific PEEK implants show good aesthetic and functional results in craniomaxillofacial reconstruction
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 15 studies (203 patients, 236 implants) assessed patient-specific PEEK implants in adult craniomaxillofacial reconstruction. The pooled overall complication rate was 20.1%, mostly minor and mainly local surgical issues, with implant loss at 6.5% and aesthetic outcomes rated satisfactory or very satisfactory in 87.4% of cases. Implant loss was numerically higher in previously irradiated patients, though that subgroup was very small.
why: For dentists and oral surgeons involved in mandibular or midface reconstruction, this suggests PEEK patient-specific implants can be a viable alloplastic option for selected cases, while irradiated patients and local risk factors call for careful case selection.

headline: Condylectomy for active unilateral condylar hyperplasia: pooled meta-analysis of 17 studies
summary: A systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis of 17 studies covering 476 patients examined condylectomy for active unilateral condylar hyperplasia. The pooled rate of secondary orthognathic surgery was about 15% (95% CI 4.7-29.7%), with no significant difference among high, proportional, and adaptable condylectomy techniques. The pooled female proportion was 63%, and the authors note that very high heterogeneity limits how far the pooled mean age of 23.47 years can be interpreted.
why: For clinicians and oral surgeons managing active condylar hyperplasia, the findings suggest condylectomy is a reasonable early option with a modest rate of later jaw surgery, though the authors call for more standardized prospective trials before firm recommendations.

headline: Cold response and bleeding time may flag vital pulp therapy failure in mature teeth
summary: A prospective study of 50 mature permanent teeth with reversible or irreversible pulpitis treated by partial or full pulpotomy tracked outcomes over one year. Overall success was 82% (41 successful, nine failed), and prolonged cold response time and intraoperative bleeding time were significantly greater in failed cases. Patient-reported symptoms and preoperative diagnosis were not linked to outcome, and the authors say pulpal biomarkers offer only complementary prognostic information.
why: Simple chair-side measures such as cold response time and bleeding time during pulpotomy may help dentists gauge the likely outcome of vital pulp therapy, though the biomarkers are not yet reliable predictors on their own.

headline: S100A7 found to drive osteoclast-mediated tooth movement via RAGE signaling
summary: Researchers studied damage-associated molecular patterns in human periodontal ligament after orthodontic force and found S100A7 was upregulated, peaking at day 7. In mice, its homolog mS100a7a15 supported osteoclast formation, alveolar bone resorption and tooth movement, and its loss reduced these processes. The authors describe a signaling pathway running through RAGE, UBE2N, TRAF6 and NF-κB that appears to mediate this effect.

headline: Digitally milled, magnet-retained partial denture for a boy with ectodermal dysplasia
summary: A clinical report describes rehabilitating a 12-year-old boy with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia using a fully digital workflow and a magnet-retained removable partial denture. Resin crowns on the maxillary central incisors served as abutments for magnetic attachments, and the denture was milled as a single piece from a dual-shade PMMA disk. At six-month follow-up, retention and stability were satisfactory and the patient reported better chewing and facial appearance.
why: It shows a digital, monolithic approach with magnetic retention that may suit growing patients, while allowing later prosthetic changes.

headline: 3D-printed holders for cell culture tested; PLA shows promise in preliminary study
summary: Researchers evaluated four 3D-printable materials for holders used in cell culture assays, aiming to reduce variability between experiments. Using human gingival fibroblasts in direct contact with the printed holders, PLA showed significantly higher cell viability at day 7 than the other materials and was the only one remaining above the ISO 10993-5 cytotoxicity threshold. Over 21 days in culture medium, PLA holders kept pH stable, showed minimal mass change, and had only minor surface changes.

headline: Novel bioactive cement shows antibacterial and remineralizing effects in vitro
summary: Researchers developed a bioactive cement built from bioactive glass, ZrO2 and MgO nanoparticles, mixed with a phosphate and O-carboxymethyl chitosan liquid, intended as a temporary seal after selective caries removal. In laboratory tests, it met ISO 9917-1:2025 requirements for setting time, compressive strength and erosion depth, showed stronger activity against S. mutans than Biodentine, and produced a greater increase in dentin mineral density in an artificial caries model. The authors describe it as a promising candidate for temporary coronal restoration, though all findings are in vitro.
why: If validated clinically, this material could offer a temporary sealing option for deep caries lesions that combines antibacterial action with remineralization, but for now the evidence is limited to laboratory testing.

source: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol
headline: Parapharyngeal space involvement predicts reoperation in odontogenic infection patients
summary: A single-center retrospective cohort study reviewed 1,173 hospitalized patients treated for odontogenic infections between January 2014 and April 2020. Of these, 38 needed reoperation for further surgical drainage, and the rest did not. Parapharyngeal space involvement was the strongest independent predictor of reoperation, while chronic renal failure, chronic respiratory disease, and buccal space 1 involvement were linked to it in univariable analysis, and admission C-reactive protein showed an association in a limited subset of patients.
why: Patients with parapharyngeal spread, and possibly those with chronic renal or respiratory disease, may warrant closer monitoring for the possible need for repeat surgical drainage after admission for a dental infection.

headline: Toothpastes partly restore microhardness of irradiated dentin in an in vitro study
summary: An in vitro study compared five toothpastes on healthy human dentin and dentin exposed to head-and-neck radiotherapy (70 Gy). Radiotherapy lowered surface microhardness and gelatinolytic activity, and all five toothpastes partially restored microhardness, with distinct tubule obliteration patterns seen between conditions.
why: Patients who have had head-and-neck radiation may benefit from active-ingredient toothpastes as a low-cost preventive measure against dentin breakdown, though these lab results do not establish clinical outcomes.

headline: Dopamine-doped nanoparticles reduce root dentin permeability in ex vivo study
summary: Researchers tested polymeric nanoparticles doped with dexamethasone, zinc, parathyroid hormone, tideglusib, or dopamine on radicular dentin after endodontic treatment, assessing fluid filtration, remineralization, and hardness at 24 hours and 6 months. Dopamine-doped nanoparticles produced the lowest micropermeability, with sealed dentinal tubules and extended mineral deposits, but gave only limited structural reinforcement. The authors note the work is ex vivo and lacks biological, cytocompatibility, and in vivo validation.
why: This is laboratory evidence only; it suggests a possible future way to improve root canal sealing, but it does not yet change clinical endodontic practice.

headline: Scoping review maps 3D-printed porous and lattice dental implant research
summary: This scoping review charted 139 English-language reports on additively manufactured porous or lattice dental implants and implant-supported prostheses, covering titanium, cobalt-chromium, zirconia and polymer materials. Most studies tested physical mechanical properties, while clinical outcome data came from 18 reports. The authors found that porous designs can change stiffness, mass and tissue interaction, but manufacturing deviations and mechanical trade-offs limit translation to practice.
why: Current evidence supports the feasibility of porous printed implant designs and some clinical use, but it does not show that porosity itself produces better patient outcomes, so clinicians should not expect superior results from these designs yet.

headline: Dental procedures and trauma can temporarily skew pulp test results, review finds
summary: A scoping review of 78 studies (from 2,679 records) examined how orthodontic, surgical, periodontal, traumatic, and restorative or aesthetic interventions affect sensibility and vitality pulp tests. It found these factors can transiently change test responses without pulp necrosis, often producing false-negative sensibility results. Cold testing was generally more reliable than electric pulp testing, while pulse oximetry and laser Doppler flowmetry measure blood flow more directly but are limited by cost and availability.
why: Clinicians may avoid misdiagnosing pulp status and unnecessary root canal treatment by recognizing that recent procedures or trauma can cause temporary false-negative pulp test results and by choosing the more reliable test, with clinical and radiographic findings considered alongside.

headline: Referral marketing as the first pillar toward a $3 million orthodontic practice
summary: Orthodontist Roger P. Levin, DDS, argues that a practice following his "Four Pillars of Orthodontic Success" could grow toward $3 million in revenue. This article focuses on the first pillar, building referrals through referral marketing across patients, parents, referring doctors, social media and community. He notes that referrals help fill open chair time, and that production depends on both referral volume and start rate.
why: For orthodontic practices, the piece frames referral volume and case start rate as the two levers of production, which matters for scheduling efficiency and revenue planning.

headline: Dentsply Sirona offers five free webinars on aligners and digital workflows
summary: Dentsply Sirona is hosting a series of five free live webinars running from 10 November to 17 December. The sessions cover aligner case selection, digital implant workflows, elastics in aligner therapy, intra-oral scanning, and CBCT-informed aligner treatment planning.
why: Dentists and their teams can use these free sessions to build practical skills in aligner therapy and digital workflows without cost.

headline: Keep Dental Marketing Going Even When the Schedule Is Full
summary: An opinion piece argues that practices should maintain digital marketing during busy periods rather than pulling back when the schedule is full. It says consistent visibility, local search optimization, patient communication, and brand presence build long-term stability. The article notes that local SEO depends on steady activity, such as fresh content, accurate listings, and recent reviews, and that it is harder to rebuild after a pause.
why: A full schedule can hide future gaps caused by cancellations, delayed treatment, or patients moving, so steady marketing helps a practice keep its pipeline and search visibility over time.

headline: Align Technology Receives 2026 Extel All-America Executive Team Honors
summary: Align Technology was recognized in Extel Insights' 2026 All-America Executive Team rankings, which judge investor relations quality, leadership, and governance based on votes from buy-side and sell-side analysts. In the Health Care Technology & Distribution sector, Align placed first or second in three Large-Cap categories: Best CEO, Best IR Program, and Best Investor Day. This is the company's fourth such recognition in five years.
why: This is an investor-relations award for the Invisalign and iTero maker rather than a clinical development, so it has little direct bearing on day-to-day dental practice.

headline: 2026 New Mexico Mission of Mercy to offer free dental care in Albuquerque
summary: A two-day volunteer-run clinic, the 2026 New Mexico Mission of Mercy, will provide no-cost dental care on November 6 and 7 at Tingley Coliseum in Albuquerque. Delta Dental of New Mexico is supporting the event with the New Mexico Dental Association Foundation. Care is first-come, first-served with no appointments, and doors open at 5:15 a.m. each day.
why: Dentists in New Mexico may want to volunteer or refer patients who struggle to afford care, and the clinic shows the continued role of dental associations and insurers in expanding access.

headline: Qatar hospital performs first digitally planned subperiosteal implant procedure
summary: Hamad Medical Corporation, Qatar's main public healthcare provider, reports it carried out the country's first subperiosteal implant procedure. The surgery used 3D imaging, virtual surgical planning and patient-specific components. The case is presented as an option for selected patients who lack sufficient bone volume.
why: It shows digitally designed subperiosteal implants may be an alternative for patients with insufficient bone, a option worth knowing about when planning treatment for those cases.

headline: MassMutual South Carolina adds Bluewater Dental Advisors team in Charleston
summary: MassMutual South Carolina, a general agency based in Charleston, has brought on the Bluewater Dental Advisors team and its founders, Steven Huskey and Brandon Wilson. The advisory firm reportedly manages more than $73 million in client assets and serves dental practice owners nationwide.
why: Dental practice owners seeking financial planning may find a new advisory option focused on the dental sector, though the announcement itself is a firm-level personnel move with no direct clinical impact.

headline: Free Browser-Based 3D Scan Viewer tresD DICOM Launches for Clinicians
summary: An orthodontist at Clínica Áncora in Málaga, Spain, has released tresD DICOM, a free scan viewer that runs in a web browser with no sign-up or software install. Files are processed locally on the user's device rather than uploaded to a server, and the tool supports 3D rendering, airway heat maps, superimposition of scans, and files from several major imaging manufacturers. A companion free tool, tresD Models, opens intraoral scans in the browser.
why: Dentists who review CBCT scans could view patient images from any computer without sending files off-site, but the developer states the tools are visualization and teaching aids, not FDA-cleared or CE-marked devices, and their measurements are indicative only.

headline: Consensus report urges dental schools to add AI training and shorten paths to practice
summary: A working group of eight academic and organization leaders met at the 2026 Reimagining Dental Education Summit at Harvard University to develop consensus recommendations on technology, AI, and practice readiness. Their recommendations include an AI and technology curriculum across all levels of dental education, a dedicated leadership role for AI integration, and pathways to shorten time to a dental degree. They also called for more external clinical experiences and additional postgraduate residency positions with incentives.
why: Dental schools may change how they teach AI and clinical skills, and new graduates may arrive with different training, which could affect hiring and how practices onboard associates.

headline: Survey finds US dental schools use varied faculty calibration methods in prosthodontics
summary: A cross-sectional survey of 27 US CODA-accredited dental programs examined how predoctoral prosthodontics and restorative faculty are standardized and calibrated. About 73% of respondents reported a formal process for standardizing teaching, and 69% reported one for calibrating faculty assessment, though methods varied widely. Among the 17 respondents who answered the perception question, all agreed these practices improve education quality and student outcomes.
why: Dental educators and practices that train or supervise students may see that consistent faculty calibration is common but uneven, and that extramural site faculty inclusion and protected faculty time are areas needing attention.

headline: Dental communication assessment tools validated in Portuguese and English
summary: Researchers adapted the Patient Communication Assessment Instrument (PCAI) and Student Communication Assessment Instrument (SCAI) into Brazilian Portuguese and tested them with students and patients in Brazil and Canada. Factor analyses found a consistent three-factor structure (Caring, Sharing, Comfort) in both languages, explaining 44.1% to 70.5% of the variance. Internal reliability was high across all domains, and the authors noted small cultural differences in factor composition.
why: The findings support using these tools to measure therapeutic communication in dental education across cultures, and suggest communication training may benefit from adapting to diverse patient populations.

headline: FACE Forward program lifts dental students' interest in academic careers
summary: A yearlong collaborative program between two universities used lectures, mentorship, professional development, and teaching experiences to introduce dental students to academic dentistry. Of 29 enrolled students, 24 completed it, and afterward 95% said they were somewhat or very interested in academic careers. Familiarity with academic career pathways rose from 20% before the program to 86% after, and scheduling conflicts with academic obligations were the main challenge.
why: Early exposure to faculty careers may help build the pipeline for the national dental faculty shortage, and similar mentorship programs could be a way for practices and schools to encourage future educators.

headline: Admetec Launches PLUS Family of Headlights for Magnification Loupes
summary: Admetec has released the PLUS Family, a line of lightweight headlight attachments for high-magnification loupes, including the wireless Butterfly EVO+ and the wired Orchid+. The Butterfly EVO+ is listed at up to 140,000 lux, weighs 29 grams with its battery, and runs up to 4.5 hours, while the Orchid+ offers up to 200,000 lux with a tighter beam, weighs 11 grams, and has up to 25 hours of runtime from its wired battery unit. The company says the headlights address dim fields that can occur when higher magnification is used with ergonomic loupes.
why: For dentists using magnification, these new headlights target the dimmer working field that often comes with ergonomic loupes, which may matter when considering lighting upgrades for loupe-based practice.

headline: Meta-analysis ranks MMF screws above hybrid and Erich arch bars for jaw fracture fixation
summary: A Bayesian network meta-analysis of 12 randomized controlled trials (624 subjects) compared Erich arch bars, hybrid arch bars, and maxillomandibular fixation screws for maxillofacial fractures. Hybrid arch bars significantly shortened operative time compared with Erich arch bars, and screws were associated with shorter operative time than hybrid bars, though that difference was not statistically significant. Screws also had the lowest overall complication rate, and rankings placed screws first, hybrid bars second, and Erich arch bars last.

headline: Whiter Isn't Always a Better Match: 12-Month Intracoronal Bleaching Reanalysis
summary: A post hoc reanalysis of a clinical trial compared 35% hydrogen peroxide with 37% carbamide peroxide for intracoronal bleaching, using four weekly walking-bleach sessions and tracking color through 12 months. Hydrogen peroxide produced a greater color change (ΔE00) across post-baseline assessments, but whiteness index results did not differ significantly between the two agents. The maximum whiteness often did not coincide with the closest match to the patient's natural homologous tooth.
why: Whitening amount alone may not indicate the best outcome, so clinicians may need to consider how closely a bleached tooth matches its natural neighbor and whether results stay stable over time.

headline: Smoking linked to more gum inflammation, staining and poorer whiteness in SMILE study
summary: Researchers compared oral health, tooth aesthetics and self-reported outcomes between 308 current smokers and 66 never smokers in the SMILE cohort. After adjusting for age, sex and nationality, current smoking was independently linked to greater gingival inflammation, extrinsic staining, reduced tooth whiteness, poorer oral hygiene and lower self-perceived general health. The authors say combining calibrated digital measurements with standard clinical indices offers a reproducible way to track changes after smoking cessation or substitution.

headline: IDL Dental Technologies to exhibit implant portfolio at GNYDM 2026
summary: Israeli implant maker IDL Dental Technologies will show its dental implant systems and related prosthetic products at the exhibition held with the 2026 Greater New York Dental Meeting. The meeting runs from 29 November to 1 December at the Jacob K. Javits Convention Center in New York. Visitors can find the company's team at Booth 910.

headline: Tom's of Maine Launches Fluoride-Free Hydroxyapatite Toothpaste for Sensitivity
summary: Tom's of Maine has added a fluoride-free, anti-sensitivity toothpaste to its natural oral care line, combining naturally derived arginine and calcium carbonate with hydroxyapatite, the main mineral in tooth enamel. The company says calcium carbonate also helps remove surface stains. The product is sold in Gentle Mint flavor at Amazon.com for $11.99 (4.4 oz), with wider retail availability planned for 2027.
why: Dentists may see more patients asking about fluoride-free, natural toothpastes for sensitivity and whitening, and this gives them another option to discuss.

headline: Dentsply Sirona Makes 100,000th Heliodent Plus Intraoral X-Ray Unit
summary: Dentsply Sirona has produced its 100,000th Heliodent Plus intraoral X-ray unit at its facility in Bensheim, Germany. The system, introduced in 2009, is installed in practices across more than 115 countries and integrates with the company's Sidexis imaging software.
why: The milestone reflects continued demand for reliable intraoral imaging that fits into daily workflows, which may matter for practices weighing digital imaging upgrades or connected systems.

headline: Planet DDS Enters Canada as Canadian Dental Services Adopts Denticon
summary: Toronto-based Canadian Dental Services (CDS) has chosen Planet DDS and its Denticon practice management software for the general practices in its GP Division, marking Planet DDS's first move into Canada. CDS, founded in 2016 by Jeremy D. Behar, is consolidating more than six practice management systems onto Planet DDS's DentalOS platform. The company says the shared platform will standardize reporting and give clinic teams and support centers the same view of operations across its national footprint.
why: It signals growing consolidation among Canadian dental service organizations onto cloud-based, multi-location management systems, which may affect how DSOs and their partner dentists handle operations and reporting.

headline: Delta Dental Survey Links Oral Health Awareness to Cognitive Decline Concerns
summary: Delta Dental Insurance Company's 2026 Cognitive Decline and Oral Health Survey examined oral and cognitive health from the perspectives of older adults, caregivers, and dental providers. It found gaps in older adults' awareness of a possible link between the two, and that 73% of caregivers say managing oral care adds to the emotional demands of caregiving. Also, 82% of dental providers said they had treated a patient with cognitive decline in the last month.
why: Dentists may see more patients with cognitive decline who need help with daily oral care, and caregivers may look to dental teams for guidance on managing that care.

headline: DentScribe Releases AI Periodontal Charting Benchmark and Performance Report
summary: DentScribe announced its AI Periodontal Charting Benchmark 1.0, a framework for evaluating AI periodontal charting, built with input from dental teams. Its November 2026 report says the software passed all 68 test scripts and got all 1,967 expected chart entries correct with no extra entries. The results measure how the engine converts supplied text into chart entries.

headline: Tend Discloses Dentist Pay Formula and One-Year Earnings Results
summary: Dental group Tend, which runs 33 studios across six markets, released a year of results from a model paying general dentists up to 40% of adjusted production, in effect since October 2025. Its top 9% of dentists earn over $400,000 a year and its top 27% earn over $300,000, while dentist applications rose 160% and 86% of candidates who received offers accepted. The company cited American Dental Association data showing average private-practice general dentist net income of $215,320 in 2025, down from $274,198 in 2010 after inflation adjustment, along with roughly 34% associate turnover across DSOs.
why: The disclosure of a specific pay formula and earnings by a large DSO is unusual, and it highlights compensation transparency as a recruiting factor for associate dentists weighing employment options.

headline: Melatonin may help limit bone loss around immediate dental implants
summary: A randomised controlled clinical trial from Alexandria University tested melatonin applied locally around newly placed implants. The researchers examined whether it could preserve bone and affect biological processes involved in early osseointegration. The findings suggest its main potential benefit may be in limiting bone loss.
why: If confirmed, melatonin as a local adjunct could be a way to reduce early bone loss around immediate implants, though the excerpt alone does not establish clinical use.

headline: Flap release and membrane fixation interact to shape ridge augmentation in dogs
summary: In a preclinical study, six male dogs received implants in chronic noncontained buccal defects augmented with particulate bone substitute and resorbable collagen membranes. Sites were split into four groups by flap approach (limited or extensive periosteal release) and whether the membrane was fixed, then assessed at 12 weeks by micro-CT and histomorphometry. The authors describe the study as exploratory, finding that the effect of flap management depended on membrane fixation, with some combinations producing greater augmented dimensions than extensive release without fixation.

headline: Custom scan bodies improve deep-learning smartphone scans of full-arch implants
summary: An in vitro study compared four ways of digitising a maxillary edentulous model with six implant analogues: conventional open-tray impression, photogrammetry, and deep-learning reconstruction from smartphone video using either stock PEEK scan bodies or custom 3D-printed ones. Custom scan bodies were significantly more accurate than stock ones in the deep-learning method, while conventional impressions and photogrammetry showed the best trueness and photogrammetry the best precision. The authors describe the deep-learning approach as early stage but potentially viable for full-arch implant scanning.
why: This suggests smartphone-based deep-learning scanning could eventually offer an alternative to conventional impressions for full-arch implant cases, though it is still experimental and conventional methods remained more accurate here.

headline: CDKN1A drives osteoblast cell death and bone loss in apical periodontitis
summary: This study examined CDKN1A (p21) in apical periodontitis, using single-cell sequencing of human periapical lesions, Porphyromonas gingivalis-infected osteoblast cultures, and rat disease models. CDKN1A rose after P. gingivalis infection and promoted osteoblast apoptosis and pyroptosis while suppressing necroptosis and ferroptosis. In rats, overexpression worsened bone destruction, while knockdown reduced bone loss and restored osteogenic activity.

headline: Heat treatment shapes NiTi endodontic file performance despite identical design
summary: Researchers compared 240 NiTi endodontic instruments with the same nominal design, split into four groups: three made with a single heat-treatment condition (GOLD, PURPLE, BLUE) and one with a Dual Wire configuration combining two heat treatments. Geometry, elemental composition and phase-transformation temperatures were broadly similar across groups, but mechanical tests showed differences. BLUE had the greatest cyclic fatigue resistance and flexibility but the lowest buckling resistance, while DUAL WIRE had greater cutting ability than BLUE.
why: Instruments that look identical can behave differently in fatigue, flexibility, buckling and cutting depending on heat treatment, so clinicians should not assume a Dual Wire design offers a general mechanical advantage.

headline: Mendelian randomisation review finds limited causal evidence linking endodontic disease to systemic health
summary: This review explains how Mendelian randomisation can be used to test causal questions in endodontics and systematically identified 10 MR studies from 2023 to 2025. The only fairly consistent signal was a positive association between rheumatoid arthritis liability and endodontic outcomes, though it was biologically non-specific and not replicated. Other systemic exposures were mostly null, inconsistent or unreplicated, and evidence that endodontic disease causes systemic outcomes was limited to isolated findings, including one lacunar-stroke analysis.
why: Associations between endodontic disease and general health should not yet be treated as established cause-and-effect, so clinicians should avoid presenting such links to patients as proven.

headline: Cleaning methods affect staining and surface properties of 3D-printed denture base resins
summary: An in vitro study compared a heat-polymerized denture base resin with an extrinsically characterized 3D-printed resin after staining in coffee, tea, wine, or tobacco solutions, followed by chemical or mechanical cleaning. The heat-polymerized resin showed greater color change, while the 3D-printed resin showed greater surface changes. Whitening tablets gave the best color recovery, Efferdent best preserved surface smoothness, and biofilm formation varied among conditions.
why: Dentists fabricating or relining dentures may need to weigh how denture cleaning products affect stain removal, surface smoothness, and biofilm control, especially for 3D-printed bases.

headline: Custom-made ocular prostheses outperform prefabricated ones in motility and satisfaction
summary: A randomized controlled trial of 40 patients with a unilateral ocular defect compared prefabricated and custom-made ocular prostheses, in patients with atrophia bulbi or implanted anophthalmic sockets. Motility was the primary outcome, and satisfaction was measured at insertion and again three months later. Motility differed significantly across the four groups at both time points, with patients with atrophia bulbi reporting higher overall motility and satisfaction than those with implanted sockets.
why: For clinicians who fit ocular prostheses, the findings suggest custom-made prostheses and atrophia bulbi cases are associated with better movement and patient satisfaction, which can inform treatment planning and patient expectations.

headline: Cemental tear found in 0.37% of CBCT exams in retrospective Brazilian study
summary: A retrospective study of CBCT scans from 2022 to 2025 looked for cemental tear, a root surface defect, and checked about 30,865 examinations. Cemental tear was confirmed in 114 patients involving 123 teeth, an overall prevalence of 0.37%, with most cases in older adults (mean age 63.2 years). Maxillary central incisors and the middle root third were the most commonly affected sites, and root third was significantly linked to alveolar bone loss and tooth group.

headline: Pre-treatment diode laser may let dentists use less articaine for endodontic anesthesia
summary: A randomized clinical trial of 60 patients with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis in mandibular posterior teeth compared 1.8 mL of 4% articaine with epinephrine against 0.9 mL of articaine preceded by high-power diode laser irradiation at the puncture site. The laser group reported 100% anesthetic success with no supplemental anesthesia, versus 76.7% in the control group, and lower pain scores during puncture, access and instrumentation. The authors conclude the laser approach halves the required anesthetic volume while maintaining efficacy.
why: If replicated, pre-injection laser irradiation could offer a way to reduce anesthetic volume and improve comfort during root canal treatment of inflamed mandibular molars, though this is a single trial with a modest sample.

headline: Zinc-based MOF filler added to resin infiltrant shows antibacterial effects in lab study
summary: Researchers tested an experimental resin infiltrant modified with a zinc-based metal-organic framework (IRMOF-3) that was post-modified with glycidyl methacrylate to improve dispersion. Adding 5% of this filler reduced biofilm formation and improved resistance to demineralization for both L. casei and S. mutans, while the penetration coefficient stayed unchanged and the degree of conversion increased. The authors describe the filler as a promising antibacterial additive for helping arrest and manage caries.

headline: GC presents carbonate apatite bone graft research at AAP 2026 meeting
summary: GC Biomaterials took part in the 2026 American Academy of Periodontology annual meeting in Seattle, running a scientific symposium within the AAP Corporate Forum. The company gave two talks on the rationale, material properties and clinical uses of carbonate apatite-based bone grafts in periodontal and implant dentistry.

headline: Study compares smartphones and DSLR cameras for clinical dental photography
summary: Researchers in Chengdu, China, compared smartphones with digital single-lens reflex (DSLR) cameras for clinical dental photography. Earlier work had looked at individual aspects of performance rather than colour accuracy, dimensional accuracy and image quality together. The team used a standardised workflow with colour calibration and controlled magnification.
why: The results may help dentists decide which device to use for clinical photos, which affects documentation quality and equipment choices for the practice.

headline: UIC researcher studies protein DPP for possible dentin self-repair
summary: Prof. Anne George of the University of Illinois Chicago has received a grant to study dentine phosphophoryn (DPP), a protein involved in dentin mineralisation. The work builds on her team's recent findings and will examine how DPP may protect dental pulp stem cells and support their development into odontoblasts.
why: If DPP proves useful, it could eventually inform approaches that help damaged teeth repair themselves, though this project is at an early research stage with no clinical application yet.

headline: BMPR1A in periodontal ligament stem cells helps maintain periodontal bone balance
summary: A mouse study found that removing the BMP receptor BMPR1A from Gli1+ periodontal ligament stem cells caused periodontal breakdown, including alveolar bone loss, cementum defects, and disorganized collagen fibers. The loss of BMPR1A both weakened the stem cells' bone-forming ability and increased osteoclast formation, with conditioned medium from BMPR1A-deficient human cells boosting osteoclast differentiation through a higher RANKL/OPG ratio.
why: This suggests BMP signaling in periodontal ligament stem cells is a regulator of bone turnover around teeth, a basic mechanism that may matter for future periodontal therapies, though it is preclinical work in mice and cells.

headline: Delphi study yields 24 consensus recommendations for deep caries and vital pulp treatment
summary: A national modified Delphi study with 22 completing experts developed consensus recommendations for general dentists on deep and extremely deep carious lesions in permanent teeth. Starting from 29 statements, the panel reached agreement on 24 final statements, with the last three settled after an online meeting and re-rating. The output includes a clinical decision-support pathway covering pulpal assessment, selective caries removal, management by root maturity, vital pulp treatment, asepsis, biomaterials, restoration and follow-up.
why: It offers a structured, expert-agreed framework for managing deep caries and pulp-preserving care, though the authors note its feasibility and clinical outcomes still need external evaluation before wide adoption.

headline: Study examines how many arthrocentesis sessions with hyaluronic acid are needed for TMJ osteoarthritis
summary: A retrospective study of 101 adults with temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis, who had not responded to at least 6 months of conservative care, received five weekly arthrocentesis sessions with hyaluronic acid injections. Pain, chewing efficacy, functional limitation, and mouth opening were tracked before each session and at 3-month follow-up. All measures improved overall, and the session-by-session analysis suggested that some improvements appeared after fewer than five sessions, leading the authors to call for more individualized protocols with fewer interventions.
why: For dentists treating TMJ osteoarthritis with injections, this suggests the standard five-session course may not be necessary for every patient, which could reduce chair time and treatment burden, though the study is retrospective and observational.

headline: Cerebrospinal fluid leak during infratemporal fossa clearance for buccal carcinoma
summary: A case report describes an intraoperative cerebrospinal fluid leak during compartmental infratemporal fossa resection, performed as en-bloc removal of a buccal mucosa carcinoma with the fossa's contents. The authors say this complication has not been documented before, and they supported their observations with a cadaveric correlation. The report also discusses management of such leaks and intraoperative considerations in this region.
why: Surgeons and oral oncology teams treating advanced buccal cancers with deep infratemporal fossa involvement should be aware that dural or CSF leakage is a possible intraoperative risk of this approach.

headline: Proposed three-type classification guides surgery for temporomandibular joint CPPD disease
summary: A single-center case series of 10 surgically treated patients proposed sorting temporomandibular joint calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease into three types by lesion location and extent. Treatment was complete excision with reconstruction using autologous tissue or alloplastic materials. Mouth opening and pain improved at a mean follow-up of 25.1 months, with no recurrence reported.
why: For clinicians who see TMJ pain or restricted opening, this offers a possible framework for categorizing CPPD cases, though the small sample of 10 patients limits how far the outcomes can be generalized.

headline: OT bridge shows more screw loosening than multi-unit angled abutments at molar implants
summary: An in vitro study compared screw loosening in 3-unit implant-supported partial dentures using an OT bridge abutment versus a multi-unit angled abutment on a tilted implant in a mandibular model. Screw stability at the premolar site was similar between the two systems, but the OT bridge showed significantly greater screw loosening and retentive torque loss at the second molar site. Cyclic loading did not significantly cause loosening within either group.
why: When an implant must be tilted at the molar region, the choice of abutment system may affect screw stability, so clinicians may want to monitor these high-stress sites closely.

headline: Quercetin and bioactive glass toothpaste reduces dentin erosive-abrasive wear in vitro
summary: An in vitro study tested experimental fluoride toothpastes containing quercetin and bioactive glass against erosion-abrasion on enamel and dentin over a 7-day cycling protocol. The toothpastes were stable, alkaline, and biocompatible with gingival fibroblasts. The formulation with 0.075 wt% quercetin and 4 wt% bioactive glass best reduced dentin lesion depth and preserved the demineralized organic matrix, while enamel protection was comparable to the fluoride base and commercial controls.
why: This suggests a fluoride toothpaste with quercetin and bioactive glass could be a future adjunct for dentin erosive wear, though the findings are laboratory-based and not yet tested clinically.

headline: Long-term crestal bone levels stable around implants restored by digital or conventional workflows
summary: This retrospective follow-up of 65 microthreaded, platform-switched implants in 38 patients, observed for roughly 5 to 11.6 years, compared peri-implant crestal bone levels across restorative workflows. Of 128 evaluable implant surfaces, 87.5% showed either radiographic improvement or stable bone, and results were similar for digital and conventional impressions. The authors did not run statistical comparisons and describe the links to abutment type and splinting as exploratory.
why: Suggests that digital impressions did not compromise long-term bone levels around implants in this small cohort, though the study cannot prove equivalence or isolate the effect of individual restorative choices.

headline: Review examines ambient AI for dental clinical documentation and its limited evidence base
summary: This narrative review looks at ambient AI, which passively captures clinician-patient conversations and generates structured records, as a way to reduce documentation workload in dentistry. The authors drew mainly on broader healthcare studies and a small number of dental studies of AI-assisted speech recognition. They found no published studies that specifically evaluated fully ambient AI documentation systems in routine dental practice.
why: Ambient AI may eventually ease charting burden and improve workflow, but its benefits for dental practice remain unproven and should not drive adoption until dental-specific clinical validation is available.

headline: Enamel matrix derivative in extraction sockets boosts early soft tissue healing
summary: A randomized human study of 20 single-rooted tooth extractions compared sockets filled with a collagen hemostat alone against sockets filled with the same hemostat embedded with enamel matrix derivative (EMD). After 4 weeks, tissue samples taken at implant placement showed thicker epithelium and lamina propria, more blood vessel area, and higher VEGF immunostaining in the EMD group.
why: Adding EMD to an extraction socket may speed early gum healing by promoting blood vessel formation, though this small study only examined early-stage healing at 4 weeks and does not show clinical outcomes.

headline: Galimplant expands into Belgium, Netherlands and Luxembourg
summary: Spanish implant manufacturer Galimplant, founded in 2007, is extending its European presence to Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg. The company showed its implant range and ran clinical lectures at Dentex 2026 in Belgium in October. Dental Tribune also interviewed company representatives and clinicians about growth plans, clinical protocols and implant planning.
why: Dentists in the Benelux region may see more local access to this implant brand and related clinical education, though the excerpt gives no details on products, pricing or availability.

headline: Lyon College Dental School Holds First Give Veterans a Smile Event
summary: The Lyon College School of Dental Medicine hosted its first "Give Veterans a Smile" event on Nov. 10 at its Little Rock campus, offering free preventive care to veterans.
