About 80 dental students took part, along with the school's faculty and staff. Services included screening exams, fluoride treatments, oral hygiene instruction, toothbrushes, and hygiene goodie bags, and veterans also received vouchers toward future care at the school.

headline: Aspen Dental's Day of Service Gives Free Care to Over 6,400 Veterans
summary: Doctors and team members at Aspen Dental-branded practices provided free dental care valued at more than $2.8 million to more than 6,400 veterans in one day, the most patients in the event's history. Visits focused on urgent needs such as fillings, extractions, and denture repairs. Veterans identified as candidates for full-arch implants will be evaluated at participating ClearChoice centers, which will donate up to $1 million in treatment.
why: It shows how large-scale charity events and the Healthy Mouth Movement commitment may create referral and volunteer opportunities for practices, while also highlighting urgent-care approaches for veteran patients.

headline: Angelalign unveils six clear aligner innovations slated for 2027
summary: Angelalign Technology announced six new clinical innovations aimed at complex orthodontic cases. They include a SuperElastic (MC-SE) aligner material that will launch once registrations are received, an Adapt-MA System for growth guidance in young patients, and a DeepBite Solution with expanded indications. The company also described pressure points and trimlines meant to improve force expression and aligner contact.
why: Orthodontists and general practices referring complex cases may gain new aligner options for deep bite, growth guidance, and tooth control, though some items depend on regulatory approvals.

headline: Kristi M. Soileau Installed as AAP President for 2026–2027
summary: The American Academy of Periodontology has installed New Orleans periodontist Kristi M. Soileau as its president for the 2026–2027 term, starting at the AAP Annual Meeting in Seattle. Dr. Soileau is a board-certified periodontist in private practice who has held leadership roles in several dental associations and served on ADA councils. She also teaches part-time in the periodontal postdoctoral program at the LSU School of Dentistry.
why: A periodontist with a long record in clinical care, dental education, and leadership now heads the AAP, which may shape the academy's priorities for periodontal care over the coming year.

headline: Aligners Symposium 2026 to cover digital workflows and biomechanics online
summary: A free online continuing education event, the aligners Symposium 2026, will take place on 20 November on the DT Study Club platform. It will focus on digital workflows, materials and biomechanics in clear aligner therapy, especially treatment planning and complex cases. Seven expert-led sessions are planned for orthodontists and general dentists.
why: Dentists interested in clear aligner treatment can attend a free online CE event to learn about planning and managing complex cases, which may help them widen the options they offer patients.

headline: Comparing pulp cap materials after pulpotomy in primary molars
summary: A randomised split-mouth trial compared ProRoot MTA, Biodentine and TotalFill BC RRM Putty as pulp caps after pulpotomy in primary molars. MTA is well established for this use, but its handling demands and cost have led clinicians to look at other calcium silicate-based materials. The researchers reported notable differences between the materials in application time and treatment cost.
why: For pediatric dentists, the study suggests application time and cost may be practical factors when choosing a pulp capping material for primary molar pulpotomy.

headline: Angelalign's Dai Feng on the Company's U.S. Expansion and Strategy
summary: In a podcast episode, host Alison Werner talks with Dai Feng, executive chairman of Angelalign Technology and co-founder of CareCapital, about the clear aligner maker's approach. The discussion covers its origins under orthodontic professors, its focus on complex extraction cases early on, and its U.S. push, including local support teams and a Wisconsin manufacturing plant slated to start in early 2027. Feng also addresses patent challenges common in the litigious aligner market.

headline: YouGov Survey for TheraBreath Finds Gaps in Americans' Oral Care Routines
summary: A nationally representative YouGov survey commissioned by TheraBreath found that most U.S. adults call their oral care routine consistent, yet 84% skip at least one tested habit. Flossing was the most often skipped (45%), followed by tongue cleaning, mouthrinse use, and brushing before bed. Dentists and dental hygienists were named as the most trusted source for product recommendations by 61% of respondents, while 2% chose social media or influencers.
why: Patients appear to rely on dental teams for product guidance, so clear, manageable routine recommendations built on what patients already do may be more useful than long lists of changes.

headline: Graphy finishes EU MDR review for five dental 3D printing materials
summary: Graphy Inc has completed the final conformity assessment under the EU Medical Device Regulation for five of its dental 3D printing materials, and it is now waiting for the certificates to be issued. The materials include three TeraHarz Clear products and two TeraHarz products. The company already holds US FDA 510(k) clearance and registration in Brazil, and it plans to use the European certification to strengthen supply and local partnerships in the region.
why: For dentists using or considering 3D printed resins, this signals that these materials may soon be available through European channels under the stricter EU device rules, though certification has not yet been issued.

headline: Oral Biolife Receives NIH Grant to Study Peri-Implantitis Treatment
summary: Oral Biolife, a biotechnology company developing a piezoelectric regenerative platform for new bone formation, has received a National Institutes of Health grant through the National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research. The funding will support research into whether its technology can serve as a non-surgical treatment for peri-implantitis, with Temple University's Ronaldo Santana, DMD, as principal investigator.
why: If the research supports the approach, it could offer dentists a less invasive option for bone loss around implants, a condition that can otherwise lead to implant failure and often requires surgery.

headline: ADA to Host Live Webinar on Infection Control and OSHA Requirements
summary: The American Dental Association will hold a live continuing education webinar on December 3, running from 5 to 8 pm CST. Titled "Infection Control and OSHA: What Every Team Member Must Know and Do," it will review OSHA bloodborne pathogens rules, CDC recommendations for dental settings, and guidance from other professional groups. Topics include sterilization, instrument reprocessing, waterline management, environmental cleaning, personal protective equipment, and administrative controls.
why: The course offers three CE credits for dental teams seeking to meet compliance standards and reduce risks to patients and staff, though it falls outside the standard ADA CE subscription; a 10% early registration discount runs through November 18.

headline: Free flaps for osteoradionecrosis show 10% failure and 6% recurrence in meta-analysis
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 30 studies (851 patients, 896 microvascular free flap reconstructions) assessed flap surgery for osteoradionecrosis of the head and neck. The pooled flap failure rate was 10% and the pooled ORN recurrence rate was 6%, with a mean follow-up of 35.8 months. The authors judged the certainty of evidence to be very low because the included evidence was mostly retrospective and heterogeneous.
why: Microvascular free flaps remain a useful option for jaw osteoradionecrosis that improves function, but flap survival is more variable than in general head and neck reconstruction, so case selection and counseling should reflect that uncertainty.

headline: Light beam profile and photoinitiator choice drive uneven cure in experimental composites
summary: This lab study tested experimental filled resin composites with different photoinitiators (CQ, TPO, or both, at varying concentrations) cured by two LED light-curing units using homogenising and non-homogenising tips. The researchers mapped light transmission, temperature and degree of conversion across the specimens, both after curing and in real time. Cure was uneven, with peripheral conversion lower than central conversion in nearly all combinations, and the unevenness was reduced only in materials with combined photoinitiators cured using homogenous beam profiles.
why: Central measurements of light transmission, temperature and cure may miss local under-curing at the edges of large restorations, so matching the light unit's output to the photoinitiator system and using even beam profiles may matter for restoration longevity.

headline: Non-isothermal sintering boosts zirconia strength and shortens processing time
summary: Researchers compared conventional sintering, which holds zirconia at temperature for two hours, with a non-isothermal protocol that has no hold time, across three yttria-stabilized zirconia compositions. The non-isothermal method at higher temperatures reached densification similar to conventional sintering, produced more tetragonal phase and smaller grains, and significantly increased flexural strength. Translucency was unchanged for 3YSZ but lower for 4YSZ and 5YSZ.
why: Dropping the dwell time could let labs produce stronger zirconia restorations faster, though 4YSZ and 5YSZ lose some translucency, so shade-critical cases may still call for the conventional approach.

headline: Bulk-fill and incremental placement perform similarly in Class II thermoviscous composite restorations at 2 years
summary: A randomized split-mouth trial compared incremental and bulk-fill placement of thermoviscous resin composites in paired Class II restorations in 30 patients. After 2 years, 25 patients (50 restorations) were recalled, and no statistically significant differences were found between techniques on any measured parameter. Minor fractures in two restorations per group were repaired, and overall success was 95.9% for both techniques.
why: This suggests bulk-fill placement with thermoviscous composites can be a viable alternative to incremental placement in Class II restorations, though the 2-year results come from a small sample with dropout.

headline: Neutrophil extracellular traps linked to peri-implant bone loss in rat model
summary: Researchers examined clinical peri-implantitis specimens and a rat model to test whether neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) drive peri-implant bone loss. NET-related markers were higher in diseased specimens and tracked with inflammatory cytokines, and local DNase I treatment reduced bone resorption and inflammation in rats. The study also identified pro-inflammatory macrophages as an upstream population that promoted NET formation via a MIF-CD74-p38 MAPK pathway.
why: This points to NET formation as a possible contributor to inflammatory bone loss around implants and to macrophage-neutrophil signalling as a future immunomodulatory target, though the evidence so far comes from animal and in vitro work.

headline: exocad releases DentalCAD 3.3 Chemnitz service release 2 with expanded AI features
summary: Exocad, an Align Technology company, has released DentalCAD 3.3 Chemnitz service release 2, which adds to the software's artificial intelligence capabilities. A main addition is batch submission for AI Design, its AI-powered crown design service, letting users send several cases at once directly from the DentalDB case management interface.

headline: Osstem Europe Meeting 2026 opens in Prague with over 1,000 attendees
summary: The Osstem Europe Meeting 2026 began at the Prague Congress Centre, drawing more than 1,000 participants. The two-day event, organised by Osstem Europe with the Osstem Implant Scientific Community Europe, focuses on scientific exchange and clinical education under the theme "Mastering the unexpected: Pathways from complications to predictable success."

headline: Oral health may flag metabolic risk, linked to periodontitis and diabetes research
summary: Ahead of World Diabetes Day, which promotes prevention, early diagnosis and management, Dental Tribune spoke with researcher Dr João Botelho. He discussed an international study suggesting that oral health could serve as useful indicators of metabolic risk. The campaign theme this year, "Early action on diabetes," emphasizes identifying people at risk of Type 2 diabetes.
why: Dentists may be able to use oral health findings as an early signal for patients who could be at risk of Type 2 diabetes, though the excerpt does not detail how this would work in practice.

headline: Five Questions Dentists Should Ask Their Financial Advisor
summary: A financial planner writes that many dentists hand their retirement savings to advisors recommended by friends or colleagues and rarely review their accounts closely. He cites FINRA year-end 2025 figures showing 625 new disciplinary cases and fines and disgorgement up 31.7% to $99.6 million. The piece introduces five questions to ask an advisor, starting with the advisor's credentials, such as whether they are a fee-based fiduciary.
why: Dentists who rely on a referred financial planner without understanding fees, performance, or credentials could lose substantial money over their careers, so checking the advisor's qualifications matters for long-term financial security.

headline: Microlux DW Illuminator Aims to Spot Caries, Cracks, and Biofilm
summary: The Microlux DW Illuminator is a dental diagnostic device that uses dual wavelengths and is described as working without X-rays or UV light. Its white-light transillumination mode is meant to show caries and cracks, while its fluorescence mode targets bacteria and plaque. The listed detection targets include white spot lesions, S. mutans in caries, biofilm, demineralization, and differences between composite and tooth structure.
why: For clinicians, this is a new option for visualizing caries, cracks, and plaque during exams, though the excerpt is manufacturer promotional and offers no independent performance data.

headline: Graphy Completes EU MDR Final Review for Five Dental 3D Printing Materials
summary: Graphy Inc. says five of its dental 3D printing materials have completed the final conformity assessment review under the EU Medical Device Regulation. The materials are three TeraHarz Clear products and two TeraHarz products, and the company is now waiting for the certificates to be issued. Graphy also plans to expand its European manufacturing and distribution partnerships, including with Smilers, the clear aligner brand of France-based Biotech Dental.
why: For dentists using or considering direct 3D-printed aligner materials, the EU MDR review signals that these resins meet stricter European requirements for clinical evidence, documentation and quality management, though certification is not yet final.

headline: Curve Dental Names Nat Harrison Senior Vice President of Marketing
summary: Curve Dental, an AI-powered, cloud-native dental practice management software company, has appointed Nat Harrison as senior vice president of marketing. He will lead marketing strategy as the company expands its all-in-one platform, which it is backing with a $200 million R&D commitment. Harrison previously was vice president of B2B marketing at Mindbody and held marketing roles at Wayfair Professional.
why: For practice owners, this is a leadership change at a dental software vendor that is putting significant investment into AI and integrated tools for clinical care, payments and operations.

headline: CareQuest and Henry Schein Launch BRIDGE Health Network for Dental-Medical Integration
summary: CareQuest Institute for Oral Health and Henry Schein, Inc. announced the BRIDGE Health Network, a group of providers across varied geographies and care settings focused on linking dentistry and medicine. Initial pilots will add workflows to collect vital signs, lifestyle markers, and chairside point-of-care screenings, including HbA1c testing, during routine hygiene visits. The excerpt notes that 80% of people with prediabetes and 28% of people with diabetes are unaware of their condition, and that chairside A1C screening identified elevated levels in over 11% of previously undiagnosed type 2 diabetes patients and an additional 47% with prediabetes.
why: Dental hygiene visits may become a practical place to screen patients for systemic risks like diabetes and to refer them for medical follow-up, which could change how dental teams handle chairside testing and medical coordination.

headline: Envista Prices $430 Million Senior Notes Offering Due 2033
summary: Envista Holdings has priced $430 million in 6.250% Senior Notes due 2033 at 99.482% of principal. The offering is expected to close around November 24, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Proceeds will go toward repaying its U.S. dollar term loan A facility and for general corporate purposes.
why: Envista, the parent of dental brands such as Dentsply-adjacent implant and orthodontic lines, is refinancing debt, which signals its financial position and may affect pricing and supplier stability for practices that buy from it.

headline: Align Technology to Speak at 2026 Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference
summary: Align Technology announced that its executives are scheduled to speak at the 2026 Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference in London on November 17, 2026, during an 8:30 to 8:55 AM GMT slot. The presentation will be webcast live on Align's investor relations website, with an archived replay available for about one month. CEO Joe Hogan, CFO John Morici, and Shirley Stacy will be presenting.
why: This is an investor-focused appearance by the maker of Invisalign, iTero scanners, and exocad software, so it offers little direct practice guidance but may signal the company's financial outlook for the clear aligner and digital dentistry market.

headline: Flex Dental Redesigns FlexVerification Insurance Checks for Open Dental Users
summary: Flex Dental Solutions has introduced a redesigned FlexVerification tool for Open Dental that automates eligibility and benefits checks. Its new VerifySync review step lets front desk staff compare insurance portal responses with existing Open Dental data and choose which fields to update. The release also adds connection alerts for portal login problems and a single queue showing each patient's review status.
why: Front desk staff can automate insurance checks while keeping control over what changes in patient records, which may help offices prepare for the January benefit resets.

headline: Patients favor CBCT over periapical radiography in endodontic assessment
summary: A cross-sectional study of 117 patients referred for endodontic assessment compared cone-beam CT with periapical radiography and surveyed their perceptions and radiation knowledge. Most patients rated CBCT as more useful than periapical radiographs and reported greater confidence in their treatment plans and trust in clinicians. Baseline knowledge of ionizing radiation was limited, with 59% rating their understanding as poor or very poor.
why: Patients in this study valued CBCT's diagnostic benefits over its radiation risks and would accept it for future care, but clinicians should explain both the advantages and radiation risks during consent.

headline: Human Review Essential When Orthodontic Practices Use AI for Patient Messages
summary: An opinion piece argues that AI can speed up orthodontic consultation summaries, insurance claim narratives, and follow-up messages, but needs careful human review. Unchecked AI drafts may leave out important conditions, invent treatment details, or promise outcomes the orthodontist never approved. The author outlines five tips for using AI safely, starting with three routine documentation workflows.
why: Practices adopting AI for patient communications and billing should assign a named clinical or billing reviewer to check every draft, since errors can cause reimbursement problems and damage credibility.

headline: Acid reflux far more common in infants with Pierre Robin sequence than isolated cleft palate
summary: A retrospective cohort study of 118 children who had preoperative 24-hour pH monitoring between 1988 and 2017 found gastroesophageal reflux disease in 61.3% of those with Pierre Robin sequence, compared with 16.1% of those with isolated cleft palate. Reflux was defined as a reflux index above 10%. The authors concluded that children with Pierre Robin sequence should receive systematic gastroenterological evaluation.
why: Dentists and specialists treating children with cleft or Pierre Robin sequence may see feeding difficulties linked to reflux, supporting coordination with gastroenterology before and around surgery.

headline: Intraosseous lipoma of the mandibular condyle causing progressive jaw deviation: case report
summary: A case report describes a 55-year-old woman with a 10-year history of worsening mandibular deviation caused by an intraosseous lipoma of the right condyle. The lesion appeared as a well-defined swelling with a thinned cortex and no soft-tissue invasion, and was completely excised through a hemicoronal approach. Histology confirmed mature fat within bone, and the deviation and occlusion were corrected with no recurrence at 6 months.
why: Condylar intraosseous lipoma is extremely rare, and this report shows that such a lesion can present as slowly progressive jaw deviation and that histopathology is needed for diagnosis, which is useful when evaluating long-standing condylar swelling or asymmetry.

headline: Cantilevers Raise Bone Loss and Stress in Mandibular Implant-Supported Prostheses
summary: A study combined a retrospective clinical review of 17 patients with finite element analysis of 32 simulated mandibular models to compare fixed implant-supported prostheses with and without cantilevers. Both clinical groups had high 3-year implant survival, but the cantilever group had significantly greater marginal bone loss. Simulations found distal cantilevers increased peri-implant stress and strain, and zirconia frameworks reduced stress more than polymethyl methacrylate.
why: For edentulous mandible cases, avoiding long distal cantilevers may limit marginal bone loss, and a six-implant design with a short cantilever may be a better option than a highly tilted four-implant setup when posterior bone is deficient.

headline: Surface layer affects remineralization of artificial enamel caries by three agents
summary: Researchers induced artificial caries in 80 extracted human premolars using a lactic acid buffer, creating lesions of 48 or 72 hours, and then treated them with a rosin-based fluoride varnish, a water-based fluoride agent, a self-assembling peptide agent, or artificial saliva as a control before 12 pH-cycles. Micro-CT and OCT were used to measure demineralization depth, reflectivity, lesion depth and mineral gain. The 72-hour lesions had a distinct surface layer while the 48-hour lesions did not, and the surface layer significantly affected outcomes for the peptide agent and rosin-based fluoride but not the water-based fluoride.
why: Whether early white spot lesions have a surface layer may influence how well a remineralizing agent works, so the choice of product could depend on lesion characteristics, though this is an in vitro study on extracted teeth.

headline: Barriers to fluoride caries prevention in German nursing homes identified in qualitative study
summary: A qualitative study based on the Theoretical Domains Framework interviewed nursing staff, residents and dentists from five nursing homes in Krefeld, Germany, about implementing fluoride-based caries prevention. Participants reported barriers such as limited fluoride-specific knowledge and training, uncertainty about application and dosage, unclear responsibilities, unreliable product supply, uncertain financing, weak dental-nursing communication, and little fluoride-specific documentation. Fluoride products were often used only as part of general oral care rather than as planned, monitored preventive measures.
why: It suggests that dentists working with nursing homes may need to offer fluoride-specific guidance, clarify who does what, and coordinate closely with care staff to make preventive fluoride routine for residents.

headline: Intraoral scanners show moderate accuracy for detecting caries in systematic review
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 22 studies pooled diagnostic results for intraoral scanner-assisted caries detection and compared them with conventional methods. Sensitivity was moderate overall and higher for occlusal than approximal surfaces, while specificity was higher in clinical studies. No statistically significant differences were found between intraoral scanners and conventional methods.
why: Intraoral scanners may help monitor early caries lesions and could reduce radiation exposure, but their limited sensitivity means they cannot replace conventional diagnosis or serve as a reliable standalone screening tool.

headline: Delivering Better Oral Health's fourth edition flags research gaps in prevention
summary: The fourth version of Delivering Better Oral Health, a guideline on prevention now available as an online digital resource, has been reviewed to identify priority areas for further research. These cover dental caries, oral cancer, periodontal disease, tooth wear and behaviour change. The authors suggest national research funding should ideally target these areas within an integrated plan.
why: Dentists may see future guidance on caries, periodontal disease, tooth wear and oral cancer prevention shaped by these identified evidence gaps, and national funding may follow these priorities.

headline: Review reframes antimicrobial resistance in dentistry across past, present and future
summary: A British Dental Journal article examines antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in dentistry through historical, current and future perspectives, from the penicillin era to modern stewardship. It analyses dental prescribing patterns using English surveillance data for 2023-2024 and explores options such as rapid diagnostics, microbiome restoration and non-antibiotic therapies. The authors argue AMR is a microbial ecological imbalance driven by industrialisation and antibiotic overuse, not only a clinical problem.
why: Dentistry is cited as contributing roughly 10% of antibiotic prescriptions worldwide, often for conditions where they offer limited benefit, so prescribing restraint and stewardship are directly relevant to everyday practice.

headline: UK nations' NHS dental systems have diverged since devolution, study finds
summary: A British Dental Journal paper compares how England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland plan, commission and deliver NHS dental care since health policy was devolved in the late 1990s. It describes three contract models: target-driven in England, fee-per-item in Scotland and Northern Ireland, and a shift toward needs-based care packages in Wales. The authors report that Scotland and Wales run strong national oral health programmes, while England relies on local initiatives and Northern Ireland faces capacity limits in dental public health.
why: Dentists working under NHS contracts should understand that payment and contract structures differ across the UK, and these differences shape prevention focus, access and workforce pressures in each nation.

headline: Community-based child oral health programmes compared across the four UK nations
summary: A British Dental Journal article gives a descriptive overview of the main community-based (midstream) child oral health programmes in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. It looks at the challenges and opportunities of each approach and the policy framework each operates within. Cross-party political support and integration with early years services were common facilitators, while funding sustainability and workforce capacity were challenges.
why: It shows which community-level approaches have support and which strain resources, which can inform how dental teams work with early years services and local programmes.

headline: Dental public health's role in health protection, with case studies from England
summary: This narrative overview in the British Dental Journal describes how dental public health specialists contribute to health protection across the UK. It presents two case studies: specialist leadership during the COVID-19 pandemic response, and the management of a dental practice with infection prevention and control concerns. The authors conclude that these specialists provide clinical and system leadership that enables coordinated action across organisations.
why: It shows how dental public health specialists can be called on to help manage infection control failures and system-level incidents that affect practices, patients and staff.

headline: Public health review calls for systemic reform of the UK oral health workforce
summary: A British Dental Journal paper takes a public health view of how to build a sustainable oral health workforce in the UK, looking at need, demand and supply through the lens of sociological theory on professions. It notes that the UK has more dental professionals than ever and a varied skill mix, yet access to dental care is limited and adult disease levels are rising. The authors argue that a sustainable workforce needs systems redesign, workforce development, and a focus on prevention, equity, and leadership.
why: It suggests that adding more dental staff alone will not solve access and disease problems, so practices and policymakers may need to rethink how the workforce is organised and used.

headline: Oral health challenges of older adults call for prevention and integrated care
summary: This Br Dent J paper reviews the oral health challenges facing older people in the UK and Republic of Ireland, where the over-65 share of the population is projected to reach 25% by 2050. It notes that older adults have a high prevalence of dental disease, that most are now dentate or partially dentate with heavy repair and replacement needs, and that recent studies and training initiatives aimed at promoting oral health in this group are summarized.
why: Dentists will see a growing older patient base with complex restorative needs, and the paper argues that a shift from treatment toward prevention across the life course, plus better domiciliary care and inter-professional working, is needed.

headline: Consultants in dental public health drive change in complex English systems
summary: A British Dental Journal article describes how consultants in dental public health turn national policy and evidence into local action to reduce oral health inequalities in England. It presents three case studies: dental services equity audits in the West Midlands, oral cancer prevention in the North West, and water fluoridation expansion in the North East. The authors argue these consultants combine clinical dental credibility with population health expertise to align NHS dental commissioning, local authority prevention and wider health pathways.
why: It shows how dental public health leaders shape commissioning and prevention programmes that can affect access to services and the local context in which general practices work.

headline: Hospitals Rarely Post Discounted Cash Prices for Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
summary: A cross-sectional study of hospital price transparency data examined nine elective oral and maxillofacial surgery procedures. Of 7,319 hospitals, 2,717 reported a price for at least one of them, and nearly all of those reported insurer-negotiated rates, while only about one in five reported a discounted cash price. Discounted cash prices were far more common for professional fees than for facility fees, and were less likely for dental extractions and implant or ridge augmentation than for orthognathic procedures.
why: Patients paying out of pocket for dental-related surgery may struggle to find upfront cash prices, which could make cost discussions with them harder for practices and surgical teams.

headline: Pre-extubation bupivacaine infiltration lowers pain and opioid use after orthognathic surgery
summary: A randomized controlled trial at Başkent University in Ankara compared bimaxillary orthognathic surgery patients who received extra bupivacaine/epinephrine infiltration before extubation with those who did not. Of 108 patients assessed, 102 were randomized (51 per group), and pain scores were recorded out to 48 hours. The treated group had significantly lower visual analog pain scores at every time point and used less rescue and total morphine.
why: This suggests a simple, low-cost adjunct to multimodal analgesia could reduce pain and opioid needs for patients undergoing bimaxillary orthognathic procedures, though it is a single trial from one center.

headline: Scoping review finds wide variation in oral hypofunction prevalence among older adults
summary: This scoping review pooled 15 studies on oral hypofunction, an intermediate stage between oral frailty and oral dysfunction, in older adults. Most included studies came from East Asia and used variations of the Japanese Society of Gerodontology seven-item checklist, with reported prevalence ranging from 14.3% to 95.5%. The authors found the evidence lacked uniform diagnostic criteria and longitudinal data, and called for standardized criteria and longer-term research.
why: Dentists screening older patients may see large differences in how oral hypofunction is defined and measured, so standardized screening tools and longer-term evidence are needed before its links to malnutrition, frailty and cognitive decline can be relied on in care planning.

headline: Dynamic computer-guided implant surgery shows high accuracy in edentulous private-practice patients
summary: A retrospective cohort study of 107 fully edentulous patients (500 implants) treated with dynamic computer-assisted implant surgery in a private practice between June 2020 and September 2025 compared planned and actual implant positions using superimposed CBCT scans. Mean angular deviation was 1.87°, with platform and apex deviations of about 1.06 mm and 1.07 mm. Older age, maxillary location, anterior region, post-extraction sites, and pterygoid implants were associated with greater deviation.
why: It supports dynamic navigation as a reliable option for fully edentulous cases in general practice, and flags maxillary, anterior, post-extraction, and pterygoid sites as areas needing closer planning attention.

headline: Multimodal AI models show uneven skill reading dental radiographs
summary: Researchers tested six general-purpose multimodal large language models and two clinicians on 27 radiograph interpretation tasks covering periapical, panoramic, and lateral cephalometric images. The models did relatively well on some visually obvious findings, such as root fillings and restorations, but struggled with low-contrast findings, spatial localization, and prediction or decision-making tasks. Only 6 of the 27 tasks showed significant differences between models, and no model showed a broad advantage.
why: These results suggest general-purpose AI image tools are not yet reliable for dental radiograph interpretation without clinician oversight, and the error types identified (false positives from artifacts, missed low-contrast lesions, localization mistakes) are worth keeping in mind when evaluating any AI diagnostic aid.

headline: Meta-analysis finds AI-assisted restoration design inconclusive versus conventional CAD
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis compared AI-assisted and conventional CAD software for designing dental restorations, covering 28 eligible studies, 10 of which were pooled. The pooled design time difference was not statistically significant, and accuracy results showed high heterogeneity. Evidence was mostly from in vitro studies, and the authors judged it inconclusive on restoration quality, though AI designs were generally clinically acceptable with technician refinement still helpful.
why: AI design tools may save some design time, but the evidence does not yet show they match conventional CAD in fit or morphology, so clinicians should still plan on technician review of AI-generated restorations.

headline: Narrative review looks at oral and salivary signs of hantavirus infection
summary: A recent narrative review examines the oral and salivary features of hantavirus infections, an area that dental research has largely overlooked compared with the well-documented systemic effects. The paper covers oral symptoms and the role of oral secretions in transmission. It also discusses saliva-based diagnostics and how dental professionals might recognise signs of infection and manage affected patients.
why: Dentists may need to recognise possible oral signs of hantavirus and understand whether oral secretions play a part in spread, which could affect infection-control and patient-triage decisions in the practice.

headline: Journal of Endodontics collection of 15 papers examines regenerative endodontics
summary: A set of 15 papers in the November 2026 issue of the Journal of Endodontics covers stem cells, regenerative therapies, inflammation, and emerging approaches to pulp preservation and regeneration. The papers come from the 2025 Pulp Biology and Regeneration Group Symposium and look at how researchers might preserve or regenerate inflamed or lost pulp tissue. AAE President W. Craig Noblett said the work reflects a shift toward preserving tooth vitality and more personalized care.
why: The research points toward biological and regenerative options that could help dentists keep more natural teeth alive, though the excerpt describes early research rather than ready-to-use treatments.

headline: vVARDIS prices IPO at $18 per share ahead of NYSE debut
summary: vVARDIS Holding AG, a Swiss company in dental med-tech, priced its initial public offering of 9,722,223 Class A shares at $18.00 each. The shares are expected to trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol VVVV starting November 13, 2026, with closing expected around November 16, 2026. Underwriters also hold a 30-day option to buy up to 1,458,333 additional shares to cover over-allotments.

headline: Innovate 32 Partners With Houston's Post Oak Dental
summary: Nashville-based dental services organization Innovate 32 has announced a partnership with Post Oak Dental, a general and cosmetic practice in Houston's Uptown area. Dr. Chris Gowan, who has over 30 years of experience, will continue to lead the practice's clinical direction and patient care. The deal adds to Innovate 32's existing Houston presence and its network across the Southeast, Midwest, and Texas.
why: This is another example of dental service organizations acquiring or partnering with established private practices, while the clinicians keep clinical leadership, which may matter for dentists weighing partnership options.

headline: Aspen Dental Opens Independently Owned Office in Willis, Texas
summary: Aspen Dental has opened a new office at 12250 Interstate 45 N in Willis, Texas, serving Willis, Panorama Village, northern Conroe, and the Lake Conroe area. The independently owned practice is led by Anthony Spates, DMD, a former oral and maxillofacial surgery fellow, and offers general, restorative, implant, and emergency dental care, with written cost estimates and third-party financing for larger plans. The excerpt also cites U.S. Census Bureau figures showing Willis's population grew about 19% from April 2020 to July 2025.
why: For dentists, this is another example of independent multi-location ownership expanding into fast-growing suburban markets, and it highlights demand for implant, extraction, and same-day emergency services.

headline: Hannover Medical School completes upgrade of dental simulation facilities
summary: Hannover Medical School (MHH) in Germany has finished modernising and expanding its dental simulation facilities. The two simulation rooms now offer 92 digital training units, funded by more than €13 million from the state of Lower Saxony.
why: It shows dental schools investing in digital workflow and simulated clinical training, which may shape how future dentists are prepared before treating patients.

headline: Crest Gum Detoxify toothpaste adds hops-derived compounds to stannous fluoride
summary: A new Crest Gum Detoxify formulation pairs stabilized stannous fluoride with hops-derived β-acids, which are intended to disrupt the protective biofilm matrix in the mouth. The article examines the science behind the product, its possible role in biofilm management, and what dental professionals should know about clinical use.

headline: Angelalign Unveils Six Clinical Innovations, Most Slated for 2027
summary: Angelalign Technology has announced six clinical innovations for North American doctors, including new aligner materials, a mandibular advancement tool for growth guidance, a DeepBite solution, and iPlan planning software. Most are preannounced for 2027, while the Halo retention system is available now. The SuperElastic (MC-SE) material will be offered pending appropriate registrations.

headline: Oral microbiota around zirconia implants in reconstructed jaws compared with natural teeth
summary: A prospective observational study of 10 patients with vascularized bone flap jaw reconstruction (six fibula, four deep circumflex iliac artery flaps) compared the oral microbiome around zirconia implants with that around natural teeth. Samples were collected at 3, 6 and 12 months after implant surgery. Zirconia implants showed higher relative Streptococcus levels than teeth, and lower relative Actinomyces levels in fibula patients, while Porphyromonas gingivalis and Tannerella forsythia were more prominent around teeth in the fibula group and rose over time. By 12 months, teeth and implants did not show similar prevalence or levels of the target species.
why: Early evidence suggests zirconia implants in reconstructed jaws harbor a different peri-implant microbial profile than teeth, which is relevant to planning maintenance and monitoring in these complex cases, though the sample of 10 patients is small.

headline: Synovectomy margin method may improve intraoperative disc position check in TMJ discopexy
summary: A prospective cohort study at a tertiary referral center evaluated an objective intraoperative method for judging disc position during arthroscopic discopexy, using the relationship between the anterior synovectomy margin and the articular eminence instead of roofing evaluation. Across 131 patients (209 joints) treated with the mattress-loop (Yang) technique, every joint was judged reduced intraoperatively, and immediate postoperative MRI confirmed reduction in 207 of 209 joints. The association between the two was statistically significant (P < .001), and the authors describe the concordance as high.
why: For surgeons performing arthroscopic TMJ disc repair, this suggests a more objective intraoperative landmark may help confirm disc position than roofing assessment alone, though the study's single-center, cohort design and short-term MRI follow-up limit how far the findings can be generalized.

headline: Processed nerve allografts show high sensory recovery in trigeminal nerve repairs
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of eight observational studies (160 subjects, 164 repairs) pooled functional sensory recovery after processed peripheral nerve allograft reconstruction of trigeminal nerves. Recovery occurred in about 89.5% of repairs, with similar rates for inferior alveolar nerve-only studies and mixed inferior alveolar and lingual nerve studies. No graft-related adverse events were reported, but the certainty of evidence was graded as low.
why: For clinicians managing inferior alveolar or lingual nerve injuries, this suggests allografts may achieve sensory recovery in most cases, though the low-certainty evidence and lack of comparative or patient-reported outcome data limit firm conclusions.

headline: Longer antibiotic prophylaxis after cleft lip/palate surgery linked to no reduction in severe SSI
summary: A nationwide Japanese retrospective cohort study of 13,333 cleft lip and/or palate surgery patients compared short-term (≤2 days) and prolonged (≥3 days) postoperative antibiotic prophylaxis. Severe surgical site infection requiring debridement or reoperation was extremely rare, occurring in one patient in the prolonged group. Short-term prophylaxis was associated with a hospital stay about half a day shorter but no difference in hospitalization charges.

headline: Gene expression profiling compares symptomatic irreversible pulpitis with healthy dental pulp
summary: Researchers ran RNA sequencing on pulp tissue from patients with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis and from healthy controls having elective root canal treatment, analyzing differentially expressed genes with edgeR. Many inflammatory and angiogenesis-related genes, including IL6, TNF, ANGPT2, and VEGF-A, were upregulated in diseased pulp, while TGF-β1 and TGIF2 were downregulated. The authors suggest these genes could serve as biomarkers of disease activity and targets for future diagnostic and treatment strategies.

headline: FDA MAUDE reports on endodontic files show reporting patterns, not comparative clinical risk
summary: Researchers analysed 2,666 FDA MAUDE adverse-event reports for endodontic files filed from 2015 to 2025, grouping them into heat-treated NiTi, conventional NiTi, and manual hand files. Hand-file reports showed more injury events than heat-treated NiTi reports, but this was driven almost entirely by stainless-steel hand files. The authors conclude MAUDE cannot support alloy-level clinical-risk comparisons, and 87.2% of reports came from Dentsply-affiliated entities.
why: Adverse-event databases like MAUDE cannot reliably show whether one file type is riskier than another, so clinicians should not change instrument choice based on these reports alone.

headline: Bioactive glass hydrogels show promise in protecting enamel and dentin from erosion
summary: Researchers built bio-adhesive hydrogels containing bioactive glass nanoparticles in sodium carboxymethyl cellulose or carbomer and tested them against erosion of enamel and dentin. The hydrogels stayed colloidally stable, were non-cytotoxic, and cut surface loss by about 80% compared with deionized water, with protective layers forming on the tooth surface. Collagen preservation in dentin was comparable to chlorhexidine, and molecular simulations suggested the carboxymethyl cellulose version binds collagen more strongly.
why: This laboratory study suggests a bioactive glass hydrogel could give longer-lasting erosion protection than a rinse-off suspension, but it has not been tested clinically, so it does not change current practice yet.

headline: Smartphone 3D reconstruction of dental models less accurate than dental scanners
summary: Researchers benchmarked a sparse-view smartphone workflow for digitising dental models against an intraoral scanner and an extraoral scanner, using coordinate measuring machine measurements as the reference under the ISO 20896-1:2019 protocol. Images captured with an iPhone 15 Pro were reconstructed using 3D Gaussian Splatting and Neural Surface Reconstruction. The intraoral scanner was the most accurate, followed by the extraoral scanner, while the smartphone methods showed deviations of roughly 200 to 300 µm.
why: Smartphone-based reconstruction is not yet precise enough for high-precision prosthodontic work such as crowns and inlays, so dedicated scanners remain the standard, though the approach may suit less demanding clinical or teaching uses.

headline: Formnext 2026 opens in Frankfurt with focus on additive manufacturing
summary: Formnext 2026, an additive manufacturing trade event, opens today at Messe Frankfurt and runs until 20 November. The article notes that dental AM is now established, with attention moving toward production efficiency, automation, quality and scalability. It also says Formnext now offers year-round AM information through its Industry Insights platform.

headline: Southern Orthodontic Partners Appoints Sarah Sharfstein as Chief Operating Officer
summary: Southern Orthodontic Partners, an orthodontic support organization, has named Sarah Sharfstein its Chief Operating Officer to oversee operations across its network of more than 120 practices. Sharfstein has nearly two decades of experience in orthodontics and the DSO sector, including earlier leadership roles at Align Technology and most recently as Vice President at Aspen Dental Management, where she led sales enablement and field effectiveness. CEO John Nelson said her appointment marks a new chapter for the company.
why: The hire signals continued focus on standardized, technology-enabled orthodontic practices within large DSO networks, a trend that may affect how practices in this space are managed and compete.

headline: Dr. Silverman's weekly reflection urges teams to listen more closely to patients
summary: In reflection #15 of his Tuesday column, Dr. Harvey N. Silverman looks back over 15 weeks of topics on patient conversations, hidden concerns, and the role of the team in cosmetic dentistry. He encourages readers to have their team listen more carefully to each patient, learn what they hope to change for a more self-confident smile, and look for one overlooked opportunity.

headline: Dentsply Sirona Backs Ultrasonic Instrumentation Day at Fresno City College
summary: On October 3, more than 90 attendees, including dental hygiene students and local dental professionals, gathered at Fresno City College's Dental Hygiene Clinic for an Ultrasonic Instrumentation Day with clinical education from Dentsply Sirona. The event combined a lecture, hands-on learning, and student research presentations, and extends a collaboration that started with faculty training.
why: It shows how manufacturers are partnering with dental hygiene programs to teach ultrasonic instrumentation, and it links classroom training with the local practicing community.

headline: Operation Smile and ISAPS Sign Two-Year Surgical Education Partnership
summary: Operation Smile and the International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgery (ISAPS) signed a two-year Memorandum of Understanding to collaborate on medical education and clinical capacity. The partners plan to share education programs, create training and service-learning opportunities, and expand access to surgical care in under-resourced settings, while tracking the impact of their work. Patient safety is stated to remain central to all activities.
why: This signals growing international collaboration on surgical training and access to care, though the announcement itself offers no direct change for dental practice operations.

headline: Pearl Street Dental Partners Adds Four Greater Houston Practices
summary: Texas-based dental partnership organization Pearl Street Dental Partners announced partnerships with four practices in the Greater Houston area: Conroe Comprehensive Dental Center, Montgomery Comprehensive Dental Center, Waheed Dental Professionals in Houston, and Gustafson Dental in Humble. With these additions, its network reaches 50 locations across Texas and Oklahoma and eight locations in Greater Houston. Under its joint venture model, owner-dentists keep an equity stake and continue leading clinical care.

headline: Frequent snacking linked to higher caries risk but less preventive care in dental school clinics
summary: A study using data from 9 BigMouth repository institutions reviewed adult patients examined between July 2022 and August 2023. Among 8,067 patients with complete dietary questionnaires, 30.1% reported frequent snacking, and these patients were far more likely to be rated high or extreme caries risk, even after adjusting for age, gender, race or ethnicity, and examination type. Despite this, frequent snackers were less likely to receive prophylaxis, and nutritional counseling was documented in only 7.8% of encounters.
why: Patients who snack frequently between meals show higher caries risk and disease signs, yet dietary counseling and preventive steps are rarely documented, suggesting dentists should build diet assessment into routine caries risk management.

headline: Childhood adversity linked to tooth loss and fewer dental visits in U.S. adults
summary: Using 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data from 73,537 adults across 12 states, researchers examined links between adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and oral health. Adults with one or more ACEs had higher odds of missing 6 or more teeth, with the risk rising at 4 or more ACEs. Those with 4 or more ACEs were also less likely to have visited a dentist in the past year.
why: Patients with a history of childhood adversity may have more tooth loss and less regular dental care, so clinicians may benefit from trauma-informed approaches that build safety and trust.

headline: Tutorial urges dentists to read heterogeneity in meta-analyses more carefully
summary: A narrative tutorial in the Journal of the American Dental Association explains how heterogeneity should be interpreted in dental meta-analyses, which have grown rapidly in number. It works through a hypothetical low-level laser therapy example for oral mucositis and lists six common interpretive errors. The author concludes that no single statistic is sufficient and that the prediction interval is the most clinically useful of the four statistics discussed.
why: Dentists reading pooled estimates should check heterogeneity measures together, especially the prediction interval, before assuming a treatment effect will hold across different clinical settings.

headline: Sleep deprivation worsens pulpal inflammation and repair in rats via neutrophil activity
summary: In rat studies, sleep deprivation worsened pulp inflammation and impaired healing after direct pulp capping, with incomplete bridge formation and later necrosis and apical periodontitis. In an induced pulpitis model, sleep-deprived rats showed faster inflammatory progression and more pulpal necrosis, along with higher neutrophil abundance and activation and elevated neutrophil elastase. Depleting neutrophils or inhibiting neutrophil elastase reduced inflammation and tissue damage.
why: This is animal research suggesting poor sleep may impair pulp healing and worsen inflammation, pointing to neutrophil-related pathways as a possible mechanism, but it does not yet show effects in patients or guide clinical care.

headline: Silver diamine fluoride may help young children avoid dental general anaesthesia
summary: In Germany, a large share of general anaesthesia procedures for children under 5 are done for dental reasons, and guidelines favour minimally invasive care first. Researchers at University Medicine Greifswald studied outcomes of starting caries management with silver diamine fluoride (SDF) in children referred for treatment under general anaesthesia. They report that this approach may allow restorative work to be done chairside instead.

headline: Patient-perceived donor site morbidity after fibula, scapula and iliac crest free flaps
summary: A single-site prospective cohort study at a large metropolitan hospital followed 59 head and neck reconstruction patients for over 12 months after osseous free flap harvest from the fibula, scapula, or iliac crest. Patients' own ratings of donor site function showed no significant change after scapula harvest, while fibula and iliac crest patients reported significant declines. The authors concluded that scapula harvest, especially in females, was associated with minimal perceived morbidity, iliac crest harvest caused significant morbidity beyond 12 months, and fibula results were equivocal.

headline: Orthognathic surgery does not raise screening-based OSA risk in healthy adults over one year
summary: This prospective cohort study followed 70 healthy adults undergoing orthognathic surgery for Class II or Class III dentoskeletal deformities, using sleep questionnaires before surgery and at 6 and 12 months afterward. Patients with Class II deformities, mostly treated with mandibular or bimaxillary advancement, showed a statistically significant drop in obstructive sleep apnoea risk on two questionnaires, with no significant change in daytime sleepiness. Class III patients, most of whom had bimaxillary surgery, showed no significant rise in OSA risk or daytime sleepiness.
why: For clinicians planning jaw surgery, this suggests that orthognathic procedures did not increase screening-measured sleep apnoea risk in healthy patients within one year, though the findings rely on questionnaires rather than sleep studies.

headline: Narrative review maps autonomy levels, evidence, and liability for robotics and AI in oral surgery
summary: This narrative review classifies robotic systems in oral and maxillofacial surgery by level of autonomy and evidence stage, and looks at AI surgical planning tools and their regulatory and liability issues. Dental implant placement accounts for most clinical activity. The only FDA-cleared OMS system offers haptic guidance only, while other systems that perform osteotomies and implant placement along a surgeon-approved plan are not yet FDA-cleared and have been reported in patient series; most autonomous tumor resection and orthognathic systems remain preclinical.
why: Dentists using robotic implant guidance should know that the only cleared system does not act independently, and that competency standards, guidelines, and consent language have not caught up, which may leave the operating surgeon carrying most of the legal risk.

headline: Repaired cleft lip and palate alters pterygomaxillary anatomy and separation during Le Fort I surgery
summary: A single-centre retrospective study compared 31 patients with repaired cleft lip and palate undergoing orthognathic surgery with 31 age- and deformity-matched non-cleft Class III controls. Preoperative CBCT showed thicker and wider pterygomaxillary junctions and a shorter medial pterygoid plate on both sides in the cleft group, with a greater right-side pterygomaxillary angle. Separation patterns on 1-month postoperative CBCT were similar on the right but differed on the left, with more type 4 separations in the cleft patients.
why: For dentists planning Le Fort I osteotomies in patients with repaired cleft lip and palate, the study supports detailed preoperative CBCT assessment of the pterygomaxillary region to help plan safe separation and reduce surgical risk.

headline: Concentrated growth factor and collagen fleece may speed palatal donor-site healing
summary: A randomised controlled trial of 39 patients undergoing palatal graft harvesting compared concentrated growth factor (CGF), collagen fleece (CF) and a gelatine sponge control, with 38 completing the study. Both CGF and CF groups showed faster soft-tissue normalisation, smaller wound areas in the first two weeks, lower pain scores during the first week and better patient-reported oral health outcomes than control. CGF also showed lower analgesic use during Days 4-7.
why: For clinicians performing palatal grafts, these materials may offer a way to reduce donor-site pain and speed early wound closure, though the small sample and short-term follow-up limit how far the findings can be applied.

headline: Spatial transcriptomics reveals uneven inflammation and epithelial differences in peri-implantitis
summary: This exploratory study used high-resolution spatial transcriptomics on five peri-implantitis lesions and four healthy tooth-associated gingival reference tissues. Lesions showed descriptively more immune-cell presence than the reference tissue, with fibroblast-state differences near immune-rich areas and an 11-gene epithelial inflammation-associated set that needs further validation. The authors also reported suggested increased epithelial signalling involving WNT5A, MIF and ANXA1.

headline: AI system automates crown lengthening assessment and post selection from radiographs
summary: Researchers developed and validated a two-part deep learning system that uses dental radiographs to evaluate whether crown lengthening is needed and to recommend post dimensions for endodontically treated teeth. The crown pipeline combines U-Net tooth segmentation with Mask R-CNN crown measurement, while the post pipeline uses Mask R-CNN to detect and measure endodontic posts. The segmentation model reported a mean IoU of 0.52 and a Dice coefficient of 0.66, and the authors described its recommendations as closely aligned with expert decisions.
why: Such a tool could offer a more consistent, less time-consuming way to plan restorations for root-canal-treated teeth, though the excerpt describes early validation work rather than clinical deployment.

headline: AI shows promise for finish-line detection in digital crown workflows, but evidence is early
summary: A systematic review and functional meta-synthesis of 17 studies examined AI use for finish-line detection, margin extraction, and margin-related accuracy in tooth-supported fixed prosthodontic digital workflows. The authors found AI performed measurably well at margin detection and often shortened crown design time, while marginal and internal fit were generally clinically acceptable or comparable to conventional methods. However, the evidence was too heterogeneous to pool quantitatively, and the authors judged it mostly early-stage and insufficient to show consistent clinical superiority.
why: For dentists using digital crown workflows, AI margin detection looks technically feasible and may speed design, but it has not yet been shown to produce consistently better fit than conventional workflows.

headline: Indexing component improves linear accuracy of reverse scan body implant scans
summary: An in vitro study compared seven intraoral scanners using a standard reverse scan body protocol and a modified version that added an indexing component, on a maxillary edentulous model with four implants. Adding the indexing component significantly improved linear trueness and precision, while the effect on angular deviation depended on which scanner was used.
why: Dentists using digital implant impressions may get more reliable linear accuracy with an indexing component, but scanner choice and workflow may need scanner-specific adjustment before relying on the same protocol across systems.

headline: Indirect posterior restoration using universal materials in a digital workflow
summary: A Dental Tribune article describes how CAD/CAM technology combined with universal materials can make restorative procedures simpler and more predictable. It presents a clinical case restoring an endodontically treated second molar using Kuraray Noritake products, including a flow composite, a universal bond, a CAD/CAM resin block, a cleaner and a self-adhesive universal cement.

headline: Robotic guided implant surgery showed highest accuracy in healed partially edentulous sites
summary: A retrospective comparative study of 73 patients with 92 implants compared static, dynamic, and autonomous robotic computer-assisted implant surgery in healed partially edentulous sites. Using pre- and postoperative CBCT scans, the robotic approach had the smallest platform, apex, and angular deviations, and it was faster chair-side than dynamic guidance (which was timed alongside the robotic group).

headline: Non-surgical periodontal therapy lowers inflammation markers in periodontitis, with and without diabetes
summary: A study of 90 participants compared serum levels of AIM2, IFI16, and IL-18 in healthy controls and in stage III periodontitis patients with or without type 2 diabetes. Biomarker levels were highest in patients with both conditions, and they fell after six weeks of non-surgical periodontal therapy, which also improved probing depth, attachment level, and glycemic status.

headline: MCPIP-1 and MALT-1 levels differ in peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis
summary: This cross-sectional study compared peri-implant tissue levels of MCPIP-1 and MALT-1 in granulation tissue from patients with peri-implantitis (25) and peri-implant mucositis (23), with 24 control soft-tissue samples taken during second-stage implant surgery. MCPIP-1 was higher in the mucositis group than in both controls and the peri-implantitis group, while MALT-1 was lower in both disease groups than in controls. MCPIP-1 was associated with IL-6, IL-8 and IL-17A, and MALT-1 was associated with IL-1β.

headline: Food-simulating liquids alter Martens parameters of heat-cured, milled and printed denture resins
summary: An in vitro study compared heat-polymerized, subtractively manufactured (milled) and additively manufactured (printed) denture base resins after immersion in artificial saliva, citric acid or ethanol for 24 and 168 hours at 37°C. Material type, liquid type and time all significantly affected the Martens parameters measured by instrumented indentation. Milled resins showed the highest hardness and indentation modulus, printed resins had the lowest baseline hardness, and ethanol reduced hardness and modulus at 168 hours.
why: Suggests that the manufacturing method of a denture base affects how well it resists indentation and that ethanol exposure can degrade heat-cured resins over time, which may matter when choosing materials for denture fabrication.

headline: Dandy Appoints Angela Winegar as Head of Marketing
summary: Dandy, a fully digital dental lab, has named Angela Winegar its new Head of Marketing. She joins from Invisible Technologies, where she was Chief Marketing Officer, and previously led growth and fund administration marketing at Carta. Her role includes unifying growth, product marketing, and storytelling across Dandy's U.S. and international markets.

headline: Straine Acquires Indianapolis Practice, Entering Indiana as Its 18th State
summary: Dentist-owned DSO Straine has acquired Washington Street Dentistry in Indianapolis, led by Dr. Matthew Church. The deal marks Straine's entry into Indiana and brings its national network to 58 practices across 18 states. The practice offers implants, full-arch restorations, Invisalign, sedation, and general, cosmetic, pediatric, and emergency care.
why: It signals continued DSO consolidation in the Midwest, and the practice's emphasis on implants and full-arch work shows how acquired practices may be positioned within a larger network.

headline: Colgate-Palmolive Executives to Join Morgan Stanley Consumer Conference Fireside Chat
summary: Colgate-Palmolive's Chief Growth Officer John Hazlin and Investor Relations EVP Claire Ross will take part in a fireside chat at the Morgan Stanley Global Consumer & Retail Conference on December 2, 2026, at 8:00 AM ET. The session will be webcast live on Colgate's website, with a recording posted later on the Investor Center page for those who cannot attend live.

headline: Why dental vendor gifts and perks differ from company to company
summary: An article explains that what dental vendors can give practices, such as gifts, meals, and sponsorships, depends on each company's obligations under the Physician Payments Sunshine Act. It also says federal reporting rules, FDA device classifications, and corporate ownership shape what industry representatives can offer.
why: Practices evaluating vendor relationships may need to understand which reporting obligations apply to a given company before accepting gifts, meals, or sponsorships.

headline: Modified miniscrew-assisted expander with distalizer outperforms pendulum appliance in adolescents
summary: This study compared modified miniscrew-assisted rapid palatal expanders with distalizers (MMDs) against pendulum appliances (PAs) in 36 adolescents with Class II malocclusion and maxillary crowding who had nonextraction treatment. The MMD group showed greater bodily molar distalization, less molar rotation, less incisor labial tipping, and a shorter alignment time (8.6 vs 14.1 months) than the PA group, along with larger increases in intermolar and interpremolar widths.

headline: Kristi M. Soileau Installed as American Academy of Periodontology President
summary: The American Academy of Periodontology installed periodontist Dr. Kristi M. Soileau as its president for 2026-2027 at its 112th Annual Meeting in Seattle, held Oct. 29-Nov. 1. Dr. Richard Nagy was named president-elect, Dr. Brad Crump vice president, and Dr. Thomas J. Kepic secretary/treasurer. The excerpt also outlines Dr. Soileau's background, including her full-time periodontics practice in Uptown New Orleans since 1988 and her long involvement in local, state, and national dental organizations.
why: Leadership changes at the AAP can shape the academy's direction on periodontal education and policy that affects how general practices refer and manage gum disease patients.

headline: Alien Milling Launches Multi-Layer 2.0 Multi-Yttria Zirconia
summary: Alien Milling Technologies introduced Multi-Layer 2.0, an updated multi-colored zirconia that grades from 3Y zirconia at the cervical to 5Y zirconia at the incisal edge to mimic the dentin-to-enamel shade transition. The company lists a flexural strength of 1,025 MPa and translucency up to 46%, supplies it as a 98-mm disc for open milling systems, and also offers finished restorations through its milling service for practices without mills. The product was also named to Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 Technology Products.

headline: DentalEZ Star E900 Electric Handpiece System Launches with Presets and Tracking
summary: DentalEZ introduced the Star E900, an all-in-one electric handpiece platform for restorative and endodontic work, in early 2026 after FDA 510(k) clearance. The system offers tabletop or delivery-unit-integrated setups, three factory presets, a temperature sensor that stops the motor if the handpiece overheats, and RFID-based asset and usage tracking. The product was also named to Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 Technology Products list.
why: For practices, the lighter attachments, overheat shutoff, and usage tracking may ease clinician strain and help manage handpiece inventory and motor replacement timing.

headline: Cleartooth Launches Turnkey Digital Intraoral X-Ray System, Named a 2026 Top 50 Product
summary: Cleartooth Electronics has introduced a 2D intraoral imaging package that combines its own direct digital sensors, offered in large and small sizes, with radiography software that automatically orients bitewing, full-mouth, and periapical images. Each exposure is balanced for light and dark, and the system keeps data available offline while syncing among users through a private cloud on the practice's computers. The company sells directly to US dentists and handles installation, configuration, and maintenance, and the product was named one of Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 Technology Products.
why: For a practice weighing an in-office digital radiography upgrade, this offers a single-vendor option with manufacturer-managed setup and maintenance, plus software designed to make image review and comparison across visits easier.

headline: Denbright's BrightFLEX 3D flexible partial named a 2026 Readers' Choice pick
summary: Denbright Dental Labs' BrightFLEX 3D, a lab-fabricated 3D-printed flexible partial denture, was named to Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 Technology Products. The partial is designed digitally, printed from Carbon's FP3D dual-cure resin, and cured with UV light and heat, with the lab citing flexural testing, dimensional accuracy, and a delivery time of as little as five days.
why: Practices that refer removable prosthetic cases may have a digital, lab-made flexible option with faster turnaround, and digitally archived cases can simplify remakes and add-ons without a new impression or rescan.

headline: Align's iTero Lumina intraoral scanner adds wider, faster multi-angle capture
summary: Align Technology's iTero Lumina intraoral scanner replaces confocal imaging with Multi-Direct Capture, which records data from several angles at once. Align reports a capture field three times wider than the iTero Element 5D's at 12 mm, scanning twice as fast, and a wand 50% smaller and 45% lighter than its predecessor's. The Lumina Pro configuration adds near-infrared caries detection and an integrated intraoral camera, and the product was named to Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 Technology Products list.

headline: LightScalpel CO2 Laser Named to Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50
summary: LightScalpel's CO2 dental laser line was recognized as one of Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 Technology Products. The lineup includes three models (LS-1005, LS-2010, LS-4020) that deliver a 10,600 nm beam through a flexible hollow waveguide to autoclavable handpieces. Reported uses include frenectomies, gingivectomies, biopsies, and treatment of aphthous and herpetic lesions, with clinicians citing minimal bleeding and shorter procedures than diode lasers.

headline: Medit i700 intraoral scanner features compact body and full-color capture
summary: Medit has introduced the i700 intraoral scanner, which weighs 245 g and captures full-color 3D data at up to 70 frames per second. It connects through a single USB Type-C cable, has a reversible 180-degree tip, and includes a built-in UV-C LED and remote-control button. The scanner was also named to Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 Technology Products list.
why: For practices weighing a new intraoral scanner, the i700's smaller size, simpler cabling, and compatibility with both Medit Link and third-party CAD/CAM software could affect chairside workflow and choice of lab or design system.

headline: Trident X-View 3D CBCT line offers three configurations and a five-year warranty
summary: The Italian-built Trident X-View 3D CBCT, distributed in the US by Mid America Dental Sales, comes in 3D-only, 3D PAN, and 3D PAN CEPH versions. It uses an IGZO flat panel detector with eight selectable fields of view, scan times of 2.4 to 15.5 seconds, and pulsed emission that the company says can cut exposure by up to 57%. The system was also named to Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 Technology Products list.

headline: ErgoAngle prism loupes from Q-Optics named a 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 product
summary: Q-Optics' ErgoAngle loupes were named to Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 Technology Products list. The custom-built through-the-lens prism loupes use angled optics meant to keep the clinician's head and neck in a more neutral position, with magnification from 3.0x to 4.5x and a lifetime warranty.

headline: Hiossen T2 CBCT combines 3D and panoramic imaging in one unit
summary: Hiossen's T2 CBCT is a three-in-one imaging system that combines cone beam CT and panoramic imaging, with optional cephalometric imaging. It has FDA 510(k) clearance for 2D and 3D oral and maxillofacial imaging in adults and children, offers five standard fields of view plus a stitched 15 × 15 cm volume, and was named to Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 technology products.

headline: DEKA SmartXide UltraSpeed2 CO2 laser named to 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50
summary: DEKA Dental Lasers' SmartXide UltraSpeed2 CO2 laser was named one of Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 Technology Products. The single platform is marketed for soft-tissue work across general dentistry, periodontics, endodontics, implantology, and oral surgery, with optional fractional handpieces for facial aesthetic treatments and QuietNite soft-palate therapy.
why: A single laser platform covering several specialties, with optional add-ons, could let a practice widen its services without buying additional laser equipment, though the excerpt is promotional and gives no clinical outcome data.

headline: exocad DentalCAD named a 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 technology product
summary: Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice awards listed exocad DentalCAD among its Top 50 technology products. The CAD software is marketed to dental labs and in-house labs for designing crowns, bridges, veneers, implant work, dentures and other restorations, and it now includes a reworked Implant Module, a split denture workflow and AI-enabled design tools.

headline: Pac-Dent's Rodin Chroma Flash post-curing system named a 2026 Readers' Choice top product
summary: Pac-Dent's Rodin Chroma Flash was selected for Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 Technology Products list. The post-curing system uses xenon flash light across 280–950 nm with material-specific profiles for 3D-printed restorations and appliances, and it needs no external nitrogen supply for validated materials.

headline: Owandy's I-Max 3D XPRO CBCT adds AI segmentation and named a 2026 Readers' Choice pick
summary: Owandy Radiology's I-Max 3D XPRO was named to Dentistry Today's 2026 Readers' Choice Top 50 Technology Products. The compact CBCT system uses AI to automatically isolate jaws, individual teeth, the mandibular canal, roots, and fillings, and its imaging chain includes a sensor that raises MTF by 30% and deep-learning noise reduction. It offers 70-µm resolution, fields of view from 5 x 5 to 16 x 11 cm, and a footprint under 10 sq ft, and it will be shown at Booth 3614 at the Greater New York Dental Meeting.
why: Automated segmentation and a smaller footprint could speed up 3D treatment planning and case explanations for practices that are considering a CBCT upgrade, though the excerpt is promotional and no independent performance data is given.

headline: FIXED: CAD/CAM tooth-bonded device for intermaxillary fixation in clear aligner orthognathic patients
summary: Researchers describe FIXED, a CAD/CAM-designed device that is planned from intraoral scans, 3D-printed in biocompatible resin, and cemented to buccal enamel before surgery to provide anchorage for wires and elastics. The device was used in 3 patients with Class II or Class III malocclusion undergoing orthognathic surgery during clear aligner therapy, one of them with a surgery-first protocol. Intraoperative fixation was achieved as planned in all cases, with no device-related complications during the perioperative period.

headline: Intraoral photogrammetry matches conventional impressions for complete-arch implant frameworks in pilot trial
summary: A pilot randomized controlled trial compared intraoral photogrammetry (IPG) with conventional impressions for complete-arch implant-supported prostheses, enrolling 26 arches from 17 patients. IPG was non-inferior to conventional impressions for passive fit of the titanium framework, with accuracy values reported as clinically acceptable. Patients rated IPG as more comfortable, less anxiety-provoking and less nauseating, and operators reported fewer disruptions from patient reactions and greater fluency with IPG.
