why: For complete-arch implant cases, this small pilot suggests digital photogrammetry can be an alternative to conventional impressions without losing framework fit, while improving patient comfort and workflow, though the study is small and limited.

headline: Non-surgical therapy improves narrow and wide intrabony defects in short-term study
summary: A retrospective analysis looked at clinical results of non-surgical periodontal therapy in intrabony defects, grouped by narrow or wide radiographic angle. Both groups showed significant clinical improvement at 3 months, with no statistically significant difference in probing depth change or pocket closure between them. Baseline radiographic angle did not affect outcomes, though the short follow-up and lack of wide or deep defects limit generalisation.
why: It suggests non-surgical therapy can help certain intrabony defects regardless of angle, but the short follow-up and limited defect types mean surgical decisions for deeper defects should not rely on these findings alone.

headline: Polishing after speed-sintering gives smoothest zirconia; biofilm levels similar across finishes
summary: An in vitro study compared how different finishing protocols affected surface roughness and early Streptococcus mutans biofilm formation on enamel and dentin layers of two multilayer speed-sintered zirconia materials intended for in-office use. Polishing after sintering produced the smoothest surfaces, while glazing increased roughness. Biofilm accumulation was minimal across all groups, with no significant differences by material, layer, or finishing method.
why: For in-office milled zirconia restorations, polishing after speed-sintering appears to give the smoothest surface, but the tested finishes did not change early bacterial adhesion, so finishing choice may rest on other factors.

headline: Keyless guided implant system showed smaller linear deviations than drill-key system in vitro
summary: An in vitro study compared keyless and drill-key static computer-assisted implant systems using Straumann tissue-level implants of two macro-designs in healed ridges and simulated molar extraction sites. The keyless system produced smaller crestal and vertical deviations and higher precision, while both systems showed comparable trueness. Insertion torque was higher with the drill-key system, and healed ridges gave better accuracy and primary stability than extraction sites.
why: In this bench model, keyless guidance placed implants closer to the planned position, but accuracy fell in extraction sites, and the stability values should not be assumed to apply clinically.

source: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol
headline: Upward-facing interproximal wedge reduces overlap in bitewing radiographs
summary: A clinical study of 100 patients compared two commercial image receptor-holding devices with two modified versions whose interproximal wedge faced either upward or downward. Two oral radiologists judged proximal surface overlap on digital images, and questionnaires captured operator perception and patient comfort. The modified device with the upward-facing wedge showed significantly less overlap than the other devices across regions and arches, and the modified devices scored higher for comfort.
why: For clinicians taking bitewings, wedge orientation on a receptor-holding device may reduce overlapping proximal surfaces and improve patient comfort, though this is a single study and its findings should be confirmed before changing routine technique.

headline: Low-level laser may shorten numbness in children after dental anaesthesia
summary: Researchers in India ran a randomised split-mouth clinical trial testing low-level laser therapy on how quickly older children recover from oral numbness after local anaesthesia. The findings add to earlier work in younger children, suggesting photo-biomodulation can shorten the period when children are at risk of accidental soft-tissue injury such as lip or cheek biting.

headline: Narrative review of rotational path removable partial denture design concepts
summary: This narrative review and case report covers the rotational path removable partial denture (RPRPD), described as a viable option for restoring esthetics and function in Kennedy Class III and IV partially edentulous patients. It reviews the basic concept's indications, contraindications, advantages and disadvantages, moving from analog to digital workflow. Two clinical cases are described in detail.
why: Dentists treating Kennedy Class III or IV partially edentulous patients may find this a reference for considering RPRPD as a treatment option, along with its limits and digital workflow steps.

headline: AI models tested for predicting people at high risk of untreated caries
summary: A recent study examined whether artificial intelligence models could predict untreated caries and cumulative caries experience using only socio-economic, demographic and behavioural data. The authors suggest the approach may have potential for public health screening to direct preventive dental care toward those most in need, based on established social determinants of health.

headline: OneHolo.ai Shows Tala AI Concierge at AIMed26 and Offers Event Pilots
summary: OneHolo.ai presented Tala, its multilingual AI concierge, at the AIMed26 healthcare conference in Orlando. The company, which first deployed Tala at founder Dr. Kianor Shah's Palm Desert practice, is now offering professional associations and conference organizers a pilot in which Tala guides attendees online and on compatible displays. Tala answers website visitors' routine questions about services, patient forms, and booking, while the clinical team handles individual care questions.

headline: Align Technology adds Paul Clancy and Ian Bell to its Board of Directors
summary: Align Technology, maker of the Invisalign clear aligner system, iTero intraoral scanners, and exocad software, has appointed Paul J. Clancy and Ian Bell as directors. Clancy, a former CFO of Alexion Pharmaceuticals and Biogen, joins effective immediately, while Bell, COO of Alcon, joins effective December 10, 2026.

headline: Henry Schein's video series spotlights dental hygienists, with pediatric hygienist Kimberly Kyd in Episode 2
summary: Henry Schein's "The People Behind the Prophy" series profiles dental hygienists and their personal stories. Episode 2 features pediatric dental hygienist Kimberly Kyd, RDH, who discusses patience, prevention, and a whole-patient approach to helping children build positive dental experiences.
why: The episode offers practical perspective on building trust with young patients, recognizing airway concerns early, and reducing dental fear, which may be useful for team training and pediatric patient care.

headline: Case series tests rhPDGF-BB with β-TCP and coronally advanced flap for gingival recession
summary: This case series from Rutgers University School of Dental Medicine reports four patients treated for Miller Class I and II gingival recession in the maxilla and mandible. The treatment combined rhPDGF-BB with β-tricalcium phosphate under a porous wound dressing, along with a coronally advanced flap, and outcomes were judged by root coverage, gingival thickness gain, and keratinized tissue width. In one patient, a CT scan at ten months showed hard tissue gain on the previously exposed root surface.
why: It offers a documented regenerative option for recession defects, though the evidence comes from only four patients, so it is an early signal rather than a proven standard.

headline: THRIVELIVE 2027 Opens Registration for Las Vegas Event in April-May
summary: Registration is open for THRIVELIVE 2027, co-hosted by Henry Schein and Henry Schein One, to be held at Resorts World Las Vegas from April 28 to May 1, 2027. The event offers more than 100 courses worth up to 15 CE credits, along with new partnerships with AADOM, BioHorizons, Dykema, Spear, and 3Shape. Ultra Early Bird registration runs through December 31, 2026.

headline: Aspen Dental Opens Three Independently Owned Practices in Three States
summary: Aspen Dental announced the opening of three new offices in Pueblo, Colorado; Moncks Corner, South Carolina; and Hanover, Maryland, each run by an independently owned practice led by an established owner. The offices offer a full range of services, including preventive, emergency, implant, oral surgery, and clear aligner care, with walk-in availability and upfront cost estimates. The openings are tied to Aspen Dental's Practice Ownership Program, which the company says helps associate dentists progress to ownership; the number of practice owners rose from 85 to 277 between 2014 and 2024.
why: It shows a dental support network expanding through doctor ownership pathways, which may matter to associates weighing ownership or to practices competing in these markets.

headline: Saliva diagnostics and AI may usher in precision prevention in dentistry
summary: This is the last part of a four-part series on the saliva movement and the future of precision prevention in dental care. The excerpt is brief and does not give specific findings, methods, or data. It frames saliva testing combined with AI as a developing area of preventive dentistry.
why: Dental hygienists and dentists may see saliva-based risk assessment and AI tools become part of preventive planning, but the excerpt offers no details on how these would be used in practice.

headline: New CBCT-based Sivan TMJ-OPMS classification for temporomandibular disorders validated against MRI
summary: Researchers developed a CBCT-based classification, Sivan TMJ-OPMS, that scores osseous changes, disc position, disc morphology, and joint space to standardize phenotyping and severity of temporomandibular disorders. In a retrospective study of 132 patients (264 joints), 15 blinded raters showed near-perfect agreement, and the scheme performed strongly against MRI as the reference standard (AUC 0.94). Path analysis suggested bone changes led to disc displacement, which in turn related to joint-space changes.
why: If validated further, this structured CBCT scoring system could help dentists assess TMD severity more consistently and support individualized treatment planning without relying solely on MRI.

headline: Dental implants in fibula free flaps after cancer show high survival in review
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 35 studies (979 patients, 3,472 implants) pooled data on implants placed into fibula free flap reconstructions in patients with malignant disease. The pooled implant survival estimate was 92.7% and success was 90.6%. The authors found little data on implants in the maxilla compared with the mandible, and said radiotherapy effects and implant timing need more study.
why: For dentists treating patients rebuilt with fibula flaps after oral cancer, the pooled results support implant rehabilitation as a generally successful option, though evidence for maxillary sites, irradiated patients, and placement timing remains limited.

headline: Seldinger technique shows comparable complication rates to trocar method in TMJ arthroscopy
summary: A retrospective cohort study at Massachusetts General Hospital compared Seldinger (guidewire and sequential dilation) access with the conventional trocar technique in 78 patients who had 100 level 2 TMJ arthroscopies between 2022 and 2025. Total complications were 34% of Seldinger-treated joints and 30% of trocar-treated joints, a difference that was not statistically significant. Major complications were rare, occurring in 0 Seldinger joints and 2 trocar joints, and the difference was not significant.
why: For dentists and oral surgeons considering TMJ arthroscopy, this single-center study suggests the Seldinger approach does not raise complication rates compared with the trocar method, though its retrospective design and modest sample limit how firmly this can be generalized.

headline: Free fibular flap mandibular reconstruction linked to larger upper airway volume
summary: A retrospective cohort study of 25 patients who had mandibular reconstruction with a free fibular flap between 2016 and 2024 measured upper airway changes using preoperative and postoperative imaging. Mean airway volume rose from about 21.5 cm3 to 26.5 cm3, and the relative increase in volume was about 32%, with the minimal cross-sectional airway area also rising, though that change was not statistically significant. Reconstruction stage was the only factor significantly associated with changes in postoperative airway volume.
why: Surgeons and oral and maxillofacial teams may want to know that free fibular flap reconstruction was associated with a larger upper airway, and that the staging of the reconstruction appeared to matter for airway morphology.

headline: 3D printed denture base materials compared with milled bases on strength and appearance
summary: An in vitro study compared flexural strength, impact strength, translucency, and stain resistance of ten commercial denture base materials, including two milled, six vat-polymerized, one PolyJet, and one MultiJet product. Several 3D printed materials matched milled materials in flexural strength and elastic modulus, while material-jetted products had lower impact strength. Several printed materials were more translucent and showed greater staining than milled ones, and results varied by material.
why: Some 3D printed denture base resins can perform comparably to milled bases, but properties depend on the specific material, so clinicians should check product-specific data before choosing a printed base.

headline: In vitro study compares composition and cell response of three vital pulp therapy materials
summary: Researchers characterized MTA (the commercial reference), MTAvpt and IRAP, materials used for vital pulp therapy, before and after setting using structural, morphological and particle size analyses. They then exposed L929 fibroblasts to extracts from each material to assess viability and proliferation. Extracts from MTAvpt and IRAP after setting showed no cytotoxic effect, with viability above 70% of control, and MTAvpt performed best, though the authors call for further studies.

headline: Scanning the palate improves maxillary complete-arch intraoral scan accuracy
summary: An in vitro study digitized a fully dentate maxillary typodont with a reference scanner and compared three intraoral scanners (Aoralscan Elite, TRIOS 4, Primescan) with and without palatal acquisition. Scanner choice was the main factor for trueness, and including the palate improved overall and posterior trueness, though only Aoralscan Elite showed a significant trueness gain. Palatal acquisition also reduced interscan deviation for TRIOS 4 and Primescan, and all scanners overestimated arch width, with larger errors toward the molars.
why: For long-span maxillary restorations, capturing the palate appears to be a brief, reasonable step to reduce arch-width errors, though the findings come from one typodont model and may vary by scanner.

headline: Local IL-17A blockade reduces peri-implant bone loss in diabetic rats
summary: In a rat study, thirty diabetic animals were split into control, peri-implantitis, and anti-IL-17A treatment groups. Micro-CT, TRAP, and H&E staining showed that peri-implantitis caused more bone resorption and osteoclast activity, and that local IL-17A neutralization reduced both along with inflammatory markers. The authors describe the approach as promising but note that these are preclinical results needing further validation.

headline: EFP issues first S2k-level guideline for non-dental biofilm gingival diseases and enlargement
summary: The European Federation of Periodontology has published a clinical practice guideline covering non-dental biofilm-induced gingival diseases and conditions, plus gingival enlargement, which had no prior guidance. It was built from two commissioned systematic reviews, GRADE-based evidence grading, and a structured expert consensus process. The authors state these conditions are rare and complex, with few randomised trials, so evidence is limited in many areas.
why: Dentists seeing these uncommon gingival conditions should consider referring suspected malignancies urgently and possibly referring complex cases to specialist centres, while treating biofilm-related inflammation is generally beneficial and enlargement management is usually medical first.

headline: Specialist root canal care in Germany retains teeth longer at modest extra cost
summary: A Markov cost-effectiveness model followed a tooth needing root canal treatment in a 25-year-old patient over life, comparing care by general practitioners, care by endodontic specialists, and GP treatment with specialist referral for retreatment after failure. Costs used German public and private fee schedules in 2026 euros. Specialist-only care gave the longest average tooth retention (49.5 years, 1475.89 EUR), GP-only care gave 36.8 years (1376.81 EUR), and referral gave 44.2 years at the lowest cost (1326.17 EUR).

headline: DeW Life's 10th anniversary retreat focuses on connection over job titles
summary: DeW Life, an organization for women in dentistry (short for Dental Entrepreneur Woman), marked its 10th anniversary with a three-day retreat at The Ballantyne in Charlotte, North Carolina, from November 12 to 14, 2026. The event centered on leadership, personal growth, entrepreneurship, and community, with a mix of celebration and emotional sharing. Attendees wore badges showing CliftonStrengths instead of company names or job titles, which shifted conversations toward personal goals and challenges.

headline: Septodont and Adin Implants form long-term partnership in France
summary: Septodont, a dental pharmaceuticals and solutions provider, and Adin Implants, a global dental implant company, have announced a long-term strategic partnership. The aim is to expand implant dentistry in France.

headline: Intra-oral scans may help detect secondary caries, depending on lesion severity
summary: Researchers in Brazil ran what they believe is the first clinical validation study of its kind to test whether standard intra-oral scans, taken without caries-detection features, can spot secondary caries around restorations. Lesions were grouped by severity using categories adapted from the Caries Associated with Restorations or Sealants criteria. The findings suggest the diagnostic value of these scans may depend on how severe the lesion is.

headline: A 93-year-old patient's decades-long search for a lasting smile
summary: Dr. Louis Kaufman recounts treating a 93-year-old patient who lost her front teeth as a young child and never had a prosthesis that fit well. After ten dentists declined a treatment that required extracting healthy teeth, another dentist agreed to provide it, and the patient's life changed. The dentist also paid for her to attend modeling school.
why: It is a reflective piece on balancing tooth preservation against a patient's functional and emotional goals, and on how a dentist's willingness to listen can change outcomes.

headline: MARK3 Introduces Blue Streak Diamond Burs at Lower MSRP
summary: MARK3 has launched Blue Streak Diamond Burs, which the company says offer cutting performance comparable to premium bur brands at a significantly lower manufacturer's suggested retail price. The burs are marketed for shaping, contouring, and finishing, and feature diamond exposure and high-security bonding technology. The publisher's comparison lists MARK3's 5-bur pack at as low as $21.95, versus about $43 to $75+ for other brands' 5-packs.

headline: ADA Names David Waldschmidt Senior Vice President of Testing Services
summary: The American Dental Association has promoted David Waldschmidt, Ph.D., to Senior Vice President for Testing Services and the Joint Commission on National Dental Examinations. He will provide strategic and operational leadership for the ADA's licensure and admissions examination programs, which he previously helped lead as Senior Director of Testing Services. ADA Executive Director Nader Nadershahi praised his role in expanding the association's examination offerings.
why: The promotion signals continued focus on the licensure and admissions exams that determine dental practitioner qualifications, which can matter to dentists involved in licensing or dental education.

headline: Strategies for lifelong skeletal health and what dentists can do
summary: An article from Dentistry IQ looks at how hormones, nutrition, sleep, and physical activity shape bone health across a lifetime. It covers factors affecting bone density, fracture risk, and osteoporosis prevention. It also discusses how dental professionals can link skeletal health to overall systemic health.
why: Dentists may be able to recognize bone-related health factors during patient visits and discuss how skeletal health connects to the broader health picture.

headline: Long-term bone loss around implants in periodontally healthy vs. compromised patients
summary: A retrospective radiographic case series from Naples and Piacenza, Italy, tracked marginal bone loss around 57 implants in 32 patients over a mean of 19.5 years. Mean marginal bone loss was 0.04 ± 0.69 mm in periodontally healthy patients and 1.02 ± 1.96 mm in periodontally compromised patients, a difference that was not statistically significant. The frequency of implants with bone loss of 3 mm or more did differ significantly between the groups, though the small sample limits firm conclusions.
why: For patients with a history of periodontitis, implants may keep stable bone over the long term, but the small sample and low statistical power mean clinicians should not treat this as conclusive evidence.

headline: Valian Extends Revenue Cycle Services to Orthodontic and General Dental Billing
summary: Valian, a dental and medical billing company, has expanded its revenue cycle management software to cover insurance billing for orthodontic and general dental practices, from the initial insurance check through final payment. Before visits, the service checks coverage in real time and files prior authorizations; afterward, it submits claims electronically, handles denials, and collects the patient's share. The billing service runs inside the practice's existing system, so front desk staff can track claim status and outstanding balances by carrier and age.

headline: Guided midface surgery accurate for maxilla and orbit, less so for zygoma
summary: This study compared planned and achieved positions after guided midface surgery using patient-specific implants in 12 patients with complex craniofacial anomalies, based on pre- and postoperative CBCT scans. The average 3D deviation was 2.4 ± 1.1 mm, with maxilla and orbit movements staying within the 2 mm/° threshold. The zygomatic bones showed significant posterior displacement and yaw rotation errors.
why: Virtual planning with patient-specific implants appears reliable for maxillary and orbital repositioning, but surgeons should expect zygomatic advancement to drift posteriorly and rotate inward, which may need extra attention during planning or execution.

headline: Ultrasound-guided transvelopharyngeal excision of a retropharyngeal thyroid cancer metastasis
summary: This technical note describes removing an isolated, non-iodine-avid retropharyngeal lymph node metastasis from oncocytic thyroid carcinoma in a 69-year-old woman with a previously operated and reconstructed neck. The surgeons used an endoscopic-assisted trans-velopharyngeal approach, with intraoral duplex ultrasound to locate the lesion and internal carotid artery before and during dissection. The lesion was fully excised en bloc without carotid skeletonization or neurological, swallowing, airway, or wound complications, and thyroglobulin fell from 58.6 to 1.0 ng/mL.
why: It shows that, in carefully selected patients where reopening the neck would carry high morbidity, a trans-velopharyngeal route guided by intraoral ultrasound may be a feasible alternative for deep retropharyngeal nodal disease.

headline: Life-threatening floor-of-mouth hematoma after guided implant placement in a resorbed mandible
summary: A case report describes a 59-year-old man who developed sudden bleeding and sublingual swelling after computer-guided implant placement in a severely resorbed edentulous mandible, with the swelling threatening the airway. Imaging showed lingual cortical perforation at the #31 implant site, and comparison with the original digital plan found that only that implant had shifted lingually, likely during freehand insertion after the guide was removed. Emergency intubation and conservative care led to gradual resolution of the hematoma.
why: Even with guided surgery, mucosa-supported guides without extra fixation and freehand insertion after guide removal may allow positional drift, so dentists placing implants in severely resorbed mandibles should use thorough CBCT assessment and be prepared to manage the airway.

headline: RNA-seq in rabbits compares early gene activity around turned, SLA-treated and copper titanium implants
summary: This exploratory study used a rabbit tibia model to examine early molecular responses at the bone-implant interface 10 days after placement. Turned titanium, SLA-modified titanium, and turned copper implants were compared against a drilled sham control, with bone-to-implant contact and bone area measured by histomorphometry. Both titanium groups had significantly higher bone-to-implant contact and bone area than copper, and the SLA titanium showed an immune-related gene pattern, while copper showed altered mitochondrial and oxidative stress genes; SLA and turned titanium did not differ in gene expression.
why: Copper-containing implants appeared to heal with weaker bone contact and a different early gene profile than titanium, though this small preliminary animal study does not yet support changes to clinical implant selection.

headline: Case report: migrated dental implants stable for 17 years after prosthetic rework
summary: A case report followed a 58-year-old woman who received full-mouth extractions (except teeth 34 and 43) and twelve implants, supporting fixed prostheses in both jaws. After 12 years of stable function, implants at sites 33 and 42 were found to have migrated along with the adjacent teeth and their prosthesis. Following extraction of the neighboring natural teeth, a new mandibular cross-arch prosthesis was built over the existing implants, which remained stable for a further 5 years.
why: It suggests that long-term implant migration may be managed by re-prosthetic work rather than surgical removal, though this rests on a single patient and should not be treated as a general protocol.

headline: Bite holder substitution method yields clinically acceptable implant registration in vitro
summary: An in vitro study compared a bite holder digital substitution workflow with direct scan body scanning for recording positions of four implant analogs in a mandibular model. Direct scanning was statistically more accurate, but the differences from the substitution method stayed within predefined clinical equivalence margins. The design allows implant positions and maxillomandibular relationships to be captured in a single visit, and the authors call for clinical validation.
why: For complete-arch implant cases, this approach could potentially reduce appointments by recording implant positions and jaw relationship together, though it has only been tested in the lab and still needs clinical validation.

headline: Bone and soft tissue remodeling after immediate anterior maxilla implants over one year
summary: A retrospective study of 21 patients compared two immediate implant protocols in the anterior maxilla, the Standard Healing Site and the Bone-Chamber Healing Site, tracking soft tissue and bone volume over one year. Sites in the bone-chamber group, which had more severe baseline defects, showed greater soft tissue volume loss, with most change occurring in the first 3 to 4 months and little change from 4 to 12 months. The authors describe the differences as descriptive, since group allocation followed baseline defect severity rather than treatment effects.

headline: UMAP clustering sorts immediately placed anterior maxillary implants by 5-year esthetic outcome
summary: An exploratory proof-of-concept study applied UMAP, a nonlinear dimensionality reduction method, to 103 clinical, radiographic, and patient-reported parameters from 22 patients with immediately placed and loaded anterior maxillary implants. The analysis found four clusters that differed significantly in 5-year white esthetic score and several other esthetic and tissue measures, while PCA did not produce separable groups. Clusters built from preoperative parameters alone also showed divergent 5-year outcomes, with the authors noting that favorable initial bone conditions went with better long-term esthetics and that independent validation is still needed.
why: Suggests preoperative bone and tissue characteristics may help identify which immediate implant cases are likely to achieve better esthetic results, though the small sample means this remains unvalidated and should not yet change treatment planning.

headline: IRIS-Dx model scores peri-implant bone risk using CBCT data from 52 patients
summary: A retrospective study reviewed 500 CBCT scans and analyzed 52 scans covering 125 implants from 52 patients, with a mean follow-up of about 56 months. Bone loss increased over time, narrow implants lost more buccal bone, longer implants lost more lingual bone, and socket preservation increased bone thickness. History of periodontitis and prior implant failure were the strongest predictors of peri-implantitis, and the authors built an 11-variable risk score (IRIS-Dx) with low, moderate, and high categories.
why: The model suggests that patient history of periodontitis or earlier implant failure, along with implant width, length, and socket preservation, may help clinicians identify high-risk patients and tailor implant planning, though it is a single retrospective study that still needs validation.

headline: Replacement implants at failed sites show a pooled 90.2% survival in review
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis pooled survival data for replacement dental implants placed where earlier implants had failed, covering 21 studies in total and 16 in the meta-analysis. Reported survival ranged from 73.1% to 99.0%, with a pooled estimate of 90.2% (95% CI 84.4-94.9%), though heterogeneity was very high and follow-up periods varied from 12 months to over 10 years. Smoking, poor bone quality, and previous peri-implantitis were the most often reported risk factors, while bone augmentation and advanced implant surface characteristics were linked to lower reported failure risk in observational data.
why: Clinicians considering replacing a failed implant can expect roughly 90% survival on average, but the authors caution against treating that figure as a firm long-term estimate and point to smoking, poor bone, and prior peri-implantitis as risks to assess before retreatment.

headline: Biodentine and TheraCal LC best preserve pulp cells through caries-affected dentin
summary: In an artificial pulp chamber model using caries-affected human dentin discs, researchers tested how several lining and pulp-capping materials affected odontoblast-like cells and dental pulp stem cells. Dycal markedly reduced cell viability, Ultra-Blend Plus caused a smaller reduction, while Biodentine and TheraCal LC did not differ from the water control. Biodentine and TheraCal LC also enhanced mineralized matrix formation after 14 days.
why: This lab study suggests Biodentine and TheraCal LC may be gentler on the pulp beneath caries-affected dentin than Dycal, though it is an in vitro model and does not establish clinical outcomes.

headline: Hydrogel all-in-one root filling OdneFill matches conventional obturation in ex vivo study
summary: Researchers compared a light-curable, hydrogel-based all-in-one root filling material, OdneFill, with gutta-percha and AH Plus using warm vertical compaction, and gutta-percha with iRoot SP using a sealer-based single-cone technique. Thirty extracted mandibular premolars were filled and assessed by micro-computed tomography for void volume. All three groups showed low voids with no significant differences in void volume, though the apical third had more voids than the coronal third in two groups; no material achieved a completely void-free seal.
why: OdneFill performed comparably to established filling systems in this lab setting, but the study was ex vivo with a small sample, so clinical outcomes remain unproven and apical voids persisted with every technique.

headline: Persistent residual radicular cyst case shows focal bacteria and inflammation
summary: A case report in the Journal of Endodontics describes a 55-year-old woman whose large mandibular left premolar lesion persisted after extraction while other jaw sites healed. Histopathology found bacteria confined to a small area of necrotic contents, along with neutrophil accumulation and inflammatory cell migration through the lining. The authors conclude that persistence alone does not prove a cyst was self-sustaining, since localized microbes and inflammation may keep it active and limited sampling can miss them.
why: It suggests that residual cysts left after extraction may still harbor focal infection, so clinicians should not assume a persistent lesion is a self-sustaining true cyst and should consider that limited biopsy sampling may miss bacteria.

headline: Tooth survival often reports higher than strict periapical healing after root canal treatment
summary: A systematic review and paired meta-analysis of 31 cohorts (about 7,500 teeth) found that reported tooth survival exceeded strict periapical healing in 27 of them, with a pooled gap of 8.8 percentage points. The prediction interval crossed zero and heterogeneity was very high, and the authors rated certainty as very low. They attribute the gap mainly to differences in outcome definitions, denominators and follow-up rather than a fixed biological difference.
why: Dentists reading endodontic outcome studies should not treat survival and healing rates as interchangeable when judging root canal prognosis, since the numbers often reflect how each study defined its endpoints.

headline: Delayed gap closure cuts interfacial gaps in deep bulk-fill composite restorations
summary: An in vitro study of 24 extracted human molars compared a semi-split delayed gap closure technique with conventional single-increment bulk filling for deep occlusal bulk-fill composite restorations. Using microcomputed tomography, the researchers found the delayed technique produced significantly smaller interfacial gap volumes than the conventional method (P=.041).
why: For deep, high C-factor posterior restorations, a modified placement sequence that leaves a deliberate gap for a few minutes before filling may improve tooth-restoration adaptation, though this is a single lab study and clinical outcomes are not reported.

source: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol
headline: Dental-dedicated 0.55T MRI shows promise for jaw, trauma and surgical planning
summary: This case-based report describes a 0.55T MRI system fitted with a 7-channel dental coil and dedicated sequences for teeth and jaws, as a radiation-free alternative to cone-beam CT. The authors assessed its feasibility for diagnosing jawbone cysts, dental trauma and periapical inflammation, and for planning third molar removal and implant placement. They also report that AI-based acceleration algorithms can cut scan time by more than 50%, and they state that prospective studies are needed for validation.
why: Dental-dedicated MRI could eventually offer a radiation-free option for imaging jaws and teeth, but the evidence here comes from a few clinical cases, so it remains experimental for routine practice.

source: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol
headline: Panoramic radiograph features help separate jaw plasmablastic lymphoma from myeloma
summary: A retrospective cross-sectional study compared 67 panoramic radiographs from Brazilian and South African institutions: 27 cases of plasmablastic lymphoma and 40 of multiple myeloma/plasmacytoma of the jaws. Three experts reviewed the images, and clinical data came from patient files. Plasmablastic lymphoma most often appeared radiolucent with poorly defined borders and frequently showed floating teeth, while myeloma/plasmacytoma more often appeared multilocular with a punched-out pattern and cortical thinning or loss of the mandibular canal.
why: Recognizing these radiographic patterns can help dentists think about rare jaw lesions such as plasmablastic lymphoma or myeloma when they see floating teeth, punched-out areas, or mandibular canal changes, prompting timely referral for biopsy and medical evaluation.

headline: Metabolic study links ferroptosis and lipid changes to periodontitis and peri-implantitis in type 2 diabetes
summary: This cross-sectional metabolomics study of 30 patients analyzed gingival and peri-implant crevicular fluid to compare metabolic profiles in type 2 diabetes with periodontitis versus with peri-implantitis. The authors report lipid metabolism dysregulation linked to type 2 diabetes and suggest ferroptosis, a form of cell death, as a possible common pathway in diabetes-related oral tissue destruction. The candidate metabolite findings were exploratory and did not remain statistically significant after FDR correction.
why: It is early, hypothesis-generating work with no proven clinical application, so it should not change diagnosis or treatment yet, though it adds to understanding of why diabetic patients may lose periodontal and implant support.

headline: Bibliometric study maps 25 years of headache research and its small dental interface
summary: A bibliometric analysis of PubMed records from 2000 to 2025 mapped primary and secondary headache research, including its links to dentistry. Of 50,825 records, 40,441 formed the core set, with annual output rising from 747 to 2,522 articles, led by the United States, with China growing fastest. Migraine dominated the literature, research moved from triptans toward CGRP therapies, and dental topics such as temporomandibular disorders, bruxism and orofacial pain appeared in only 1.3% of articles.
why: Dentists treating patients with temporomandibular disorders, bruxism or orofacial pain may find the study useful for locating core journals, but the authors note that few dental-focused studies address headache and dental aspects appear in the literature.

headline: Modelling study weighs fluoride drinking-water levels in China against caries and fluorosis
summary: Researchers built an illustrative decision model linking fluoride intake, skeletal fluoride accumulation, dental outcomes and costs to test drinking-water concentrations in China. At 1.0 mg/L, the modelled bone burden at age 60 was 2,432 ppm, and the model's dental optimum was 1.61 mg/L, reduced to 1.44 mg/L under a 3,500-ppm skeletal limit. The optimum shifted widely depending on assumed fluorosis harm and caries benefit, and the authors stress the results are conditional simulations with illustrative cost inputs.
why: It shows that fluoride water-level decisions depend heavily on assumptions about caries benefit versus fluorosis harm, so dentists should not treat modelled optima as clinical safety guarantees, though it may inform discussions on varnish and prevention policy.

source: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol
headline: Preliminary nomogram estimates oral candidiasis risk in type 2 diabetes patients
summary: A retrospective cross-sectional study of 314 adults with type 2 diabetes built a clinical nomogram to estimate the probability of oral candidiasis, confirmed by clinical and mycological evaluation. Of the patients, 55.4% had oral candidiasis. Denture wearing, oral hygiene status, fasting blood glucose, age and male sex were selected as predictors, and the model showed moderate discrimination (AUC 0.732) with net clinical benefit across mid-to-high threshold probabilities.
why: The tool could help dentists flag diabetic patients at higher risk of oral candidiasis, particularly those who wear dentures or have poorer oral hygiene, but the authors describe it as preliminary and in need of prospective external validation before routine use.

headline: Indigenous South Australian Adults Share Views on Improving Children's Oral Health
summary: A qualitative study interviewed 136 Indigenous South Australian adults about their childhood dental experiences and views on child oral health, using reflexive thematic analysis. Participants pointed to poor continuity of dental care, fewer supportive oral health initiatives, and negative childhood experiences as factors linked to limited dental contact. Rural and remote Indigenous children were described as especially vulnerable due to limited culturally safe support.
why: It highlights that continuity of care, school-based dental programs, culturally safe outreach in rural areas, and family-centred approaches may be needed to reduce oral disease disparities among Indigenous children.

headline: Orthodontist argues speed drives volume and profit in practice operations
summary: An opinion piece by orthodontist Roger P. Levin, DDS, argues that orthodontic practices are volume-based businesses where faster workflows boost revenue. He says practices reaching $3 million per orthodontist must get many operational areas right, from referral marketing to assistant speed. He compares orthodontic offices to manufacturing lines, where faster processes produce more output.
why: Dentists running orthodontic or multi-chair practices may find the case for workflow speed, chair alignment, and staff efficiency relevant to their own revenue and patient flow.

headline: Low-dose pregabalin linked to brain metabolic and connectivity changes in burning mouth syndrome
summary: A single-arm prospective MRI study followed 38 patients with moderate-to-severe primary burning mouth syndrome and 31 healthy controls, treating patients with a standardized 4-week low-dose pregabalin course. Patients showed higher anterior cingulate cortex metabolite ratios and altered connectivity at baseline, and after treatment their metabolic marker fell and pain scores improved, though structural gray matter deficits did not change. The authors describe the findings as exploratory.
why: It suggests low-dose pregabalin may help some patients with burning mouth syndrome, but the evidence is an exploratory, uncontrolled study with about 45% of patients reaching at least 50% pain relief, so it does not yet change standard care.

headline: Periodontal bacteria vesicles linked to disrupted pregnancy in mouse study
summary: In a murine study, pregnant mice with periodontitis received systemic outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) from Porphyromonas gingivalis or Fusobacterium nucleatum throughout gestation. P. gingivalis vesicles markedly reduced pregnancy success, while F. nucleatum vesicles worsened alveolar bone loss, affected maternal glucose tolerance, raised placental inflammatory markers, and were associated with reduced fetal weight and signs of fetal growth restriction.
why: This animal study offers a possible mechanism linking periodontal pathogens to adverse pregnancy outcomes, reinforcing the case for periodontal care in pregnant patients, though findings come from mice and do not yet establish clinical effects in people.

headline: Obesity linked to subgingival metabolome shifts in periodontally healthy adults
summary: In a study of 40 periodontally healthy adults grouped by body mass index (normal weight, overweight, obese), researchers used targeted metabolomics on gingival crevicular fluid, saliva, and gingival tissue. Metabolite profiles differed by BMI group, most notably in subgingival fluid, with changes in amino acid, fatty acid, and central carbon metabolism. Integrated analysis linked these changes to inflammatory mediators and microbial taxa, pointing to a pro-inflammatory, microbiome-associated shift in obese individuals.
why: This suggests obesity may alter the oral environment before any clinical periodontal disease is visible, which may matter when assessing periodontal risk in patients with higher BMI, though the study is small and observational.

headline: Obstructive sleep apnea may worsen periodontitis through oral microbial imbalance
summary: A preliminary study combined a human clinical comparison with a rat experiment to test whether obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) worsens periodontitis. Stage II periodontitis patients with and without OSA showed different gingival crevicular fluid microbial communities, with more Porphyromonas gingivalis and Fusobacterium in the OSA group, and 21 differing metabolites mainly linked to glycerophospholipid metabolism. In rats with ligature-induced periodontitis, intermittent low-oxygen exposure increased alveolar bone loss, inflammatory marker expression, and microbial changes.
why: Patients with periodontitis who also have sleep apnea may warrant closer periodontal monitoring, though these findings are preliminary and come from a small study.

headline: Systemic doxycycline and omega-3 add modest gains to non-surgical periodontal therapy in healthy patients
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 85 randomized trials, searched up to April 2025, assessed systemic host-modulation therapy added to non-surgical periodontal treatment. Sub-antimicrobial-dose doxycycline and omega-3 produced significant improvements in pocket depth and clinical attachment when given for at least 6 months to systemically healthy patients, but not to patients with diabetes. Omega-3 with low-dose aspirin, probiotics, bisphosphonates, and dietary interventions lacked supporting evidence.
why: For otherwise healthy periodontitis patients, adding a 6-month course of sub-antimicrobial-dose doxycycline or omega-3 may offer small extra benefit after scaling and root planing, though evidence certainty varies and diabetic patients did not show the same gains.

headline: Solid PRF vs connective tissue graft for gum recession: updated meta-analysis
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 randomized trials (11 in the quantitative analysis) compared solid platelet-rich fibrin with palatal connective tissue grafts for covering Cairo RT1 gum recessions. The graft produced statistically greater recession height reduction, keratinized tissue width gain, and gingival thickness gain, though the differences were small. The PRF group showed less postoperative pain and morbidity, and A-PRF and L-PRF did not differ significantly.
why: Palatal grafts remain the most predictable option for thickening tissue and gaining keratinized tissue, but solid PRF may be a viable alternative for patients with adequate baseline periodontal phenotype who want to avoid a second surgical site.

headline: Thicker, stiffer cortical bone raises resistance in miniscrew-assisted palatal expansion
summary: A finite element analysis modeled miniscrew-assisted rapid palatal expansion across nine craniofacial models that varied cortical bone thickness and Young's modulus. Greater cortical thickness and stiffness were associated with higher expansion resistance and peak miniscrew stress, while peak bone strain decreased. The lowest-quality group had the lowest resistance and stress and the highest bone strain.
why: Preoperative assessment of cortical bone may help clinicians anticipate how much force an expander will meet and reduce the risk of miniscrew overload or separation when planning palatal expansion.

headline: Narrative review proposes three-tier classification for prosthodontic care of Class II malocclusion
summary: This narrative review synthesized literature from 1980 to 2026 on full-mouth prosthodontic rehabilitation for Class II malocclusion, excluding orthodontic or surgical treatment. It found fixed prosthodontic rehabilitation may be an option, but the supporting evidence is limited to case reports and author opinion, with no strategies based on overjet severity data. The authors proposed a three-category system to guide restorative decisions according to horizontal overlap severity.
why: Dentists treating Class II patients with restorations may find a severity-based framework useful for deciding whether to aim for a Class I relationship or maintain the existing one, though the evidence base remains thin and largely opinion-based.

headline: Dental hygienist urges clinicians to recognize signs of human trafficking in patients
summary: In a first-person viewpoint, dental hygienist Loren King describes two patients whose experiences of sexual abuse and trafficking were not recognized by them as victims of a crime. She contrasts a survivor of childhood and adult sexual assault with a child trafficking case she was told about early in her career. King says the story changed her life's direction and led her to teach healthcare professionals to look more closely.
why: Dental teams may encounter patients who have been sexually abused or trafficked without recognizing it themselves, so being alert to warning signs matters for patient care.

headline: Low-magnitude high-frequency vibration as an adjunct in orthodontic bone remodeling
summary: This review, written by Dr. Gregori M. Kurtzman, examines whether low-magnitude high-frequency vibration (LMHFV) can improve the biological response that drives orthodontic tooth movement. It explains that tooth movement depends on bone resorption and formation around the moving tooth, and that vibration may stimulate these processes without requiring more orthodontic force. The article also notes that differing vibration frequencies, magnitudes, durations and application methods may account for conflicting results in the literature.
why: For orthodontic practice, this suggests a possible noninvasive adjunct that could support tooth movement without increasing force, though the excerpt does not establish clinical efficacy or a standard protocol.

headline: Glidewell's Guiding Leaders Program Adds Raleigh Site for 2027 Cohort
summary: Glidewell is accepting applications for the 2027 Guiding Leaders program, a six-month, in-person business and leadership course for practicing dentists. For the first time, the program will be offered in Irvine, California, and in Raleigh, North Carolina, so East Coast dentists no longer need to travel to Irvine for every session. The curriculum is refreshed yearly and covers topics such as practice management, HR strategy, financial literacy, and public speaking.
why: Dentists on the East Coast can now attend this leadership training closer to home, and the program's focus on business skills that clinical training does not cover may be useful for those planning practice growth or ownership.

headline: Public Trust in Healthcare and Dentistry Is Slipping, Opinion Piece Warns
summary: An opinion column by Dr. Alan Stern cites Gallup data showing confidence in physicians dropping from 77% in 2020 to 53% four years later, and notes a measurable decline in trust toward dentists over the past decade. It also reports a national survey finding that 30% of Americans are still looking for the right dentist, with patients prioritizing empathy and listening over technology, office appearance, or price.
why: The piece argues that empathy and patient-centered conversations build trust, and that practice priorities, not ownership structure alone, shape how patients experience care, which matters for any dentist regardless of practice model.

headline: Recent dental graduate reflects on school, TV filming, and pediatric residency
summary: Carter Bedinghaus, DMD, writes in a Shofu article program piece about finishing his final weeks at LECOM School of Dental Medicine and receiving the Dean's Award at graduation. He describes filming an episode for a television show and starting pediatric dental residency, where he has bonded with co-residents and found that pediatric care is about building trust and positive experiences with children.
why: The first-person account offers a view of the transition from dental school to pediatric residency and highlights the emphasis on building a child's positive early dental experiences.

headline: A new dentist reflects on the shift from dental student to practicing clinician
summary: Branden Franzen, writing in a sponsored Dentistry Today article program piece, describes the transition from dental school to practicing dentist. He says that despite years of study, podcasts, and continuing education, graduation brought a new sense of responsibility for deciding how to use what he had learned. He notes that he no longer needs a preceptor's approval for choices such as materials and treatment plans.
why: For practicing dentists and those mentoring new graduates, it offers a first-person view of how newly licensed dentists experience independent decision-making and the uncertainty that comes with it.

headline: Georgia School of Orthodontics Adds Retired Army Leader as Instructor
summary: The Georgia School of Orthodontics has appointed Lindsey G. Streeter Sr., a retired U.S. Army Command Sergeant Major and corporate executive, as an instructor. He will teach a leadership course to residents and faculty at the school, which the article describes as the largest orthodontic residency program in the United States. Streeter currently serves as senior vice president of global military affairs at Bank of America.
why: For dentists and specialists, this shows orthodontic residency training is expanding beyond clinical skills into leadership and team development, which matters for future practice management and staffing.

headline: Planet DDS expands into Canada via Canadian Dental Services deal
summary: Toronto-based dental support organisation Canadian Dental Services Corp. (CDS) has chosen Denticon, the practice management software from US company Planet DDS, for clinics in its general dentistry division. The agreement is Planet DDS's first move into the Canadian market and centers on its enterprise platform that links practice management and other operational data across multiple practices.
why: It signals that large dental support organisations are standardising on enterprise practice management platforms, which may influence software options and operational consolidation for dentists working with DSOs in Canada.

headline: Capline Reports 75% Faster Insurance Verification Using AI Checks
summary: Houston-based dental revenue cycle company Capline Dental Services says AI-driven checks in its verification workflow cut the time needed for dental insurance eligibility verification by 75%. The company says faster verification gives front office teams accurate coverage information sooner, with specialist review still part of the process. The article also cites American Dental Association Health Policy Institute data on dentists' staffing pressures and their growing use of AI for insurance tasks.
why: Faster, more accurate eligibility checks may reduce claim denials and billing surprises, but the 75% figure is company-reported and the article offers no independent validation.

headline: Oral-B Adds Floral-Design iO Style Electric Toothbrush, Sold Exclusively at Target
summary: Oral-B has launched the iO Style Series electric toothbrush, which pairs its iO cleaning and whitening technology with the brand's first floral-inspired handle. The toothbrush is sold exclusively at Target. Listed features include a round brush head, a gum pressure sensor that slows the brush when users press too hard, three cleaning modes, a two-minute timer, and a battery rated for up to 28 days per charge.
why: Patients who prefer a stylish brush may ask about this model, so it is useful to know its listed features, such as the pressure sensor and timer, when recommending home care tools.

headline: Osstem ramps up promotion of KS 3 implant before European launch
summary: Osstem Implant is increasing promotion of its KS 3 dental implant ahead of a planned European launch in the first quarter of next year. The implant was first presented to clinicians at the European Association for Osseointegration congress in Lisbon in September. It is designed to deliver primary stability in difficult cases, including soft bone and immediate placement.
why: Dentists who place implants may soon have another system option in Europe, and the stated focus on soft bone and immediate placement is relevant to how they plan those cases.

headline: Tooth-registered surgical guides proposed for minimally invasive Le Fort I osteotomy
summary: A technical note in the International Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery describes a CAD/CAM surgical guide system for Le Fort I osteotomy. The guides register on the maxillary incisors and canine on one side and are inserted independently on each side, which reduces guide size and the surgical exposure needed. The design combines osteotomy trajectory, fixation-hole predrilling and three-dimensional plate positioning in one device, but its reproducibility and accuracy have not yet been evaluated.
why: For dentists involved in orthognathic planning, this offers a possible route to guided maxillary surgery with less skeletal exposure, though the authors say clinical accuracy is still unproven.

headline: Rare branchial cleft cyst extending behind the sternum removed through neck incision
summary: A case report describes a 60-year-old woman with a three-month history of a painless swelling in the midline front of the neck. Imaging showed a large well-defined cyst below the hyoid bone that extended down behind the sternum, and it was completely excised through a neck approach without chest surgery. The authors note that this rare condition should be considered in the differential diagnosis of neck masses, and that early, thorough removal helps prevent recurrence.
why: Although uncommon, a midline neck swelling can be a branchial cleft cyst with deep extension, so clinicians evaluating neck masses should keep it in the differential.

headline: In vitro study compares navigation, haptic robotic, and optical robotic implant systems
summary: Researchers compared three proprietary computer-assisted implant systems: a dynamic navigation system, a haptic-feedback robotic system, and an optical guided robotic system. They placed 480 implants across 120 jaw models, covering partially and fully edentulous cases, and measured angle, platform, and apex deviations along with surgical time. Both robotic systems were significantly more accurate than the navigation system, while the haptic system was the fastest overall, and all three were judged clinically acceptable within the study's in vitro limits.
why: Robotic guidance may offer more precise implant placement than dynamic navigation, though these in vitro results apply only to the specific systems tested and do not establish clinical outcomes.

headline: Virtual occlusal records differ from clinical records for single implant crowns
summary: A clinical study compared occlusal schemes for 25 single implant-retained monolithic crowns and their adjacent teeth, using intraoral scanning-based virtual registration against conventional articulating-paper records. Implant crowns showed significantly different numbers and quality of contacts between the virtual and clinical methods, while adjacent teeth had similar contact counts with some quality differences.

headline: ADF congress 2026 set to bring together French dental community
summary: The French Dental Association has issued a welcome message for its 2026 annual congress, which it describes as the flagship event for the French dental profession. The congress draws more than 25,000 participants and around 300 exhibitors each year, including practitioners, assistants, technicians, students and industry representatives.
why: For dentists, this is a large annual gathering where clinicians, staff, students and suppliers meet, offering a venue for continuing learning and networking with industry.

headline: Case-based guide to treating deep caries while preserving tooth vitality
summary: Dr. Joseph Pelerin walks through a case of extensive deep caries on teeth Nos. 20 and 30, covering evaluation, isolation, dentin handling and the final bite. He describes using Hemaseal & Cide dentin treatment to improve bonding and reduce postoperative sensitivity, with tooth No. 30 restored first using a core and crown. The excerpt is cut off before the full procedure and outcome are described.
why: It offers a practical clinical workflow for deciding whether a deep lesion can be restored without endodontic treatment, though the excerpt provides only part of the technique.

headline: BioFlx resin crowns show higher retention failure than steel crowns in primary molars
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of nine randomized controlled trials, covering 507 treated teeth, compared BioFlx hybrid resin polymer crowns with stainless steel and zirconia crowns in primary molars. BioFlx crowns had a substantially greater risk of retention failure than stainless steel crowns at 12 months, with negligible heterogeneity between studies. Evidence versus zirconia crowns was too limited and imprecise to draw conclusions on retention.
why: For pediatric restorative care, stainless steel crowns remain the more predictable choice for retention, while BioFlx may offer a tooth-colored option with longer-term data still needed.

headline: UK study examines how the GDC views remediation for dental practitioners
summary: A mixed-methods study in the British Dental Journal looked at how the UK General Dental Council runs remediation, combining document review, interviews and a focus group with GDC staff and other stakeholders. Remediation was seen as a useful tool to apply early so practitioners can target specific shortcomings. Registrants viewed it as a route to resolution without sanctions, while patient groups favoured punitive measures; the authors call for clear, transparent guidelines and supportive regulator-led approaches, along with cultural shifts backed by legislation.
why: It signals that remediation, rather than sanctions alone, may shape how dentists under GDC scrutiny are handled, and that trust and clear processes will matter for practitioners going through it.

headline: UK survey finds wide variation in secondary care for hypodontia
summary: A national online survey of consultant-led clinicians at 101 UK hospitals, run between August 2024 and February 2025, found that 91 hospitals responded. Just over half (51 hospitals) ran dedicated hypodontia clinics, nearly all of them as multidisciplinary team clinics, with orthodontists and restorative dentists most often involved. Only 51% of MDT clinics had formal protocols and 16% used digital proformas, while workforce shortages, funding limits and long waits were common problems.
why: It suggests hypodontia care across UK hospitals is inconsistent, and the authors call for national guidance, a minimum dataset and a registry, which could shape future referral pathways and how restorative and orthodontic teams coordinate lifelong care.

headline: Patients find type 2 diabetes risk checks in UK dental practices convenient and acceptable
summary: A qualitative study interviewed 15 adults who had received a type 2 diabetes risk assessment in NHS dental practices. Participants found the single-visit process with immediate results convenient, acceptable and reassuring, and trusted familiar dental staff. They wanted a printed plain-language explanation of their HbA1c result and favoured both automatic GP notification and a patient-held copy, while some raised concerns about patient fees and protecting routine dental access.
why: It suggests patients would accept opportunistic diabetes screening in dental chairs, but that practices would need clear result explanations, strong GP referral links, and care to avoid fees or screening disrupting routine dental care.

headline: Periodontal care before mandible fracture surgery linked to fewer infections
summary: A before-after service evaluation at the Royal London Hospital Major Trauma Centre compared patients with fractured mandibles treated after a specialist periodontist and Doctorate of Clinical Dentistry students joined the outpatient trauma team (2021–2023) with a historical cohort from the same unit. Surgical site infections occurred in 12.5% of the intervention group versus 22.95% of the historical group, an association the authors reported as statistically significant. Stage III and IV periodontal disease was more common in the intervention group, yet severe periodontitis was not significantly linked to infection within that group.
why: It suggests that integrating peri-operative periodontal and oral health care into trauma pathways may help reduce surgical infections, though the non-randomised design means causation cannot be established and a controlled study is still needed.

headline: Overaugmented bone after guided bone regeneration shrinks toward the ridge over 12 months
summary: A post hoc analysis of a single-center subset of a randomized trial followed implant sites that received simultaneous guided bone regeneration with either particulate or collagenated xenografts. Using cone-beam CT, the team measured bone extending beyond the natural ridge envelope immediately after surgery and at 4 and 12 months. The extra width and volume of bone decreased over time in both groups, and at 12 months the two groups had similar overaugmented widths.
why: For clinicians, this suggests that bone built beyond the native ridge during simultaneous GBR tends to remodel toward the original contour over the first year, which is useful when planning augmentation volume and counseling patients about final bone dimensions.

headline: Singaporeans weigh cost, success and pain avoidance when choosing severe pulpitis care
summary: An online discrete choice experiment of a nationally representative sample of adult Singaporeans, with 454 usable responses, examined what drives preferences for treating severe pulpitis. Out-of-pocket cost was the most influential factor, followed by five-year success rate and post-treatment pain, and respondents were willing to pay more to avoid severe pain and to get higher success rates. Latent class analysis found two groups: a cost-sensitive group (40.5%) and an outcome-focused group (59.5%).
why: Patients may weigh price, expected treatment success and postoperative pain more heavily than clinical outcomes alone, which can shape how dentists present and plan endodontic treatment options.

headline: SEL1L knockdown impairs orthodontic tooth movement and periodontal bone remodeling in mice
summary: Researchers applied a 10 g orthodontic force to mouse maxillary first molars and used an adeno-associated virus to knock down Sel1l locally. They also subjected mouse and human periodontal ligament cells to cyclic tension, finding that tension raised SEL1L expression. Reduced SEL1L lowered osteogenic differentiation, reduced YAP nuclear localization, and markedly decreased tooth movement and bone remodeling in the mice.

headline: Clear aligner expansion linked to small root volume loss in maxillary posterior teeth
summary: A retrospective study of 30 adults with Class I malocclusion and mild crowding treated with Invisalign clear aligners examined root volume changes in maxillary canines, premolars and first molars using pre- and post-treatment cone-beam CT scans. Mild dentoalveolar expansion (transverse width changes of about 0.5 to 1.4 mm) was planned in these cases. A statistically significant reduction in root volume was found after treatment, and the authors describe the overall reduction as predominantly limited.
why: For dentists using clear aligners to expand posterior teeth in mildly crowded adult patients, this suggests root volume loss is generally modest, though the excerpt does not establish clinical consequences of that change.

headline: Bioactive Restorative Materials Aim to Preserve and Rebuild Compromised Tooth Structure
summary: Dentist Robert A. Lowe argues that restorative dentistry should prolong tooth lifespan, asking whether "smart" materials that interact with the tooth could extend restoration success. He notes that acid from bacterial metabolism drives demineralization and caries, and that the restoration margin is often the weak point limiting longevity. The excerpt cites a claim that as many as 70% of restorations are replacements for earlier failed restorations.
why: It frames bioactive materials as a way to slow caries recurrence at the restoration margin, which may influence material selection and how dentists think about conservative, long-lasting restorations.

headline: Operatory Design, Not Just Habits, Can Reduce Ergonomic Strain for Dental Teams
summary: An opinion piece by Michael C. Couch argues that good ergonomic habits such as neutral posture, adjusting seating and stretching are only part of the solution. It contends that the layout of the operatory itself can force repeated reaching, twisting and leaning, so the room should be designed to support clinicians' positioning, access and workflow.
why: Practices may get more ergonomic benefit by reviewing operatory layout, instrument placement, lighting and patient positioning than by relying on clinician behavior alone.

headline: Case review: troubleshooting a failing full-arch implant prosthesis in the digital era
summary: A case report describes a 59-year-old man with a screw-retained full-arch prosthesis that had been difficult to seat, including a fractured prosthetic screw and repeated adjustments. Cone beam imaging showed peri-implant bone loss in the anterior region and an implant placed in an unusual position for an All-on-4-type restoration. The author argues that repeated tightening should not replace a systematic check of implant positions, abutment alignment, framework fit, and occlusion.
why: It reinforces that when a full-arch prosthesis will not seat predictably, clinicians should investigate the underlying causes rather than keep adjusting, and it highlights the role of digital verification in such cases.

headline: Freehand Direct Composite Closes Central Diastema With Conservative Approach
summary: A case report describes an adult male with a prominent midline diastema between the maxillary central incisors, plus smaller spaces elsewhere in the upper anterior teeth. He had avoided broad smiles and was hesitant about porcelain veneers due to cost and the need to remove sound enamel, so he wanted the gap closed while keeping as much natural tooth structure as possible. Examination found the teeth unrestored, healthy gum tissues, and normal pulp responses in the central incisors.
why: It illustrates a direct composite option for diastema closure that avoids enamel removal, a useful alternative to veneers for cost-sensitive or conservative-minded patients.

headline: Study probes lifetime fluoride exposure and cognition in older Irish adults
summary: A new study looked at whether lifetime exposure to fluoridated drinking water is linked to cognitive performance in older adults in Ireland. It also examined whether any link differed depending on exposure during early life. Earlier research has mostly focused on early-life exposure, so the authors aimed to address the wider lifespan.
why: Community water fluoridation is widely supported for oral health, and this study adds to the public debate over its long-term cognitive safety, which patients may ask dentists about.

headline: MegaGen launches ten-part Full-Mouth Solution series on live surgery channel
summary: South Korean implant maker MegaGen is running a ten-part Full-Mouth Solution series on its YouTube channel, Dr. Park's Implant Surgery Room, hosted by CEO Dr. Kwang-bum Park. The series uses actual clinical cases to walk through treatment from planning to final restoration. It includes live surgery broadcasts and interactive Q&A sessions aimed at sharing clinical experience with dental professionals worldwide.

headline: OrthoFi and Greyfinch to Integrate Practice Management and Patient Payment Platforms
summary: OrthoFi, an orthodontic performance platform, and Greyfinch, a cloud-based all-in-one practice management system, are building a connection between their software. The integration responds to the feature OrthoFi customers asked for most and is designed to sync patient information, appointments, and financial records and show payment statuses on patient profiles. The integration has not launched yet; the announcement describes it as upcoming.
why: Orthodontic practices using either platform may eventually see less duplicate data entry and clearer visibility into overdue patient balances, though no release date is given in the announcement.

headline: Sedation need index and patient-desired awareness during dental care are related but distinct
summary: A single-center cross-sectional study of 153 Chinese adult dental patients compared Indicator of Sedation Need (IOSN) categories with the level of consciousness patients said they wanted during treatment. Using multinomial logistic regression, higher dental treatment complexity and higher dental anxiety scores were linked to uncertainty and deeper sedation preferences, while prior treatment experience was linked to lower odds of wanting to be drowsy but unaware of the process. The authors caution that the "Uncertain" group was small and its estimates imprecise.
why: The findings suggest the IOSN should not be treated as a substitute for asking patients what level of awareness they want, and it should be used alongside a formal pre-sedation safety assessment.

headline: Alien Milling Technologies launches online archive of its Alien Beanie editions
summary: Alien Milling Technologies has opened an Official Editions archive cataloging every official Alien Beanie by year, so owners can match their hat to its edition. The site also offers a designer where users can customize a beanie's crown, cuff, logo, and tag, with more than 250 yarn colors available. The beanies, first made in 2021 for dental lab technicians attending LMT Lab Day Chicago, have mostly been handed out at lab trade shows.

headline: OrthoFi and Greyfinch to Integrate Financial and Practice Management Platforms
summary: OrthoFi has announced an upcoming integration between its financial platform and Greyfinch's cloud-based practice management system. The goal is a unified digital workflow for orthodontic practices, from the initial consultation through ongoing payment management. The companies say the integration will sync patient information, appointments, and financial records automatically and show live payment statuses on patient profiles.
why: Orthodontic practices using either system could see less duplicate data entry and earlier visibility of overdue patient balances, though the excerpt does not give a release date or pricing.

headline: Periodontitis worsens diabetic kidney tubular injury in mice via parvalbumin
summary: In type 2 diabetic KK-Ay mice, ligature-induced periodontitis worsened kidney function, increased the tubular injury marker lipocalin 2, and caused more interstitial fibrosis, macrophage infiltration, and electrolyte imbalance. Gene profiling pointed to parvalbumin (PVALB), which rose in the distal convoluted tubule and in cell models triggered macrophage IL-1β release and inflammasome activation, partly through TLR2 and/or TLR4; blocking caspase-1 reduced IL-1β secretion.

headline: Review proposes a continuum model of cementum biology over fixed subtypes
summary: This J Dent Res paper argues that cementum's traditional subtype classifications, based on cellularity and collagen fiber orientation, are being challenged by new molecular, developmental, and disease data. The authors point to proteomic overlap between cementum and bone, cementoblast adaptation to mechanical loading, and animal-model evidence that infection, inflammation, and metabolic stress suppress cementogenesis. They propose a "continuum framework" in which cementum structure depends on environmental and regulatory context rather than predetermined subtypes.
why: Because cementum formation is central to periodontal regeneration, a context-dependent view of cementum could eventually shape how clinicians think about repair after periodontitis, though the paper itself is a conceptual proposal rather than a clinical finding.

headline: Dominant AMBN mutations cause thin enamel via protein misfolding and ENAM binding
summary: Researchers studied two unrelated Taiwanese families with autosomal dominant hypoplastic amelogenesis imperfecta and identified a rare heterozygous AMBN missense variant, p.Pro447Leu. Cell experiments showed this mutant and a previously reported one (p.Ala26Thr) were not secreted and were retained inside cells, triggering endoplasmic reticulum stress and apoptosis. The team also showed AMBN directly binds ENAM, and that the p.Pro447Leu mutant binds it much more weakly.
why: It suggests that some inherited enamel defects arise from faulty enamel matrix protein handling inside ameloblasts rather than from simple loss of protein, which may help explain thin enamel in affected patients, though it has no direct clinical application yet.

headline: Repeat silver diamine fluoride applications linked to fewer caries-related failures in adults
summary: A retrospective review of US Veterans Affairs dental records examined 66,199 teeth in 20,833 veterans treated with silver diamine fluoride (SDF) to arrest caries. Most teeth got one application, and about three-quarters survived with a mean follow-up of 3 years, while 7% failed by extraction or root canal and 18% by a direct or indirect restoration. Teeth receiving two or more applications had a substantially lower hazard of both failure types than teeth receiving one.
why: This suggests that repeat SDF applications may keep lesions arrested longer in adult patients, which could inform how clinicians plan caries management and follow-up, though the study is retrospective and observational.

headline: Genetic study of amelogenesis imperfecta in Sudanese families finds novel variants
summary: Researchers sequenced genes in eight Sudanese families clinically diagnosed with amelogenesis imperfecta, while considering each family's risk of dental fluorosis. They identified pathogenic or candidate variants in ENAM, LAMB3, PEX6, ITGB6, WDR72 and AMELX, several with unusual inheritance patterns or phenotypes. The authors conclude the population yielded novel AI variants and that the same genes may also influence fluorosis.
why: It shows that some enamel defects that look like fluorosis may have a genetic cause, which matters when diagnosing enamel anomalies in patients from populations with fluoride exposure.

headline: Integrated Medical-Dental Care Linked to Better Pediatric Dental Follow-Up
summary: A prospective cohort study of 1,626 patients aged 1 to 21 compared two University of Utah dental clinics, one with integrated primary medical care and one without. Over 24 months, patients at the integrated site had higher odds of returning for dental follow-up, with odds ratios ranging from 1.30 to 1.58 across three analytic methods, though the lowest estimate's confidence interval included 1.
