why: Embedding dental services within medical primary care may help pediatric patients keep up with dental visits, suggesting practices and health systems could consider collaborative models to improve access for underserved children.

headline: Color-coded distance mapping shows how jaw cysts remodel after decompression
summary: A retrospective cohort of 42 patients with jaw cysts treated by decompression compared pre-treatment and follow-up cone-beam CT scans taken at least 6 months apart. Mean lesion volume fell from 3.99 to 1.39 cm3 (a 63.05% reduction) and surface area fell from 17.74 to 10.17 cm2 (41.3%). Color-coded distance mapping showed inward surface contraction in every case and revealed spatial remodeling patterns that volume measurements alone did not capture.
why: Adding spatial surface mapping to standard volume measurements may give clinicians a more detailed radiographic picture of how a cyst is healing before definitive surgery.

headline: CT review links mandibular anatomy to unfavorable fractures in sagittal split osteotomy
summary: A scoping review of 16 studies covering 2576 patients mapped CT and cone-beam CT anatomical factors tied to unfavorable fractures during sagittal split osteotomy. Reported incidence ranged from 1.28% to 29.2% per patient. Thin ramus at the lingula level and a narrow mandibular canal-to-buccal cortex distance were most often reported as associated, while age, sex, and third molars showed inconsistent relevance.
why: Imaging the ramus and canal before sagittal split osteotomy may help flag patients at higher risk of unfavorable fractures, but the authors stress these are associations, not proven predictors, and that standardized definitions are lacking.

headline: Lateral pterygoid muscle volume shows no diagnosis-based loss before TMJ replacement
summary: A retrospective CT segmentation study of 96 patients undergoing total alloplastic TMJ replacement compared lateral pterygoid muscle volume across six diagnostic groups, including osteoarthritis, tumour, trauma, and ankylosis. Muscle volume did not differ significantly by diagnosis, while sex was the only significant independent predictor. The authors state that whether the muscle must be reattached in osteoarthritis cases still requires further investigation.
why: For surgeons and specialists planning TMJ replacement, the study suggests diagnosis alone does not predict lateral pterygoid atrophy, so reattachment decisions should not be based on osteoarthritis status alone, though the authors say no clinical recommendation can yet be made.

headline: Arthroscopic coblation and sclerotherapy tested for recurrent TMJ dislocation
summary: A technical note in the International Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery describes a minimally invasive arthroscopic technique for recurrent temporomandibular joint dislocation. The method combines coblation of inflamed synovial tissue and retrodiscal tissue and posterior capsule shrinkage with direct injection of a sclerosing agent under arthroscopic view. In four patients refractory to conservative care, there were no further dislocations over 12 months and no reported complications, though maximal mouth opening fell by about 20-22%.
why: For dentists and oral surgeons, this is an early, uncontrolled report of a possible option for selected TMJ dislocation cases without major bone abnormality, but the authors state that the evidence is too limited to support routine use.

headline: Single-cell and spatial atlas maps early human alveolar bone healing
summary: Researchers built a combined single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlas of granulation tissue from extraction sockets of healthy patients four weeks after extraction. They identified fifteen major cell populations and two fibroblast subsets, with WNT5A+ fibroblasts linked to inflammation and immune recruitment and OGN+ fibroblasts linked to matrix organisation and ossification. OGN+ fibroblasts showed extensive predicted interactions with immune and endothelial cells, including CXCL12-CXCR4 signalling, and immunofluorescence showed CXCL12-expressing fibroblasts located near CXCR4+ endothelial cells.

headline: European Endodontology Society issues position statement on endodontic tooth discolouration
summary: The European Society of Endodontology has released a consensus position statement from an expert panel on preventing and managing tooth discolouration of endodontic origin. It draws on the panel's expertise and a state-of-the-art review of the evidence. The statement covers classification and diagnosis, preventive strategies, management in root-filled, revitalized and pulp canal-obliterated teeth, bleaching agent selection and regulation, colour stability, retreatment, restorative options, and risks and complications.
why: This gives clinicians a consensus reference for diagnosing and managing discoloured root-treated teeth, including bleaching choices and restorative planning, and the panel plans to update it as new evidence emerges.

headline: Review compares continuous and sequential chelation in root canal irrigation
summary: A Journal of Endodontics review examined continuous chelation, which pairs a weak chelator with sodium hypochlorite as one irrigant, against the standard approach of applying hypochlorite and then a strong chelator in sequence. It covered two commercial continuous chelation products: one using etidronate (HEDP) dissolved in hypochlorite, and an all-in-one solution containing a chelator blend and a surfactant. The authors concluded that the HEDP formulation largely keeps hypochlorite's disinfecting and tissue-dissolving effects while reducing debris and dentinal erosion, but the two products should not be treated as interchangeable and clinical evidence on healing or tooth survival is lacking.
why: For endodontic irrigation, a fresh HEDP-hypochlorite mix may simplify protocols and reduce debris and dentin erosion, though the all-in-one product has less consistent evidence and clinical outcome data remain limited.

headline: Proanthocyanidins may reduce resin monomer leaching from dental adhesives
summary: Researchers tested whether the natural dentin biomodulator proanthocyanidins (PACs) lowers the release of residual Bis-GMA and TEGDMA from photo-cured methacrylate adhesives. Adhesives with 1 wt% A-type or B-type PAC trimers, or no PACs, were extracted with 75% ethanol and quantified using a quantitative NMR method. PACs significantly reduced extractable Bis-GMA and TEGDMA compared with control, while A-type PAC showed lower degree of conversion and elongation at break than control.
why: If confirmed, adding PACs to adhesives could reduce monomer leaching and improve adhesive stability and biocompatibility, though this is laboratory work with no clinical outcomes reported.

headline: Penicillin allergy linked to more sinus lift failures and complications
summary: A retrospective cohort study of 333 patients treated at Universitat Internacional de Catalunya between 2004 and 2022 compared lateral sinus lift procedures with delayed implant placement in patients with and without self-reported penicillin allergy. Patients with allergy had significantly higher rates of sinus lift failure (13.5% vs. 1.4%) and postoperative complications (29.7% vs. 6.1%), and all sinus lift failures occurred in patients given clindamycin. Implant failure was numerically higher in the allergy group but did not reach statistical significance.
why: Dentists treating patients who report a penicillin allergy may face higher risk of sinus graft failure and postoperative problems, though the study cannot separate the effect of the allergy from that of the substitute antibiotic, clindamycin.

source: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol
headline: PRP with local anesthetic eases traumatic trigeminal neuropathic pain in retrospective study
summary: A retrospective study evaluated platelet-rich plasma injections for patients with traumatic trigeminal nerve lesions and neuropathic pain who had few other treatment options. Thirty-seven patients received four injections two weeks apart, each preceded by local anesthetic infiltration, and their pain scores fell significantly from baseline at a three-month follow-up, though none became pain-free and no treatment-related complications occurred. The authors stress that the uncontrolled design cannot separate the effect of PRP from the lasting effect of the anesthetic, so controlled studies are needed.

headline: Practices Need Independent Cybersecurity Oversight Beyond Their IT Vendor
summary: A podcast episode from Orthodontic Products features Black Talon Security CEO Gary Salman arguing that orthodontic practices should not assume their IT provider also handles cybersecurity. He says up to 60% of firewalls his firm tested failed initial assessments, and he discusses AI-driven threats, distinguishing vendor bugs from coordinated attacks, and backup strategies such as satellite internet and disconnected physical server backups.
why: Dentists and orthodontists may be relying on IT vendors for security that requires different expertise, so reviewing firewall testing, backups, and key questions for their IT providers could protect patient data and keep the practice running.

headline: Dental instrument reliability over time is framed as a clinical concern
summary: A Dental Tribune piece argues that dental instruments must perform consistently from one day to the next, since failure during a procedure becomes a clinical issue rather than just a technical one. It says device quality should be judged by long-term reliability, not only by the best individual piece. The article presents ASA Dental, which it says has worked on this since 1961.
why: Consistent instrument performance matters for patient care, so dentists may want to weigh long-term reliability alongside single-product quality when choosing and maintaining instruments.

headline: ADF Product of the Year award recognises dental industry innovation in France
summary: The French Dental Association (ADF) uses its annual congress in Paris to showcase innovations that respond to current challenges in dentistry. Through its ADF Product of the Year award, the association honours manufacturers and suppliers whose products aim to improve clinical practice, patient safety and the patient experience.
why: The award highlights products that dentists may encounter in French practices, signalling industry offerings aimed at clinical advancement, safety and patient experience.
